note: 05 Findings/D779 Knowledge control presentation accepts schema presence.md

title: Runtime record order is deliberately mirrored by inspect handler
body: Operations reversed then capped at twelve; producer, placement, provider and startup arrays use their own ordering. Controller reconstructs the same array for index-based inspection. Active work display has no renderer-side freshness check.
note: 05 Findings/D780 Runtime record order is deliberately mirrored by inspect handler.md

title: Graph coverage is a supplied pagination statement
body: Graph draws only edges with both endpoints loaded, but selected incident inspector can request unloaded endpoints. Missing has-more flags can display complete even if totals differ; renderer does not establish full-universe completeness by count equality.
note: 05 Findings/D781 Graph coverage is a supplied pagination statement.md

title: Graph layout and viewport accounting have separate bounds
body: Scene dimensions grow with community size; dataset geometry clamps do not necessarily bound raw SVG viewBox. All loaded elements are constructed before controller viewport handling. Scene key omits query, relation, direction and revision; actual reuse consequences depend on controller.
note: 05 Findings/D782 Graph layout and viewport accounting have separate bounds.md

title: Graph connection labels may describe selected-neighbor edges
body: Per-node connection expression filters selected-node incident edges then falls back to item.degree only if result is zero. A neighbor may show its links to selected node instead of its full graph degree. Incident relations over 180 are grouped for label presentation.
note: 05 Findings/D783 Graph connection labels may describe selected-neighbor edges.md

title: Surface tests establish fixture and source contracts
body: System and scaffold tests use VM snapshots, regex assertions, fake bridge messages, CSS duplicate baselines and selected token contrasts. They do not prove real DOM layouts, click-to-native execution, current backend evidence or whole semantics of controller/editor files loaded by tests.
note: 05 Findings/D784 Surface tests establish fixture and source contracts.md

title: Wave completion percentage loses the canonical complete status
body: Raw statusGroup recognizes reconciled as complete. taskRow emits complete, then projectWaves passes that normalized status back to authoritativeProgress, where it becomes queued. A wave whose rows are all complete can therefore report complete status with zero percent.
note: 05 Findings/D785 Wave completion percentage loses the canonical complete status.md

title: Wave and plan eligible denominators diverge
body: Raw plan progress excludes explicitly approved cancelled/skipped tasks. Wave progress rebuilds rows with only status and weight, dropping disposition approval, so those tasks remain in wave denominator. Punch uses raw tasks and a separate unweighted denominator.
note: 05 Findings/D786 Wave and plan eligible denominators diverge.md

title: Bounded sidebar output does not bound source graph work
body: Dependency recursion visits every supplied task before slicing eighty tasks and twelve wave groups. Missing dependencies ignored, cycles produce fallback levels instead of invalidating graph, and duplicate task IDs collapse lookup. Deep inputs remain a stack/resource concern.
note: 05 Findings/D787 Bounded sidebar output does not bound source graph work.md

title: Wave claims and display identities have weaker selection rules
body: Wave row takes first claim with matching task ID regardless of claim status. Invalid task IDs use shared fallback and composed subtask IDs can collide or exceed final schema limit. Current canonical ownership is not independently resolved by display rows.
note: 05 Findings/D788 Wave claims and display identities have weaker selection rules.md

title: Agent liveness and attention retain bounded projection assumptions
body: Future agent heartbeat clamps to age zero. Retained stale agents expire from display after fifteen minutes, but all sessions are processed before final twelve-row slice. Twelve original attention rows can crowd out appended blocked/fallback/billing notices when final slice is applied.
note: 05 Findings/D789 Agent liveness and attention retain bounded projection assumptions.md

title: Provider telemetry presence differs from current healthy telemetry
body: Provider rows sliced before priority sort, future timestamps accepted fresh, stale rows reset activity to idle. Telemetry subsystem reports healthy whenever any providerActivity entries exist, including all-stale data. Configured count combines allowlist with only retained provider rows.
note: 05 Findings/D790 Provider telemetry presence differs from current healthy telemetry.md

title: Absent telemetry is rendered as zero billable activity
body: With configured providers but no rows, renderer displays NO BILLABLE API ACTIVITY and zero active requests. Projection itself labels configured-but-missing telemetry unavailable. Missing observation therefore produces a stronger display claim than source evidence supports.
note: 05 Findings/D791 Absent telemetry is rendered as zero billable activity.md

title: Sidebar schema checks occur after full serialization
body: 256 KiB message cap is applied after JSON.stringify allocation. Undefined serialization result reaches Buffer.byteLength outside serialization catch. Strict schema prevents unknown fields but arbitrary outbound input may contain eighty tasks per wave across twelve waves without a total-eighty refinement.
note: 05 Findings/D792 Sidebar schema checks occur after full serialization.md

title: Render acknowledgement is bound only to revision equality
body: Host accepts same-revision message and increments count without comparing expected record counts, snapshot digest/generated time, active view or prior acknowledgement. Claimed visible component count is schema-bounded rather than independently verified by host.
note: 05 Findings/D793 Render acknowledgement is bound only to revision equality.md

title: Browser ordering deliberately permits revision regression with newer clock
body: Only lower revision combined with nonnewer generated time is rejected. Lower revision/newer timestamp and same revision/older timestamp can render; latest values then replace prior ordering state. Browser test explicitly exercises first behavior.
note: 05 Findings/D794 Browser ordering deliberately permits revision regression with newer clock.md

title: Incremental component hashes omit some rendered dependencies
body: Header hash uses state/version/revision but renders label/connected too. Punch hash uses punch counts but its button also embeds execution plan ID; switching plan with equal counts can preserve old navigation target. Hash gating occurs after HTML string construction.
note: 05 Findings/D795 Incremental component hashes omit some rendered dependencies.md

title: Preference persistence is ordered but not serialized
body: Host awaits workspaceState.update before republish, while browser updates expansion locally immediately. Concurrent receives can read same old preference object and overwrite one another; host failure does not automatically roll back optimistic DOM.
note: 05 Findings/D796 Preference persistence is ordered but not serialized.md

title: Snapshot publication and delivery evidence have separate states
body: pushSnapshot stores snapshot before calculation and records lastSerialized/envelope before awaiting postMessage; false return not interpreted. GeneratedAt and projectionMs usually change, weakening deduplication. pushSnapshot posts hidden views while post(error) suppresses them.
note: 05 Findings/D797 Snapshot publication and delivery evidence have separate states.md

title: Some async sidebar callback failures bypass local diagnostic catch
body: openControlPlane/openEntity/retryConnection callbacks are returned without await inside try. Rejected callback promises can escape receive catch; event subscription invokes receive with void. Diagnostic callbacks themselves can throw.
note: 05 Findings/D798 Some async sidebar callback failures bypass local diagnostic catch.md

title: Repeated sidebar resolution needs view-specific listener custody
body: resolve stores listeners until provider dispose; an older view dispose callback sets this.view null without checking identity. Existing acknowledgement state is retained across resolution. dispose loop has no per-disposable failure isolation.
note: 05 Findings/D799 Repeated sidebar resolution needs view-specific listener custody.md

title: Browser contract and formatting trust strict host producer
body: Browser validates limited top-level shape and revision, not nested projection schema. Invalid currency string can throw Intl.NumberFormat despite host currency length bound; stale age timer only updates already-stale labels, never reclassifies live agents/providers.
note: 05 Findings/D800 Browser contract and formatting trust strict host producer.md

title: Sidebar navigation uses current bounded projection membership
body: Provider selection checks current rows, while openEntity forwards any schema-valid ID. entityRecord searches bounded projection and returns clone or null; extension opens route with this result. This is navigation, not evidence of underlying mutation authorization.
note: 05 Findings/D801 Sidebar navigation uses current bounded projection membership.md

title: Legacy tree definition is not the active sidebar
body: ControlCenterTreeProvider defines six flat items and emitter without dispose. Extension source search found only definition/export; actual controlCenter registration uses SidebarViewProvider. Avoid counting both as active presentation paths.
note: 05 Findings/D802 Legacy tree definition is not the active sidebar.md

title: Projection and protocol tests leave progress and acknowledgement gaps
body: Fixtures test raw weighted plan counts and wave IDs but not wave percent/disposition loss. Host tests accept equal revision without expected count comparison and test awaited storage in isolation. They do not establish current installed rendering evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D803 Projection and protocol tests leave progress and acknowledgement gaps.md

title: Sidebar browser test proves preview interactions when run
body: Test uses actual Chromium preview, synthetic snapshots, keyboard/layout assertions and forced-color screenshot, with browser cleanup. Manifest includes all existing PNGs rather than only current screenshot. It is not actual VS Code/native billing execution and was read, not run, in this report pass.
note: 05 Findings/D804 Sidebar browser test proves preview interactions when run.md

title: Starter setup is a concrete ten-operation execution sequence
body: Normal path issues nine approvals and ten operations, with workflow dry-run unsigned. Agent completes before workflow starts; selected test/admission/run flags required. It is operational setup, whereas draft save remains unadmitted.
note: 05 Findings/D805 Starter setup is a concrete ten-operation execution sequence.md

title: Starter ready result relies on selected fields and lacks multi-step recovery
body: Create and register-authority receipts are not exact-validated. Dry-run checks effects_executed false but not runnable true; run IDs need not be present. Earlier effects remain when a later step throws; no durable resume checkpoint or compensating rollback.
note: 05 Findings/D806 Starter ready result relies on selected fields and lacks multi-step recovery.md

title: Starter version recovery uses a different conflict boundary
body: Starter helper accepts named Error code/reason or an immutable-builder traceback suffix. It may create initial 1.0.0 then allocate; candidate allocation receives only numeric version regex check here. Strict draft path instead uses exact structured backend conflict classification supplied by extension.
note: 05 Findings/D807 Starter version recovery uses a different conflict boundary.md

title: Starter definition immutability is shallow
body: Object.freeze protects top-level exported starter objects, while nested grant/binding/node arrays and objects remain mutable. Setup clones the current exported structure each invocation. Exact approval payload clone does not restore a mutated starter baseline.
note: 05 Findings/D808 Starter definition immutability is shallow.md

title: Host trust registry binds origin request exact value and expiry
body: Source and allocation maps share total/per-origin quotas, reject duplicate same-map issuance request and permit one-use consumption. Values are canonical serialized snapshots; registry itself does not authenticate files or external actors. Wall clock supplied to expiry remains an assumption.
note: 05 Findings/D809 Host trust registry binds origin request exact value and expiry.md

title: Trust JSON rejects many non-JSON forms but is not a resource bound
body: Serializer rejects nonfinite numbers, cycles, unpaired surrogates, object accessors and nonplain objects; arrays use element access and do not apply equivalent descriptor checks. Recursive serialization has no depth/byte cap before result size checks. Sorted string keys use JavaScript ordering; cross-language parity must use matching canonical rules.
note: 05 Findings/D810 Trust JSON rejects many non-JSON forms but is not a resource bound.md

title: Allocation observation and backend publication remain separate
body: Host compares exact allocation binding except observed_utc before confirmation, consumes proof afterward, and recovers supplied-allocation publication collisions with a fresh token. Potentially long confirmation separates last allocation observation from actual create; backend owns collision/atomicity enforcement.
note: 05 Findings/D811 Allocation observation and backend publication remain separate.md

title: Initial create has two absence observations without host atomic reservation
body: Proofless create requires version 1.0.0 and exact backend absence receipt before and after confirmation. These observations do not reserve identity. If initial create collides later, this coordinator lacks supplied allocation and rethrows rather than manufacturing a recovery proof.
note: 05 Findings/D812 Initial create has two absence observations without host atomic reservation.md

title: External skill lineage is reauthenticated after confirmation
body: Selected canonical/preserved package hashes and counts are reread; source equality required before creation. Reserved preserved-original provenance supplied by caller is stripped and reconstructed from host lineage. This observes content, not a filesystem lock through commit.
note: 05 Findings/D813 External skill lineage is reauthenticated after confirmation.md

title: Standard skill domain screening is a partial semantic filter
body: capability.json must be px-standard; restricted namespace values scanned only under selected key patterns. skill.yaml uses JSON parse or regex fallback rather than a full YAML parser. This screen is not full package contract validation; native admission remains necessary.
note: 05 Findings/D814 Standard skill domain screening is a partial semantic filter.md

title: Materialization is bound to source admission before draft create
body: Host compares exact materialization fields/inventory, source directory physical equality and admitted tree/count, then strips editor_files and supplies source token. Errors before valid commit, including conflict or malformed receipt, retain materialized input rather than claiming reclaimed closure.
note: 05 Findings/D815 Materialization is bound to source admission before draft create.md

title: Create receipt classification separates shape proof from artifact proof
body: Agent/workflow receipt requires exact schema, identity/version, stopped/unadmitted state, hash shapes and path bounds; host does not reopen every referenced artifact. Skill result additionally matches source token/tree/count/files and canonical manifest digest. These strengths should not be represented as identical.
note: 05 Findings/D816 Create receipt classification separates shape proof from artifact proof.md

title: Malformed result is an unverified outcome rather than failed create
body: Host emits studioDraftOutcomeUnverified, attempts catalog refresh and returns no trusted result. A valid commit with notification/refresh failure retains created/recovered status plus warnings. Neither branch automatically retries create or rolls back persistent effects.
note: 05 Findings/D817 Malformed result is an unverified outcome rather than failed create.md

title: Production warning text overstates the unverified branch
body: The same reportPostCommitWarning callback is invoked for invalid commit receipt. Extension callback logs and warns that the immutable revision committed, even though host coordinator classified outcome unverified. Catalog recovery is needed to resolve that uncertainty.
note: 05 Findings/D818 Production warning text overstates the unverified branch.md

title: Package normalization is topology and byte exact
body: 128-file, 512 KiB-file, 2 MiB-total, directory/depth/path bounds apply. Case aliases, file/directory collisions, Windows device/stream names, non-NFC segments, unpaired surrogates and NUL are rejected. Tree digest length-frames exact UTF-8 bytes and retains BOM on read.
note: 05 Findings/D819 Package normalization is topology and byte exact.md

title: Materialized input publication is direct final-directory construction
body: Target combines sanitized identity/version plus hash suffixes. Existing trees require exact content and topology; new trees written directly with exclusive files and verified afterward. Concurrent writer can encounter incomplete target and fail rather than wait; failure retains partial tree.
note: 05 Findings/D820 Materialized input publication is direct final-directory construction.md

title: Lifecycle records do not provide crash-atomic publication
body: Parent/staging/lifecycle directories can be created before registered receipt. Receipt writes are exclusive but not fsynced; content publication and closed receipt are separate. A published tree can remain after closure-write failure and require later recovery.
note: 05 Findings/D821 Lifecycle records do not provide crash-atomic publication.md

title: Package read bounds do not create a coherent filesystem snapshot
body: Traversal checks links and opens bounded regular files using O_NOFOLLOW where available. It compares bytes read with opened size, but no lock binds entire traversal or detects every same-size mutation/ancestor replacement. Root inputs resolved to physical paths before checks; root authority comes from caller.
note: 05 Findings/D822 Package read bounds do not create a coherent filesystem snapshot.md

title: Reused materialized input has no shared-consumer lease
body: Deterministic target may be reused by independent operations, each with its own lifecycle receipt. Successful create can reclaim that shared path without a refcount/lease check for other consumers. Reattestation checks content, not concurrent usage.
note: 05 Findings/D823 Reused materialized input has no shared-consumer lease.md

title: Reclamation has explicit evidence boundaries and a post-delete receipt gap
body: Success path checks materialization/create/lifecycle identity, attests tree, moves to unique containment, reattests, deletes and then publishes reclaimed receipt. Failure after deletion but before durable receipt can leave removed input without verified completion receipt. Audit only maps this effect and does not execute it.
note: 05 Findings/D824 Reclamation has explicit evidence boundaries and a post-delete receipt gap.md

title: Preserved package read completeness differs from native input completeness
body: Reader confines engine/project paths and rejects extra empty topology, binary/special/link content. Preserved-original reads may omit native core files and report missingRequiredFiles; ordinary materialization still requires SKILL.md, capability.json and skill.yaml.
note: 05 Findings/D825 Preserved package read completeness differs from native input completeness.md

title: Studio tests span source checks mocks and real defined integration
body: Wiring tests inspect regexes; host coordinator tests mostly supply receipts; package tests exercise local files and optional links; bootstrap includes actual host-to-Python runs with disposable roots if executed. None was run as part of this report, and their existence is not a current installed-system pass.
note: 05 Findings/D826 Studio tests span source checks mocks and real defined integration.md

title: Workflow normalization can remove problems before validation
body: Unknown kind becomes task, nonvalidation config cleared, dangling edges filtered out, and missing nodes/default ports synthesized. The validator then sees repaired state rather than the original imported definition. Contract derivation identifies undriven node inputs.
note: 05 Findings/D827 Workflow normalization can remove problems before validation.md

title: Workflow and agent default authority labels differ
body: Workflow grants/bindings default to admitted and human-approval receipt strings; agent declarations default candidate. Persisted authority-unavailable marker prevents synthesizing missing definitions. These are editor values, not authenticated work authority.
note: 05 Findings/D828 Workflow and agent default authority labels differ.md

title: Workflow input requiredness can be relaxed by supplied contract
body: Derived contract takes port type and undriven key, but a supplied matching contract row can set required false even for required port. Normalization retains supplied run_inputs; runtime input values remain separately supplied and not persisted by canonical authority fixture.
note: 05 Findings/D829 Workflow input requiredness can be relaxed by supplied contract.md

title: Workflow editor validator is a partial structural boundary
body: Checks acyclicity, ports/types, duplicate drivers, branch boolean alternatives, join incoming count and declared grant/binding references. It does not enforce integer retry/timeout, full binding identity/version validity or authenticated approvers; empty graph is not independently rejected if called without normalization.
note: 05 Findings/D830 Workflow editor validator is a partial structural boundary.md

title: Editor configuration byte wording uses string length
body: Workflow config limit compares JSON.stringify(...).length with 16384, which counts UTF-16 code units rather than UTF-8 bytes. Fuzzy ranking traverses all supplied records/tokens before limiting twenty results; output limits do not bound computation.
note: 05 Findings/D831 Editor configuration byte wording uses string length.md

title: Agent graph validator checks closed topology rather than full config semantics
body: Canonical node identities/order, exact port arrays, config key sets, edge serialization and graph identity checked. Config values are not all type/meaning checked here, and JSON property ordering participates in exact ports/edge comparison. Separate spec and backend validation remain needed.
note: 05 Findings/D832 Agent graph validator checks closed topology rather than full config semantics.md

title: Agent synchronization and node editing have different omission behavior
body: Working synchronization preserves existing edge omissions and only adds edges for newly declared optional nodes. Explicit add/remove/retype node path instead calls projectAgentBuilderGraph and reconstructs all canonical edges, so an unrelated prior missing edge can reappear.
note: 05 Findings/D833 Agent synchronization and node editing have different omission behavior.md

title: Optional Agent nodes carry declaration changes as well as geometry
body: Removing/retyping tools, handoffs or memory clears source declaration array; retype moves saved coordinates. New node layout searches free default positions. Candidate payload includes graph/layout/grants/bindings, while backend still owns actual authority.
note: 05 Findings/D834 Optional Agent nodes carry declaration changes as well as geometry.md

title: Custom editor instruction hashing has its own Unicode boundary
body: Synchronous SHA-256 encoder expands code points manually but does not reject unpaired surrogate code units. Those encode differently from standard replacement-character UTF-8 behavior. Host exact trust serializer rejects unpaired surrogates; browser graph hash alone is not cross-runtime identity assurance.
note: 05 Findings/D835 Custom editor instruction hashing has its own Unicode boundary.md

title: Agent model normalization and structural validity do not prove a live route
body: Unknown provider defaults deterministic unless host harness implies vscode-lm. Host route requires exact model strings but editor does not query provider availability. Token bounds allow fractional values. Memory/handoff references yield warnings while structural valid can remain true; self-handoff alone is rejected locally.
note: 05 Findings/D836 Agent model normalization and structural validity do not prove a live route.md

title: Agent declarations need stronger runtime resolution
body: Effect/scope/evidence strings checked for presence, grant expiry only parses as a date, and root schemas only require type object. Closed test IDs do not require all checks or unique checks. Runtime owner must authenticate and resolve declarations before execution.
note: 05 Findings/D837 Agent declarations need stronger runtime resolution.md

title: Skill identity synchronization can overwrite manifest-specific data
body: Synchronization merges missing defaults, updates capability identity/domain/schema and writes its full JSON to both capability.json and skill.yaml. Distinct YAML-only fields disappear. SKILL.md name update only handles LF opening frontmatter, while preparation catches errors and returns prior normalized draft.
note: 05 Findings/D838 Skill identity synchronization can overwrite manifest-specific data.md

title: Skill editor validation is weaker than native package validation
body: Browser path checks cover basic absolute/traversal cases but not host byte/file/topology/case/device-name bounds. Contract links need an array without requiring each target exists; resource index checks listed files but not completeness. YAML fallback regex is not a full parser. Host materializer and admission must enforce their own contracts.
note: 05 Findings/D839 Skill editor validation is weaker than native package validation.md

title: Local history recorded is not a successful run classification
body: historyEntry reads status/state or valid false, but not run_state/run_outcome. A run-specific result may therefore be summarized as recorded. Selected revision/hash fallbacks likewise omit some operation-specific fields.
note: 05 Findings/D840 Local history recorded is not a successful run classification.md

title: Catalog round-trip fixtures prove selected artifact relationships
body: Agent fixtures bind graph/layout/spec/compiler hashes and reject selected rehashed semantic substitution; workflow fixtures bind layout/revision/authority and omit runtime input values. Missing modern artifacts fail, legacy unavailable state remains read-only. Fixtures manufacture receipts instead of invoking Python compiler/publication.
note: 05 Findings/D841 Catalog round-trip fixtures prove selected artifact relationships.md

title: Agent graph source test is only a wiring assertion
body: Small test checks current upgrade and select-node source strings and excludes obsolete select-section strings. It exercises no DOM or graph transformation. Neither it nor catalog fixtures establishes whole controller review or current installed execution.
note: 05 Findings/D842 Agent graph source test is only a wiring assertion.md

title: Physical catalog scans on access
body: Both all and getExtension rescan disk. Some consumers access all twice. Directory enumeration and full manifest reads precede parts of the cap enforcement; caller-supplied limits have no fixed upper ceiling.
note: 05 Findings/D843 Physical catalog scans on access.md

title: Obsolete marker retry blocks the extension host
body: Invalid JSON is retried up to eight reads with synchronous Atomics.wait intervals. Read failures caught as invalid JSON can also retry. This is bounded retry, not asynchronous host work.
note: 05 Findings/D844 Obsolete marker retry blocks the extension host.md

title: Loaded activation is matched by version rather than physical identity
body: Physical records become active from loaded version equality and isActive; path/content identity is not compared. External loaded records can contain duplicates. Realpath establishes the scan root but does not prove original supplied alias identity.
note: 05 Findings/D845 Loaded activation is matched by version rather than physical identity.md

title: Conflict signals are declaration overlaps
body: Contributions can collide even within one extension. Keybinding keys from all platforms are sorted together and when expressions compared as text, permitting false positives and missed effective-platform overlaps. Signals do not prove runtime conflict.
note: 05 Findings/D846 Conflict signals are declaration overlaps.md

title: Conflict ordering and identity have limited semantics
body: Severity sorting is lexical. Signal IDs generally omit package version; duplicate dependencies/signals can remain. Result limits apply after signal construction, so output bounds do not bound computation.
note: 05 Findings/D847 Conflict ordering and identity have limited semantics.md

title: Preview consumption and capacity affect retries
body: Execute prunes while map size is at least 64 and consumes token before approval/exact-target validation. At capacity the oldest live preview can be evicted during execution. No operation mutex or owner binding closes concurrent target changes.
note: 05 Findings/D848 Preview consumption and capacity affect retries.md

title: Local package hash does not authenticate requested extension identity
body: Source realpath, nonempty regular file and SHA-256 are checked, but VSIX package metadata is not read to bind requested extension ID/version. Whole file read has no size ceiling and native host opens path later. Native host owns its own package trust checks.
note: 05 Findings/D849 Local package hash does not authenticate requested extension identity.md

title: Immediate reconciliation has operation-specific meaning
body: Install/update checks immediate observed target/version. Unversioned update with unchanged version can be reconciled as no-version-change; this is not an independent marketplace-latest check. Enablement only opens native manager and explicitly remains unreconciled.
note: 05 Findings/D850 Immediate reconciliation has operation-specific meaning.md

title: Uninstall consumer state is frozen at preview
body: Target version is rechecked at execute, but reverse dependencies and extensionPack consumers are not recalculated. A consumer added after preview is outside the acknowledgment shown to user.
note: 05 Findings/D851 Uninstall consumer state is frozen at preview.md

title: Uninstall history and native mutation are separate commits
body: Retained history is written/read back before uninstall command, but storage updates lack concurrency transaction. Install/update local source retention can fail after native command. Thus a thrown operation can follow a native effect and a retained record can exist without completed uninstall.
note: 05 Findings/D852 Uninstall history and native mutation are separate commits.md

title: Rollback history does not mean bytes are retained
body: Update rollback target is a result field rather than durable version history. Local source map retains latest path/hash; an empty requested version may not match observed version later. Rollback without local bytes delegates exact version retrieval to native host.
note: 05 Findings/D853 Rollback history does not mean bytes are retained.md

title: Rollback record validation and consumption have gaps
body: Execute rechecks selected record identity/state but not full version/source equality. Local source is rehashed. Successful observed restore precedes consumed-history write, which can fail after installation; wrong/pending observed version leaves retained record while occupied target blocks another rollback.
note: 05 Findings/D854 Rollback record validation and consumption have gaps.md

title: Conflict route continues through a fresh preview
body: Host resolution returns lifecycle_route, and controller correlates request then requests install, uninstall or disable preview. This is real integration, but routing alone performs no native mutation. Inspect route opens native search.
note: 05 Findings/D855 Conflict route continues through a fresh preview.md

title: Existing environment snapshot is metadata evidence
body: Manager snapshots names, sizes, truncated mtime and file identity rather than file contents. Same-size content edits with restored metadata can escape comparison. Caller flags and containment do not independently establish ownership or current consumer state. Cleanup remains skipped.
note: 05 Findings/D856 Existing environment snapshot is metadata evidence.md

title: Existing environment receipt follows the move
body: Preview storage has no TTL/cap and returns shared object. Rename precedes durable receipt write with no compensating rollback. Restore trusts partly validated receipt fields and does not establish original parent identity. These branches were inspected only.
note: 05 Findings/D857 Existing environment receipt follows the move.md

title: Lifecycle fixtures are not installed-system evidence
body: Tests simulate native commands/storage and use synthetic package bytes. They cover selected exact target, source change, expiry, custody and conflict branches, but not native package identity, concurrency, full-capacity eviction or post-effect storage failure.
note: 05 Findings/D858 Lifecycle fixtures are not installed-system evidence.md

title: Activity append admits parseability rather than prior hash integrity
body: recordActivity refuses malformed JSONL but does not call eventIntegrity before append. A parsed tampered or state-divergent log can receive a new event linked to state.last_event_sha256. Appending event and replacing state are distinct commits.
note: 05 Findings/D859 Activity append admits parseability rather than prior hash integrity.md

title: Activity tail limits do not bound file reading or parsing
body: Entire JSONL is read and split, every valid line parsed until syntax failure, and only then sliced to tail. JSON shape/schema is not validated before integrity/filters; valid JSON such as null can make read paths throw.
note: 05 Findings/D860 Activity tail limits do not bound file reading or parsing.md

title: Local chain consistency has partial counter semantics
body: Tail hashes and internal links checked; first tail predecessor is not anchored. State counter greater than retained tail is considered truncation, not necessarily corruption. Missing empty log with nonzero count can avoid counterDrift because no final event exists.
note: 05 Findings/D861 Local chain consistency has partial counter semantics.md

title: Local state reads can retain evidence while failing
body: readState preserves corrupt bytes and receipt before throwing, so the read path can write local evidence. Semantic checks on parsed state are incomplete; unlocked readers can observe log/state between separate publications.
note: 05 Findings/D862 Local state reads can retain evidence while failing.md

title: Activity lock serializes cooperative writers with race limits
body: Lock uses PID/host/token and busy retry, protects live same-host PID and checks token on release. No process-start identity binds PID reuse; compare-to-rename/unlink gaps remain. Temp replacements have no fsync or failure cleanup.
note: 05 Findings/D863 Activity lock serializes cooperative writers with race limits.md

title: Activity redaction depends on field names
body: Secret/content-like keys are redacted with depth/array/key caps; arbitrary sensitive text under an innocuous key is not detected. Relative scopes are lexical rather than realpath identities. Captured-content false is a schema declaration, not arbitrary-secret proof.
note: 05 Findings/D864 Activity redaction depends on field names.md

title: Stale activity is an observation not process cancellation
body: Stale reconciliation emits cancelled observation and removes operation state without stopping a process. It checks a fresh state before calling separately locked recordActivity, leaving a renewal race. Invalid/future heartbeat values can stay outside expected stale classification.
note: 05 Findings/D865 Stale activity is an observation not process cancellation.md

title: Activity repair reseals supplied event contents
body: Repair backups retain exact old files then rewrites predecessor hashes for parsed contents and appends recovery event. This restores internal consistency, not original truth. Active operations and agents are retained from prior state rather than rebuilt from events.
note: 05 Findings/D866 Activity repair reseals supplied event contents.md

title: Repair completeness depends on an untrusted counter
body: Repair refuses a capped tail only when state.event_count exceeds tail length. If a longer actual log has an underreported count and integrity fails, the retained tail can be rewritten as the new whole log, with originals in backup. No repair was invoked.
note: 05 Findings/D867 Repair completeness depends on an untrusted counter.md

title: Repair publications and hash descriptions need separate interpretation
body: Log replacement, state replacement and receipt are separate writes. Postcondition checks memory rather than rereading disk. Recovery.output_sha256 hashes an intermediate serialization before final output/hash fields are changed; receipt.repaired_events_sha256 binds final text.
note: 05 Findings/D868 Repair publications and hash descriptions need separate interpretation.md

title: Listener coverage complete means available registration coverage
body: markRegistered marks available enabled listeners healthy even with zero events. Unsupported required APIs are reported as limitations but omitted from incomplete denominator. Drops remain sticky; bus status is a separate last-result projection.
note: 05 Findings/D869 Listener coverage complete means available registration coverage.md

title: Listener API inventory is coarser than individual callbacks
body: Editor availability checks change API but not open/save/close; task checks start/end but not process result. SCM attaches only to already-active Git at registration. Nested SCM registration errors are logged rather than failing whole registration.
note: 05 Findings/D870 Listener API inventory is coarser than individual callbacks.md

title: File capture toggle is not checked by every filesystem callback
body: Editor and watcher callbacks check captureFileEvents, but onDidCreateFiles/delete/rename callbacks only check excluded paths. recordActivity checks global enabled/paused, not category capture toggles, so direct workspace file events can still record when that category toggle is false.
note: 05 Findings/D871 File capture toggle is not checked by every filesystem callback.md

title: Watcher aggregation counts unique keys and repeats overflow per group
body: 256 operation/scope entries coalesce repeats and 64 scopes per group are retained, then local ledger further caps scopes at 50. A single overflow count is placed in every emitted operation group. Continuous editor/SCM events use trailing debounce; their maps have no equivalent fixed cap.
note: 05 Findings/D872 Watcher aggregation counts unique keys and repeats overflow per group.md

title: Host lifecycle results have differing certainty
body: Terminal session never means executable work. Task-end and debug termination are idle/unknown, while task-process uses exitCode truthiness and absent exitCode becomes succeeded. Shell absent exitCode correctly maps idle. Test callback reports newest result count, not pass/fail proof.
note: 05 Findings/D873 Host lifecycle results have differing certainty.md

title: Canonical activity loses local metadata distinctions
body: Effect converter maps observe/network-like unknown values to read and ignores metadata.observed_effect. Canonical scopes retain project and count, not paths. Extension builds canonical event before local claim/task enrichment, so local and canonical work identity can differ.
note: 05 Findings/D874 Canonical activity loses local metadata distinctions.md

title: Local activity success does not establish canonical publication
body: Extension records locally, then queues canonical publisher. A synchronous error after local record returns recorded false via catch, despite local effect. Delayed publishActivitySoon callback reads current workspace without its own try/catch and coalesces updates by resetting timer.
note: 05 Findings/D875 Local activity success does not establish canonical publication.md

title: Activity tests establish fixture behavior rather than current host proof
body: Local tests mutate tiny logs/state and check selected refusal/repair flags; listener tests fire mock emitters and manual timers. The matrix proves fixture route delivery, not real VS Code APIs or canonical publication. No fresh product tests run in this audit.
note: 05 Findings/D876 Activity tests establish fixture behavior rather than current host proof.md

title: Workflow helper tests and browser implementation are distinct
body: Repository callers import workflowTraceProjection only from its test; controller implements separate trace functions. Source regex assertions verify selected spelling and fields rather than executing browser parity.
note: 05 Findings/D877 Workflow helper tests and browser implementation are distinct.md

title: Workflow trace hash is optional and identity can be inherited
body: Complete identity requires workflow ID/version/run, not revision hash. Conflict checks compare only fields present on both sides. Missing result fields can be inherited from expected identity; no hash syntax, signature or receipt authentication occurs here.
note: 05 Findings/D878 Workflow trace hash is optional and identity can be inherited.md

title: Run list miss preserves current trace without freshness proof
body: List selects first matching current run and returns unchanged on no match. Direct results have no revision/event-time ordering guard. Browser permits new run only for start/run, while resume is processed without that allowance.
note: 05 Findings/D879 Run list miss preserves current trace without freshness proof.md

title: Trace node map has duplicate and special-key semantics
body: Projected node IDs are arbitrary nonempty strings written to a normal object. Duplicate IDs overwrite earlier rows; __proto__ assignment is not treated as an ordinary own node entry. Array/string data is unbounded at this helper layer.
note: 05 Findings/D880 Trace node map has duplicate and special-key semantics.md

title: Failure projection may use generic receipt fields
body: Explicit failure object is preferred, otherwise a failed-state last attempt, otherwise receipt itself. A generic code/message/correlation on receipt can therefore appear under failure even without failed state. Approval/recovery maps are shallow copies, not authority checks.
note: 05 Findings/D881 Failure projection may use generic receipt fields.md

title: Trace fixture authentication is an upstream assumption
body: Test named authenticated durable checkpoint supplies a plain object. It proves chosen fields project, not that runtime authenticated them. Browser rendering checks are source assertions on textContent/title/ARIA, not DOM execution.
note: 05 Findings/D882 Trace fixture authentication is an upstream assumption.md

title: Ollama admission checks only initial HTTP loopback hostname
body: URL accepts loopback HTTP host but does not reject credentials/path/query/fragment or revalidate final response URL. Fetch calls do not supply explicit redirect refusal. No external network behavior was exercised in this audit.
note: 05 Findings/D883 Ollama admission checks only initial HTTP loopback hostname.md

title: Ollama catalog capacities are fixed declarations
body: Catalog maps all returned models and reports 32768 input and 8192 output tokens for each. Body/model count and model field schemas lack bounds; malformed response returns empty list. Token cancellation is checked initially but not subscribed for catalogue request.
note: 05 Findings/D884 Ollama catalog capacities are fixed declarations.md

title: Local provider conversion discards role and content distinctions
body: All non-assistant messages become user and only string part.value content retained. Token estimate is ceil UTF-16 string length divided by four with minimum one. Output-token clamp lacks positive/integer/finite checks and temperature can become nonfinite before JSON conversion.
note: 05 Findings/D885 Local provider conversion discards role and content distinctions.md

title: Stream deadlines cover different intervals
body: Total deadline starts before fetch; idle timeout only races body reads after headers. Progress callbacks may emit partial text before terminal failure. Limit overrides are shallow merged without validating types/ranges.
note: 05 Findings/D886 Stream deadlines cover different intervals.md

title: Streaming line cap also applies to combined chunk buffer
body: After decoding, the entire buffered chunk is byte-counted before splitting lines. A chunk containing many individually small valid lines can exceed line limit and fail, even below total stream limit. Decoder replacement behavior is not configured fatal.
note: 05 Findings/D887 Streaming line cap also applies to combined chunk buffer.md

title: Done event does not stop processing remaining buffered events immediately
body: Every complete line in the current chunk is consumed before completed triggers reader.cancel; trailing buffer is consumed afterward. Thus later text or error in same chunk can follow done. Content field truthiness is checked without string/schema validation.
note: 05 Findings/D888 Done event does not stop processing remaining buffered events immediately.md

title: Provider cleanup is not complete stream ownership closure
body: Finally clears timer and cancellation subscription only. Parser/progress errors do not always cancel reader or abort fetch; successful done attempts cancel. Provider dispose only disposes emitter and does not track or cancel in-flight requests.
note: 05 Findings/D889 Provider cleanup is not complete stream ownership closure.md

title: Ollama tests prove selected synthetic transport branches
body: Fixtures run loopback HTTP responses with no real model and fake VS Code objects. They assert stable faults and explicit done, but not real model capacity, redirects, catalogue, line-boundary chunking or all resource closure paths. Audit reads tests without running them.
note: 05 Findings/D890 Ollama tests prove selected synthetic transport branches.md

title: Message field lists are not complete required-field schemas
body: Generic CONTRACTS rejects unknown top-level keys but many listed fields are optional or lack detailed validation. Graph and selected Studio/lifecycle operations receive stronger checks; ordinary catalogue/environment/coordination payloads rely on downstream owners.
note: 05 Findings/D891 Message field lists are not complete required-field schemas.md

title: Aggregate webview byte bound follows traversal and serialization
body: Depth ten, ten-thousand nodes, one-MiB string length and two-thousand array caps are checked first. Four-MiB total is enforced after JSON.stringify allocates serialized text; many large permitted strings can allocate far more before rejection.
note: 05 Findings/D892 Aggregate webview byte bound follows traversal and serialization.md

title: Object and array descriptor checks are asymmetric
body: Plain object properties require enumerable data descriptors and reject dangerous keys. Array density/key count/symbol checks do not inspect element descriptors before every/iteration accesses them. Real webview structured transport limits expressible values; this helper alone is not a hostile-object sandbox.
note: 05 Findings/D893 Object and array descriptor checks are asymmetric.md

title: Encoded working drafts get shallow parsed validation
body: Each encoded kind capped at 512KiB and total one MiB, then JSON parsed and envelope/schema/kind/draft-object checked. Inner draft structure is not recursively passed through inspectValue. View-state allowed keys also lack full type/enum checks.
note: 05 Findings/D894 Encoded working drafts get shallow parsed validation.md

title: Numeric and request-identity rules differ by operation
body: Generic numeric fields need finite numbers but not universal integer/range checks. Some Studio operations permit missing requestId, while run controls/skill operations require one; start/test agent examples intentionally accepted without it. Handler correlation and semantic validation remain separate.
note: 05 Findings/D895 Numeric and request-identity rules differ by operation.md

title: Studio and extension version grammars differ
body: Studio caps numeric components at signed 32-bit maximum and validates suffix rules; extension grammar lacks that component cap. Enablement/uninstall exact targets check prefix/suffix at message layer rather than parsing full middle version; retained host token supplies stronger equality check.
note: 05 Findings/D896 Studio and extension version grammars differ.md

title: Message validation returns the original object
body: Accepted message is neither cloned nor deeply frozen. Static CONTRACTS freeze only outer object and nested arrays remain shared with action metadata. Normal transport may supply isolated JSON, but validator itself does not create immutable authority.
note: 05 Findings/D897 Message validation returns the original object.md

title: Host dispatch and view restoration are concrete separate callers
body: Host validates before switch and request observation; panel deserializer validates saved view state and clears cached state on failure. Neither validation callback by itself grants a work admission or proves a later effect.
note: 05 Findings/D898 Host dispatch and view restoration are concrete separate callers.md

title: Action metadata describes intended boundaries
body: UI-only and HOST maps label authority/effects/outcomes; build checks host message existence only. Some UI actions described as opening an editor can cause later controller queries or view-state publication. Metadata is not an exhaustive runtime effect detector.
note: 05 Findings/D899 Action metadata describes intended boundaries.md

title: Literal action discovery is lexical
body: Regex finds literal data-action attributes in JavaScript files, including possible comments/dead branches, and cannot discover arbitrary computed action names. Exact missing/stale reconciliation proves agreement between declarations and that lexical set, not actual DOM coverage.
note: 05 Findings/D900 Literal action discovery is lexical.md

title: Action artifact currentness omits source content identity
body: Artifact stores action names/source filenames/contracts but not hashes of implementation files. A source change preserving literal actions can leave artifact bytes unchanged. Current control manifest later hashes referenced source files independently.
note: 05 Findings/D901 Action artifact currentness omits source content identity.md

title: Control source manifest authenticates bytes rather than handler semantics
body: Checks exact lexical inventory path, schema, per-surface ordered-ID hash and unique IDs; resolves source files and hashes them. Source reference symbols/handler backend are copied or described, not AST-validated. Filesystem containment uses resolve/stat without realpath alias rejection.
note: 05 Findings/D902 Control source manifest authenticates bytes rather than handler semantics.md

title: Control contracts have descriptive fallbacks
body: Unknown actions and non-action control kinds can use source-owned-semantic fallback with label-derived effects. Host handler text is synthesized as extension.js plus message name. These relationships need caller inspection rather than assuming the string is a callable path.
note: 05 Findings/D903 Control contracts have descriptive fallbacks.md

title: Interaction profiles and mutation classification use labels
body: Supplied surface/control profiles can override inference. Otherwise regexes classify labels such as remove/run/config, even when an action only edits a draft. This is conservative metadata, not actual effect observation.
note: 05 Findings/D904 Interaction profiles and mutation classification use labels.md

title: Exact action resolver can represent many instances
body: No suffix means all same-action matches form exact class; row variant accepts any dataset key containing id/index/row/key. Multiple named matches can also be exact. This does not mean unique element identity or every instance exercised.
note: 05 Findings/D905 Exact action resolver can represent many instances.md

title: Attempted control IDs can imply visibility without a match
body: Base record sets rendered to exact resolver OR attempted ID; visible follows rendered and enabled uses every over matches, which is true for empty array. Open/display stages then become observed. Caller must supply trustworthy attempt evidence; base projection does not prove DOM presence.
note: 05 Findings/D906 Attempted control IDs can imply visibility without a match.md

title: Interaction completeness does not validate stage identity
body: isCompleteInteractionChain checks thirteen entries and allowed statuses only, not exact names/order/uniqueness, evidence, hashes or timestamps. A malformed thirteen-entry list can satisfy this local predicate. Broader consumers need their own validation.
note: 05 Findings/D907 Interaction completeness does not validate stage identity.md

title: Installed mismatch is caller-supplied to base chain builder
body: hostSourceMismatch defaults false. A true flag blocks every stage; absent false does not establish current installed/source identity. Real walker separately composes source identity and many probe observations after these initial records.
note: 05 Findings/D908 Installed mismatch is caller-supplied to base chain builder.md

title: Contained walk covers only action controls and first match
body: Manifest filtered to kind action. Each control opens fresh preview; only first matching visible enabled element clicked even when match_count exceeds one. DynamicRepair labels are specially unwrapped here, unlike base manifest locator/resolver.
note: 05 Findings/D909 Contained walk covers only action controls and first match.md

title: Contained before and after hashes are narrow UI projections
body: Hashes cover first forty-thousand body-text characters, message count, dialog count and active identifier. They do not bind complete DOM, posted payloads, runtime effects or persistence. A changed hash is not necessarily intended successful action.
note: 05 Findings/D910 Contained before and after hashes are narrow UI projections.md

title: Contained exit success does not mean full interaction success
body: Missing/invisible/disabled controls produce statuses but only interaction_error sets failure exit. Fixed 140ms post-click delay can miss late response/error. Receipt explicitly sets operationally_complete false, preserving correct non-certification boundary.
note: 05 Findings/D911 Contained exit success does not mean full interaction success.md

title: Contained browser cleanup starts after context and page creation
body: Browser launch, context and page creation precede try/finally, so setup failures can bypass browser.close. No whole-run timeout or network interception is supplied in this file. Receipt is exclusive-written after close; fixture resource ownership depends on surrounding runner.
note: 05 Findings/D912 Contained browser cleanup starts after context and page creation.md

title: Installed smoke checks selected live surfaces and cardinalities
body: Driver checks sidebar ready/render acknowledgment, nonzero graph geometry and selected live versus Python snapshot counts. These are concrete host observations when executed, but count equality is not semantic equivalence and geometry does not prove all graph interactions.
note: 05 Findings/D913 Installed smoke checks selected live surfaces and cardinalities.md

title: Installed Studio smoke partly bypasses editor interaction
body: Requires installed source modules directly, creates bridge/approval material and calls setup/creation functions with confirmCreate true. It checks catalog reopening and run outcomes, but receipt knowledge_ui_bridge_cli_backend true is not evidence of an actual webview editor click path.
note: 05 Findings/D914 Installed Studio smoke partly bypasses editor interaction.md

title: Installed smoke assumes isolated ownership from runner
body: Local driver requires receipt path and a workspace folder but does not prove disposable ownership, exact source hash or receipt-path containment. It mutates files/configuration/Studio state and starts host work. External runner owns admission and cleanup; audit did not invoke it.
note: 05 Findings/D915 Installed smoke assumes isolated ownership from runner.md

title: Smoke wait helper cannot bound a hanging predicate
body: waitFor checks elapsed time between awaited predicates. A predicate consuming shell execution stream can itself hang past the nominal timeout. Debug wait result is not checked before exercised-live label; task timeout rejects but listener cleanup only occurs on expected event.
note: 05 Findings/D916 Smoke wait helper cannot bound a hanging predicate.md

title: Smoke event verification matches names rather than exact attempted correlation
body: Operation Set comes from recent activity events; required names may have been produced by other activity. Test/debug/shell/SCM/extensions are reported but not all required complete. Extensions registration is checked while live mutation intentionally omitted.
note: 05 Findings/D917 Smoke event verification matches names rather than exact attempted correlation.md

title: Smoke cleanup and receipt publication are not one closure transaction
body: Bridge disposal and key-env restoration have a local finally; test controller, terminal, task listener and configuration restoration are not enclosed by a global cleanup finally. Receipt write uses overwrite mode and occurs only after assertions; failed runs may leave no final receipt.
note: 05 Findings/D918 Smoke cleanup and receipt publication are not one closure transaction.md

title: Broad extension contract tests are mostly source assertions
body: Many test titles describe live/governed paths but assertions match source strings or relative positions. A few normalization/context/path tests execute helpers with synthetic data; their evidence is stronger only for those bounded cases.
note: 05 Findings/D919 Broad extension contract tests are mostly source assertions.md

title: Hardening fixtures test selected boundaries rather than all host outcomes
body: Coordination corruption and locks use local trees, process termination uses injected fake processes, and message tests validate supplied objects. Protocol-copy equality is source currentness, not installed-host execution. No fresh tests run for this report.
note: 05 Findings/D920 Hardening fixtures test selected boundaries rather than all host outcomes.md

title: Action inventory tests prove declared denominator agreement
body: Compare generated bytes, source handler strings, metadata presence and synthetic row matches. Manifest hash-format assertions do not prove a clicked control reached backend effect or durable receipt.
note: 05 Findings/D921 Action inventory tests prove declared denominator agreement.md

title: Contained walker unit tests do not run the walker
body: Tests exercise actionIdentity/matchesVariant and status predicate only. They do not launch browser, inspect repeated instances, validate exact stage names or verify receipt custody.
note: 05 Findings/D922 Contained walker unit tests do not run the walker.md

title: Transcript adapter planning does not run extraction
body: Profile validates schema and optional tool root; adapter plan binds runner hash and argv but returns execution_authorized false. CLI ingest independently dispatches without loading profile, so profile input formats are not its enforcement source.
note: 05 Findings/D923 Transcript adapter planning does not run extraction.md

title: Transcript source link check follows resolution
body: Explicit input is resolved before is_symlink, hiding original alias. Directory child links are excluded, but ancestor aliases and later replacements are not locked. File count/byte budget follow enumeration and precede full hashing/copying.
note: 05 Findings/D924 Transcript source link check follows resolution.md

title: Transcript identifiers can collapse distinct source relationships
body: Source ID derives from first twenty digest characters, so identical bytes in different files have same source ID. Conversation ID is filename stem, so separate source names/extensions can share conversation. Writer/export dictionaries collapse those keys without uniqueness checks.
note: 05 Findings/D925 Transcript identifiers can collapse distinct source relationships.md

title: Ingest verifies copied bytes but publishes without exclusive final target
body: Copies are hashed against plan before os.replace stage to target. Existence checked earlier, no final exclusive reservation, no fsync and no aggregate size recheck during copy. Failure retains stage under failed name; output parent aliases are not independently rejected.
note: 05 Findings/D926 Ingest verifies copied bytes but publishes without exclusive final target.md

title: Transcript span validation is numeric rather than textual
body: Schema requires positive line bounds and runtime rejects end before start. It never checks source line count or whether record text/label is supported by the cited span. The immutable source copy preserves evidence for a separate reviewer.
note: 05 Findings/D927 Transcript span validation is numeric rather than textual.md

title: Verified transcript states rely on declared evidence strings
body: Verified completion/outcome needs ASSERTED plus nonempty validation_evidence array. Strings may be empty and are not resolved/authenticated. Certain unconfirmed action states cannot be verified outcomes, but this is consistency logic rather than verification execution.
note: 05 Findings/D928 Verified transcript states rely on declared evidence strings.md

title: Canonical record writing trusts manifest before checking provenance
body: Writer loads run manifest without verifying its digest/source-copy bytes first, then binds records against its supplied sources/queue. Records and manifest write separately using overwrite-capable write_text after earlier exists check; no lock/reservation protects concurrent writers.
note: 05 Findings/D929 Canonical record writing trusts manifest before checking provenance.md

title: Later run validation omits writer relationship checks
body: validate_run checks source schemas/copy hashes and individual record schemas plus digests. It does not repeat record-ID uniqueness or source/conversation/queue binding. Resealed malformed relationships can pass this local integrity check.
note: 05 Findings/D930 Later run validation omits writer relationship checks.md

title: Run source paths are not constrained by source schema
body: ingested_copy is only nonempty string, then joined with run_dir without containment check. A supplied absolute/traversal path in a resealed manifest can make validation read outside run. Manifest itself lacks a complete schema validation here.
note: 05 Findings/D931 Run source paths are not constrained by source schema.md

title: Export validates then rereads mutable files
body: Run validation is followed by fresh records and manifest reads, so checked bytes are not retained throughout export. Unknown requested conversation IDs yield blank rows; duplicate conversation sources use last mapping. Output uses existence check then ordinary write without atomic reservation.
note: 05 Findings/D932 Export validates then rereads mutable files.md

title: Transcript summary labels can overgeneralize a mixed conversation
body: Any record with VERIFIED or VERIFIED_COMPLETED selects verified outcome for entire conversation, even when other records report failure/uncertainty. CSV quotes syntax through DictWriter but does not neutralize spreadsheet formula-leading values.
note: 05 Findings/D933 Transcript summary labels can overgeneralize a mixed conversation.md

title: Queue normalization and transcript workflow checks are structural
body: Cross-queue transfer matches declared queue/term; reviewer/evidence are strings, not authenticated receipts. Workflow check compares step-ID set and unknown dependencies only: duplicates, missing intended dependencies and cycles/order are not rejected.
note: 05 Findings/D934 Queue normalization and transcript workflow checks are structural.md

title: Transcript fixtures do not prove extraction accuracy
body: Tests cover dry-run, source copying, selected state/queue refusals, stable CSV and tampered copy. They supply invented canonical text and do not validate text spans, authenticated validation evidence, resealed relationships or publication races.
note: 05 Findings/D935 Transcript fixtures do not prove extraction accuracy.md

title: Audit archive exclusions are filename policy rather than secret scanning
body: Inventory excludes selected directories/environment filenames by case-sensitive names. Root resolution hides original root aliases, traversal materializes before filtering, and payload bytes are retained in memory. No aggregate byte/file bound establishes bounded packaging.
note: 05 Findings/D936 Audit archive exclusions are filename policy rather than secret scanning.md

title: Portable audit includes prerequisites without proving readiness
body: Prerequisite JSON must be an object, but no valid/ready result is enforced. Optional attestation need only parse as JSON; signature/trust not verified. Empty eligible payload can still produce archive. These are packaged claims, not certification.
note: 05 Findings/D937 Portable audit includes prerequisites without proving readiness.md

title: Archive and checksum are separate publications
body: Temporary ZIP replaces destination, then destination read/hash and checksum temp replace follow. Failure can leave new ZIP with old/missing checksum. Output roots excluded from inputs, but prerequisite/attestation output collisions are not comprehensively excluded; no pair rollback/fsync.
note: 05 Findings/D938 Archive and checksum are separate publications.md

title: Audit verifier establishes internal consistency only
body: Checks outer hash, duplicate/unsafe names, declared per-file hashes and exact member set/count. It does not validate full manifest schema, payload byte totals, unique manifest rows, exclusion semantics or nonempty payload. Recomputed unkeyed hashes do not authenticate origin.
note: 05 Findings/D939 Audit verifier establishes internal consistency only.md

title: Portable archive verification has resource and shape limits
body: Whole archive hashed before verification try and members read without decompression/aggregate cap. Unsafe-name checks are not an extraction engine; some malformed shape or encrypted-member exceptions fall outside caught types. No extraction performed by verifier.
note: 05 Findings/D940 Portable archive verification has resource and shape limits.md

title: Bundle CLI is a dispatcher rather than certification owner
body: Unique label=path arguments dispatched to runtime builder/verification, printed result determines exit status with missing valid default true. Build has no dry-run mode here. Audit only inspected this entrypoint.
note: 05 Findings/D941 Bundle CLI is a dispatcher rather than certification owner.md

title: Exact lock parsing is narrower than package semantics
body: Requires exact pin and lowercase SHA-256 syntax, handles continuations and rejects interrupted continuation. Name normalization lowercases and replaces underscore only; versions are nonwhitespace strings, not fully parsed package-version semantics. Empty lock returns invalid with possibly empty errors.
note: 05 Findings/D942 Exact lock parsing is narrower than package semantics.md

title: Wheelhouse hash membership does not bind wheel identity
body: Top-level wheel bytes compared to union of allowed hashes; package metadata, filename/version and platform compatibility not parsed. One allowed hash can satisfy multiple pins sharing it. Caller may receive valid true for empty wheelhouse/empty invalid lock when no errors exist.
note: 05 Findings/D943 Wheelhouse hash membership does not bind wheel identity.md

title: Environment scrub does not itself isolate network or executable search
body: Allowlist retains PATH/system locations and sets pip offline/config flags. Empty mapping uses ambient environment because of source-or-os.environ fallback. Offline argv construction returns a list and does not execute or apply a network boundary.
note: 05 Findings/D944 Environment scrub does not itself isolate network or executable search.md

title: Toolchain identity can combine two different interpreter identities
body: Optional executable path is hashed, but Python version/platform fields come from current running process. Filesystem case-sensitivity field is based on path normalization behavior rather than probing actual target filesystem.
note: 05 Findings/D945 Toolchain identity can combine two different interpreter identities.md

title: Support matrix validation uses declarations and text presence
body: Compares project requires-python/classifiers to policy, then checks CI text for expected minor/runner strings. It does not execute CI jobs or validate parsed job matrix topology. Certificate platform fields are checked as supplied strings, not cryptographically measured platform identity.
note: 05 Findings/D946 Support matrix validation uses declarations and text presence.md

title: Release environment validity and lock validity can diverge
body: Validator copies lock errors but not false lock.valid as error, checks installed distribution versions and declared support/current minor. Empty lock can therefore yield valid true with lock_valid false when other checks pass. It does not verify installed package bytes or require current OS in the environment path.
note: 05 Findings/D947 Release environment validity and lock validity can diverge.md

title: Portable audit tests exercise tiny byte fixtures
body: Source relocation verifies archive independence; tamper test adds duplicate ZIP entry and exclusion test checks known names. No independent signature proof, zip bomb bound, pair failure or full manifest semantics established.
note: 05 Findings/D948 Portable audit tests exercise tiny byte fixtures.md

title: Release environment tests do not execute offline installation
body: Tests named installation/network check generated argv/environment and fake wheel byte hashes. Support tests compare declared metadata; one local FileLock fixture does not prove all advertised platforms. This audit ran none of these product tests.
note: 05 Findings/D949 Release environment tests do not execute offline installation.md

title: External catalog checks are partial structural checks
body: Loader checks schema/count/ID and selected deferred-state invariants, but does not validate all record schemas, candidate/bundle ID uniqueness or cross-record references. License data is returned rather than semantically verified.
note: 05 Findings/D950 External catalog checks are partial structural checks.md

title: External metadata limits follow full loading and ranking
body: Catalogs are fully read, tokenized and sorted before output limits. Hydration deduplicates the complete input iterator before slicing; full record serialization precedes byte-budget rejection. Top-level body/content/raw_source removal does not remove nested payloads.
note: 05 Findings/D951 External metadata limits follow full loading and ranking.md

title: Metadata truncation can obscure requested identities
body: Missing IDs consume selected positions. First oversized record stops processing, so later requested IDs may never be examined or reported missing; valid can be true with no returned record. max_records has no fixed ceiling.
note: 05 Findings/D952 Metadata truncation can obscure requested identities.md

title: External stage commissioning check does not bind project identity
body: Plan requires commissioning file existence, not its schema/content or project identity. Caller project_id is not bound to resolved root. Source body containment/hash is checked, but no expected catalog hash or aggregate body budget is enforced.
note: 05 Findings/D953 External stage commissioning check does not bind project identity.md

title: Stage dependency closure omits unknown identifiers
body: Dependency rejection concerns known candidate IDs not selected; unknown dependency strings are not comprehensively rejected. Plan digest binds chosen identities/hashes/collisions/dependencies, not full project root, current catalog and approval evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D954 Stage dependency closure omits unknown identifiers.md

title: Direct stage apply trusts plan while CLI plans freshly
body: Apply does not recompute plan hash, source body hashes, commissioning or dependencies. Frozen plan object contains mutable dictionaries. CLI stage calls planner immediately, so direct forged/stale-plan behavior must not be represented as inevitable CLI behavior.
note: 05 Findings/D955 Direct stage apply trusts plan while CLI plans freshly.md

title: Stage receipt labels are not authenticated approvals
body: Supplied evidence values are stringified and truthiness-filtered, rather than resolved and signature-verified. Candidate receipt is written without body installation, active registry admission or authority grant. No fsync or full cross-step transaction closes publication.
note: 05 Findings/D956 Stage receipt labels are not authenticated approvals.md

title: Stage and revoke plan IDs need caller boundary distinction
body: Direct apply builds target from supplied plan.plan_id. Revoke accepts raw plan_id from CLI and interpolates it into path without portable ID or resolved containment guard. A crafted ID may select paths outside expected candidate directory; audit did not execute this path.
note: 05 Findings/D957 Stage and revoke plan IDs need caller boundary distinction.md

title: Existing revocation marker is trusted without equivalence check
body: Revoke requires source is_file but does not authenticate source receipt. Existing marker returns valid true/applied false without checking marker content or new evidence equivalence. Source receipt remains retained.
note: 05 Findings/D958 Existing revocation marker is trusted without equivalence check.md

title: External hook token is context rather than authority
body: Hook checks enabled/event/evidence labels/reentry/depth. Token hashes hook/event/chain but not full profile, authenticated evidence or expiry; no consumption or execution follows. CLI valid envelope does not mean allowed hook decision.
note: 05 Findings/D959 External hook token is context rather than authority.md

title: Portable session filtering is shallow
body: Sensitive-key regex examines top-level keys, not nested values. Retained fields can stringify arbitrary supplied objects and reference strings can be iterated as characters. No aggregate byte budget or authenticated session identity is established.
note: 05 Findings/D960 Portable session filtering is shallow.md

title: Session parity can pass while authority differs
body: Comparator valid is based on selected semantic fields and excludes authority equality. It separately returns authority_equal, so consumers must inspect both fields. Empty or weakly shaped mappings can compare equal without normalized session provenance.
note: 05 Findings/D961 Session parity can pass while authority differs.md

title: Route rank trusts supplied measurements and nonfinite values
body: Threshold checks and weighted score use supplied floats without finite/range checks. NaN can bypass comparisons; negative cost/latency can improve score. Authority/safety booleans are required declarations, not authenticated grants. Quality threshold then weighted score is not strict highest-quality ordering.
note: 05 Findings/D962 Route rank trusts supplied measurements and nonfinite values.md

title: External workflow validation checks quoted names
body: Required workflow step strings are searched in source text, not parsed into executable dependency graph. Presence of inventory/license/search/stage/admission/certification names proves neither ordering nor successful operation.
note: 05 Findings/D963 External workflow validation checks quoted names.md

title: External provider fixtures stop at candidate semantics
body: Tests use empty commissioning JSON and fake evidence labels; selected schema checks occur inside tests rather than all runtime paths. They do not establish installed skill bodies, authenticated approval, hostile plan-ID safety, concurrent writes or finite route metrics.
note: 05 Findings/D964 External provider fixtures stop at candidate semantics.md

title: Security catalog count checks do not validate every relationship
body: Loader checks provider/source declarations, 817 records, domain counts, risk classes and selected lifecycle/high-risk fields. Optional graph load checks count, not endpoint/relation uniqueness; without graph load, reported edge count is expected constant. Full schemas and all risk-count declarations are not enforced here.
note: 05 Findings/D965 Security catalog count checks do not validate every relationship.md

title: Security discovery scores correlated metadata signals
body: BM25, domain aliases and framework boosts come from the same catalog; they are not independent verification. All records are processed before top-k. Descriptions are opt-in, but other external metadata remains untrusted candidate text.
note: 05 Findings/D966 Security discovery scores correlated metadata signals.md

title: Security golden routes measure expected-domain retrieval
body: Each case repeats catalog search and succeeds when expected domain appears in top-k. This does not measure top-one precision, authority soundness, archive custody or successful security operations.
note: 05 Findings/D967 Security golden routes measure expected-domain retrieval.md

title: Security risk decisions are engagement declaration checks
body: R0 allows nonempty non-denied targets; R1 requires allowlist and read-only/advisory. Higher risks require supplied authorization labels, date window, human flag and mode-specific fields. No evidence signature, target identity normalization or actual host grant is authenticated; authority_granted remains false.
note: 05 Findings/D968 Security risk decisions are engagement declaration checks.md

title: Security environment labels are exact policy inputs
