body: Active production exception tests exact production string. R4 requires exact isolated_lab and lab_simulation. Caller-supplied environment labels are not independently measured environment containment. Tests exercise these declarations with synthetic broad-date engagement.
note: 05 Findings/D969 Security environment labels are exact policy inputs.md

title: Security graph input seeds can exceed node budget
body: Initial seed set is built before traversal and is not trimmed to max_nodes. Depth zero can return too many seeds without truncation. Entire graph and all seed input are loaded before output budgets. Positive parameters lack fixed upper limits.
note: 05 Findings/D970 Security graph input seeds can exceed node budget.md

title: Capped security graph may return dangling edges
body: Outgoing edge is appended before target-node cap check. At cap, target may be omitted while edge remains, so returned edge endpoints need not all appear in returned nodes. One-seed tests assert counts only.
note: 05 Findings/D971 Capped security graph may return dangling edges.md

title: Security package ranks before filtering authority
body: Despite docstring and test naming, build calls search with limit 100 before risk/engagement checks. Eligible candidates below that cutoff cannot be selected. Selection stops once max_bodies is filled; rejected list is not exhaustive.
note: 05 Findings/D972 Security package ranks before filtering authority.md

title: Security execution package is candidate context only
body: Package contains selected metadata and declaration decisions, not hydrated bodies or executed scripts. Catalog is loaded separately from search, allowing changed metadata between reads. Package digest omits full engagement scope/authorization and exact body identity. Runtime authority remains false.
note: 05 Findings/D973 Security execution package is candidate context only.md

title: Security reference hydration pins bytes but reopens archive
body: Whole archive digest is checked before opening ZIP separately, so exact checked handle is not retained. Selected body is matched by source-path suffix, hashed and returned as untrusted text; no extraction or provider script execution occurs.
note: 05 Findings/D974 Security reference hydration pins bytes but reopens archive.md

title: Security archive byte limits follow expensive reads
body: Whole archive hash precedes body budget, all input IDs deduplicate before slice, and selected ZIP member is decompressed/read before byte-cap comparison. No total archive/decompression resource cap is established. Empty selection can succeed without bodies.
note: 05 Findings/D975 Security archive byte limits follow expensive reads.md

title: Verified security finding requires labels rather than proof
body: Required keys are checked for presence; verified status requires nonempty evidence list of mappings with truthy reference and sha256. Hash grammar/file bytes, severity/confidence/assets/actions and evidence authority are not authenticated. Canonical promotion remains false.
note: 05 Findings/D976 Verified security finding requires labels rather than proof.md

title: Security workflow step text is not executed ordering
body: Validator searches quoted names for normalize/authority-filter/discover/rank/hydrate/validate-outcome/record-learning. It does not parse dependencies or run them. Its stated authority-before-ranking order differs from candidate package implementation.
note: 05 Findings/D977 Security workflow step text is not executed ordering.md

title: Security archive test substitutes a fixture trust pin
body: Hydration test patches expected archive SHA and catalog loader for tiny ZIP. It proves chosen fixture hash and no extraction/script load, not actual production archive identity or reopen/decompression race safety.
note: 05 Findings/D978 Security archive test substitutes a fixture trust pin.md

title: Security tests do not observe claimed filter ordering
body: Package test checks allowed risk outputs and some rejections, not call order or eligible candidates beyond top 100. Graph test uses one seed and does not check endpoint closure. Finding test supplies invented hash string; it does not resolve evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D979 Security tests do not observe claimed filter ordering.md

title: Security CLI exposes independent authority and reference routes
body: Authority result wraps valid true around the decision, while package, hydrate, graph and finding validation are separate commands. Reading reference content does not imply engagement approval or security execution.
note: 05 Findings/D980 Security CLI exposes independent authority and reference routes.md

title: Readiness version parsing is a bounded numeric subset
body: First numeric substring supplies three-part version and ignores prerelease semantics. Caret ceiling always increments major, so zero-major constraints differ from full semver. Alternatives short-circuit, potentially leaving unsupported later alternatives unexamined. This is local comparison logic, not package-manager resolution.
note: 05 Findings/D981 Readiness version parsing is a bounded numeric subset.md

title: Readiness resolves executable paths without byte identity
body: Explicit relative/absolute paths and PATH candidates resolve to files; no digest/ownership or expected tool identity is checked. Windows batch dispatch selects ambient COMSPEC. A parseable version string is not proof of the intended binary or its launch functionality.
note: 05 Findings/D982 Readiness resolves executable paths without byte identity.md

title: Probe output is bounded after subprocess capture
body: subprocess.run captures complete stdout/stderr before joining and truncating to 4096 characters. Individual deadlines bound direct waits, not aggregate work or descendant lifetime. Scrubbed environment does not impose network or filesystem isolation; read_only/not-used fields are declarations.
note: 05 Findings/D983 Probe output is bounded after subprocess capture.md

title: Browser readiness can use file version without launch
body: Windows browser file-version metadata yields ready with no version requirement or process launch. Other platforms use --version. Neither path checks that the browser can render the certification app or that required automation features work.
note: 05 Findings/D984 Browser readiness can use file version without launch.md

title: Readiness dependency parity is version-label parity
body: Lock v3 root name/version/direct dependency mappings must match and direct pins must look exact. Installed direct package.json version is compared, but bytes/integrity hashes, transitive installed closure and executable scripts are not verified. Registry package names are joined as paths without additional containment grammar.
note: 05 Findings/D985 Readiness dependency parity is version-label parity.md

title: Managed readiness consumes phase without receipt authentication
body: Managed campaign at validated or later with intake closed and no unresolved entries returns ready. repair_campaign_status validates state shape/phase, not current full-profile/validation receipts or source digest. This avoids rerunning ordered validation but is a weaker local evidence check.
note: 05 Findings/D986 Managed readiness consumes phase without receipt authentication.md

title: Unmanaged readiness launches validation and parses truncated combined output
body: Unmanaged path invokes runtime.cli validate and requires exit success plus valid true JSON. Probe combines stderr with stdout and truncates before JSON parsing, so otherwise valid noisy/large output may be rejected. Nested malformed metadata or nonobject payload can escape handled exceptions.
note: 05 Findings/D987 Unmanaged readiness launches validation and parses truncated combined output.md

title: Readiness tests mock tool execution
body: Tests use invented executable paths/version strings and synthetic late-phase campaign JSON without validation receipts. They prove selected classifications and no managed validation rerun, not actual browser startup, executable authenticity or network isolation.
note: 05 Findings/D988 Readiness tests mock tool execution.md

title: Readiness entrypoints have different failure exits
body: CLI release readiness returns normal CLI invalid status while bootstrap wrapper returns 2 for unready. Both call same assessor; bootstrap label read-only does not change effects of child tools or unmanaged validation.
note: 05 Findings/D989 Readiness entrypoints have different failure exits.md

title: Exact certification fixtures are concrete but narrow
body: Harness defines tiny repository, policy, memory, benchmark, JSON and archive fixtures for 56 helper IDs. Positive case coverage is set equality against registry, which does not separately reject duplicate admitted IDs; each helper has one main positive scenario.
note: 05 Findings/D990 Exact certification fixtures are concrete but narrow.md

title: One negative argument case produces multiple coverage labels
body: Eleven explicit denial examples are supplemented by generic --pacify-x-invalid-boundary for other tools. Every negative ToolCase is labeled malformed_input, wrong_type and boundary_denial; later booleans reuse the same passed flag. These are not three separately exercised scenarios.
note: 05 Findings/D991 One negative argument case produces multiple coverage labels.md

title: Exact helper isolation is working directory and environment convention
body: Runner copies ambient environment and sets only no-bytecode/no-user-site flags. It does not create an OS filesystem/network sandbox or use governed process/workspace custody here. Absolute source scripts execute outside fixture tree; selected interpreter is supplied directly.
note: 05 Findings/D992 Exact helper isolation is working directory and environment convention.md

title: Exact filesystem comparison misses deletions and outside effects
body: Snapshot hashes files under temp except __pycache__. Changed list iterates only after entries, so deleted files are absent and unreported. Writes outside temp, metadata-only changes and effects in excluded caches are not observed. Symlink targets may be followed by is_file/read_bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D993 Exact filesystem comparison misses deletions and outside effects.md

title: Exact output pass does not enforce semantic result schema
body: Pass requires expected exit, parseable JSON when requested, output existence and no observed unexpected local additions/changes. Parsed JSON need not be object or valid true; json_object is reported but not checked. Expected output may be directory, and semantic contents are not asserted by ToolCase.
note: 05 Findings/D994 Exact output pass does not enforce semantic result schema.md

title: Exact timeout branch loses observed effect information
body: Timeout returns failed result with empty effect lists and all declared outputs missing without taking an after snapshot. Direct subprocess timeout does not prove descendant closure. OSError/decoding failures outside TimeoutExpired handling can abort aggregate and skip terminal receipt.
note: 05 Findings/D995 Exact timeout branch loses observed effect information.md

title: Repeat normalization can remove meaningful differences
body: JSON keys containing time, created, updated, duration or timestamp are removed recursively, in addition to selected volatile names. This can hide timeout/runtime or other semantically meaningful fields. Fixture-root redaction is case-insensitive substring replacement, not path-token equivalence.
note: 05 Findings/D996 Repeat normalization can remove meaningful differences.md

title: Shared fixture state differs from the repeat tree
body: Positive and negative cases for all tools share one temp tree; repeat cases share its repeat-run child. Earlier helper outputs persist for later cases, while repeat has separate accumulated history. The comparison is not independent fresh-tree execution per helper/case.
note: 05 Findings/D997 Shared fixture state differs from the repeat tree.md

title: Helper source hash precedes a separate execution open
body: Each registry target hash is checked once before subprocess runs or cache reuse. No immutable copy/handle binds the executed script bytes to that hash across four cases. Target path is joined from registry without containment guard; registry is trusted input at this layer.
note: 05 Findings/D998 Helper source hash precedes a separate execution open.md

title: Exact cache identity omits selected interpreter and dependencies
body: Cache key binds tool, complete registry, harness and current Python process platform/version, but not python_executable argument bytes/version, dependency/import trees, environment variables or wrapper implementation. Reusing cache across those changes is not excluded by this key.
note: 05 Findings/D999 Exact cache identity omits selected interpreter and dependencies.md

title: Cache seal detects corruption but is not authenticated provenance
body: Persistent receipt seal is SHA-256 of canonical JSON, recomputable by a writer. Loader checks key/seal/result.passed/repeat presence but not complete nested schema. Tests flip passed without resealing; they do not test a coherently forged seal.
note: 05 Findings/D1000 Cache seal detects corruption but is not authenticated provenance.md

title: Exact aggregate timeout is a between-tool check
body: Deadline is checked at beginning of admitted-tool loop only. Up to four case deadlines and snapshot work follow; wrapper loop runs even after aggregate break and has no aggregate check. Fixture creation, hashing, output capture and temp cleanup are outside a hard aggregate deadline.
note: 05 Findings/D1001 Exact aggregate timeout is a between-tool check.md

title: Wrapper certificate strength differs from exact helper checks
body: Seven wrappers run one positive JSON fixture; there is no wrapper expected source hash check before execution, negative case or deterministic repeat here. Report hashes wrapper afterward. Their count should not imply equivalent coverage to admitted exact helper cases.
note: 05 Findings/D1002 Wrapper certificate strength differs from exact helper checks.md

title: Harness progress and caches use ordinary overwrite publication
body: Progress rewrites whole receipt in_progress with accumulated events/results; final overwrites it after temporary directory context exits. Cache files similarly write directly. No atomic commit/fsync/locking or guaranteed terminal write on exception protects these publications.
note: 05 Findings/D1003 Harness progress and caches use ordinary overwrite publication.md

title: Certification strength label does not include every tool-pass condition
body: negative-path-certified label depends on denial and repeat, while tool_passed also requires direct load and positive behavior. A row may retain stronger label despite failing another required case. Final aggregate correctly checks all tool conditions; consumers must not rely only on label.
note: 05 Findings/D1004 Certification strength label does not include every tool-pass condition.md

title: Python surface direct label consumes only positive case
body: Classifier direct_paths selects positive_behavior.passed and wrapper behavior.passed without requiring full exact result valid or negative/repeat success. CLI combines final valid flags separately; map builder still writes projection before returning failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1005 Python surface direct label consumes only positive case.md

title: Ownership map current flag is publication intent rather than success proof
body: Builder unconditionally sets map_current true, writes normal overwrite, then returns combined validity. It does not reread/hash the published map or refuse write on failed certification. Clean source export likewise sets this flag in its projection sequence.
note: 05 Findings/D1006 Ownership map current flag is publication intent rather than success proof.md

title: Exact harness tests mostly assert its own aggregate projections
body: Tests run fixtures then assert counts, inferred coverage fields, local effect lists and normalized repeat. Timeout test is one direct sleeping child; cache test observes simple corruption rejection and may reuse process cache. No deletion/outside effect, resealed cache, alternative interpreter or hard aggregate deadline coverage is established.
note: 05 Findings/D1007 Exact harness tests mostly assert its own aggregate projections.md

title: Canonical owner index silently keeps first duplicate identity
body: Records deduplicate by object_type/object_id and ignore later competing owner metadata. Registry extraction visits top-level lists only; workflow IDs use filename stems. Index digest seals projected records, not source file hashes or runtime implementation.
note: 05 Findings/D1008 Canonical owner index silently keeps first duplicate identity.md

title: Disposition ownership is path and alias inference
body: Large first-match rule table assigns known packs to canonical files/skills based on names, suffixes and path markers. Rationale strings such as reviewed/implemented/admitted are fixed text, not results of semantic comparison or admission checks. Unknown code falls back to merge into capability_routing.
note: 05 Findings/D1009 Disposition ownership is path and alias inference.md

title: Source inventory does not compare expected tree digest
body: expected_tree_sha256 is copied to output only. inventory_sha256 hashes enumerated relative path/size/content rows, but no equality condition compares the two fields. CLI expected-tree flag therefore does not enforce source snapshot identity.
note: 05 Findings/D1010 Source inventory does not compare expected tree digest.md

title: Disposition zero-unaccounted count is not independent closure
body: Builder sets unaccounted_count=0 after is_file enumeration. Nonfiles/empty directories are not represented; symlink files can be followed. No second matching snapshot or immediate equality check establishes stable full-tree inventory. File size is read after content hash, allowing mixed-time metadata.
note: 05 Findings/D1011 Disposition zero-unaccounted count is not independent closure.md

title: Overlay classification checks current target bytes without durable binding
body: Existing matching bytes yield retain, existing differing target merge, absent target admit. Target may be directory or alias; no target expected hash is retained in differing case. No actual merge/admission or owner existence verification occurs.
note: 05 Findings/D1012 Overlay classification checks current target bytes without durable binding.md

title: Disposition validator accepts some weakly shaped resealed records
body: Path check detects nonobject/duplicates but never tests nonempty string, so one empty path can pass. Owner/hash need truthiness only. Byte totals, digest syntax, inventory digest recomputation, disposition counts and expected-tree identity are unchecked; recomputed report seal can cover malformed values.
note: 05 Findings/D1013 Disposition validator accepts some weakly shaped resealed records.md

title: Disposition report seal authenticates no external evidence
body: Self-digest establishes consistency with supplied report fields, not provenance authenticity or equality to current source. Report validation never reads source or selected owners. Empty records with matching count/zero-unaccounted and seal can be valid.
note: 05 Findings/D1014 Disposition report seal authenticates no external evidence.md

title: Disposition writer has separate unconstrained output publications
body: Owner report writes before disposition report with ordinary overwrite. Outputs may coincide with each other or source paths; no containment/collision guard, atomic pair or readback is shown. Failure can leave one new report and one old or absent report.
note: 05 Findings/D1015 Disposition writer has separate unconstrained output publications.md

title: Disposition tests cover labels rather than completed integration
body: Fixtures exercise new overlay, cache exclusion and direct/wrapped external defer. They do not compare expected tree hash, test owner implementation, or execute a merge. Invalid owner fixture also changes report digest, so it does not isolate every semantic check.
note: 05 Findings/D1016 Disposition tests cover labels rather than completed integration.md

title: Structural closed-world scope is explicitly selective
body: Duplicate inventory excludes external environments, evidence, __pycache__, committed WAL and selected derived/custody directories; links are skipped. Walker limits are 100000 files, depth128 and 2GiB and raise on excess. Other checks independently scan folders, so one inventory denominator does not cover every subcheck.
note: 05 Findings/D1017 Structural closed-world scope is explicitly selective.md

title: Exact duplicate exemption can misname nonempty package files
body: All matching paths ending __init__.py are classified empty-package-markers without testing empty content in classifier. Group byte equality proves they match each other, not that they are empty. Other classes likewise rely on fixed path sets and names.
note: 05 Findings/D1018 Exact duplicate exemption can misname nonempty package files.md

title: Logic duplicate signature omits decorators and short functions
body: Only functions with at least three body statements are hashed. Root function name/decorators and all type_comment/type_params fields are removed, while local identifiers remain. Decorated or generic functions with different semantics can normalize together; short or renamed-local equivalence can be missed.
note: 05 Findings/D1019 Logic duplicate signature omits decorators and short functions.md

title: Duplicate review metadata is not behavioral execution
body: Function/path patterns assign digest adapters, CLI boilerplate, progress helpers and other reviewed categories after normalized equality. Their behavioral-parity/regeneration descriptions are labels; classification does not run those behaviors or regeneration commands.
note: 05 Findings/D1020 Duplicate review metadata is not behavioral execution.md

title: Import graph resolves first matching ancestor rather than most specific module
body: For each candidate, next module satisfying equality-or-prefix is selected in insertion order. A package ancestor can be chosen before exact submodule. From-import aliases are not expanded into submodule candidates, and package __init__ relative context uses parent calculation. Cycle graph therefore approximates actual imports.
note: 05 Findings/D1021 Import graph resolves first matching ancestor rather than most specific module.md

title: Import cycle traversal can revisit many paths
body: Cycle detection recursively explores paths from every node with active-set detection but no global visited/SCC reduction. Dense acyclic or cyclic graphs can cause large repeated work and recursion depth; no explicit time/node output budget bounds this stage.
note: 05 Findings/D1022 Import cycle traversal can revisit many paths.md

title: Callable reachability executes imports in current process
body: Entrypoint resolver import_module uses current sys.path/cache and checks callable attributes. It does not load from audited root, authenticate module bytes or call workflow. Import side effects and exceptions other than ImportError/AttributeError can escape.
note: 05 Findings/D1023 Callable reachability executes imports in current process.md

title: Workflow and skill set equality can hide duplicate declarations
body: Catalog, semantic skill IDs, workflow definitions/handlers and binding maps are compared as sets/dictionaries. Duplicate IDs or repeated binding paths can collapse. Skill orchestration dependency graph catches unknown edges/cycles but not duplicate step IDs or intended operational order beyond supplied dependencies.
note: 05 Findings/D1024 Workflow and skill set equality can hide duplicate declarations.md

title: Policy consistency does not establish enforcement reachability
body: Policy index body paths must equal top-level JSON files excluding index files, and startup IDs must be known. This does not check complete policy semantics or runtime enforcement callers; duplicate IDs/bodies collapse into sets.
note: 05 Findings/D1025 Policy consistency does not establish enforcement reachability.md

title: Structural release claims depend on selected text and lifecycle label
body: release_open is lifecycle.status != complete, then selected document strings/version patterns/count tables are checked. Forbidden claims are exact substrings after limited formatting removal. This does not authenticate the lifecycle completion claim or semantically inspect all documentation.
note: 05 Findings/D1026 Structural release claims depend on selected text and lifecycle label.md

title: Documented CLI checker uses an independent static command list
body: Only lines starting engineering-bootstrap space in README/START_HERE are tokenized. Hand-maintained top-level/nested names omit newer commands such as release readiness; flags and deeper parser semantics are not exercised. Valid examples can be rejected or malformed options missed.
note: 05 Findings/D1027 Documented CLI checker uses an independent static command list.md

title: Structural marker check dynamically executes scanner module
body: Loader suppresses bytecode while exec_module runs and restores process-global flag afterward, then calls audit. No module digest is authenticated here. It is executable local analysis rather than pure text scanning, and concurrent threads share bytecode flag.
note: 05 Findings/D1028 Structural marker check dynamically executes scanner module.md

title: Structural aggregation can lose delegated invalid state
body: Five delegated validator results contribute errors lists; their valid fields are not required true. A false valid with empty errors can contribute no failure, and generated failed fallback is used only if errors key absent. Final valid is not errors. Other top-level stages lie outside checked exception wrapper.
note: 05 Findings/D1029 Structural aggregation can lose delegated invalid state.md

title: Policy audit-item coverage is supplied category membership
body: Audit-item IDs form dictionary, so duplicates overwrite. Empty categories pass all vacuously; category names are indexed without schema check here. Required item count reflects surviving IDs rather than an independent expected list.
note: 05 Findings/D1030 Policy audit-item coverage is supplied category membership.md

title: Structural release composition can run the same audit twice
body: Release certification calls audit_framework, which itself calls structural audit, then calls structural audit again in its checks mapping. These are repeated local inspections, not independent evidence owners or an atomic snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1031 Structural release composition can run the same audit twice.md

title: Structural fixture tests do not execute named parity or regeneration
body: Tests with behavioral-parity/regenerate names inspect equivalence-rule strings and classifications. Selected mutation tests exercise orphan/declaration drift. Cached root audit is reused across assertions; fixture clone uses hardlinks and explicit detach before changing known files.
note: 05 Findings/D1032 Structural fixture tests do not execute named parity or regeneration.md

title: Doctor validity and operational readiness are separate
body: Composer returns valid true after section-shape checks even when overall blocked. operable means not blocked; ready and certification_ready mean all eight states healthy. CLI defaults operable and exits 2 when unmet; --require syntax can succeed on blocked report.
note: 05 Findings/D1033 Doctor validity and operational readiness are separate.md

title: Doctor composer trusts supplied section states
body: Exact section-key set, known state, remediation mapping and px:// prefix are checked. It does not authenticate evidence, verify full section schema or validate evaluation timestamp. Public composer intentionally supports fixtures; certification_ready remains a derived diagnostic label.
note: 05 Findings/D1034 Doctor composer trusts supplied section states.md

title: Doctor Git budget follows full subprocess capture
body: Git commands use five-second direct timeouts and capture entire output before byte checks. Status excludes untracked then separately counts nonignored untracked files. No ignored-file inventory, process-tree cleanup, aggregate deadline or environment scrub is provided by this helper.
note: 05 Findings/D1035 Doctor Git budget follows full subprocess capture.md

title: Doctor local JSON size check precedes separate read
body: is_file/stat byte cap precedes read_text, leaving a change window; symlink/ancestor identity is not checked. Returned fields such as snapshot_hash/phase may retain arbitrary values even though secret_values_retained is fixed false. This is projection policy, not value scanning.
note: 05 Findings/D1036 Doctor local JSON size check precedes separate read.md

title: Near-future Doctor evidence can be healthy but fresh false
body: Age between minus300 and zero seconds sets fresh false but adds no problem; section state uses problems only. More than five minutes future adds clock skew. A caller comparing fresh flag and section state can therefore observe disagreement.
note: 05 Findings/D1037 Near-future Doctor evidence can be healthy but fresh false.md

title: Doctor handoff freshness compares declared hashes
body: Old handoff age is removed as problem when its verified_state_hash equals nonempty coordination state_hash. Neither hash is recomputed or authenticated. Absent coordination state leaves no current-state proof, and weak string checks accept empty handoff hash when no state comparison applies.
note: 05 Findings/D1038 Doctor handoff freshness compares declared hashes.md

title: Doctor provider readiness does not pair budget and adapter
body: Healthy requires some admitted ready adapter, some enabled budget and no scan violations. It does not match budget provider/model/scope to a ready adapter or check remaining allowance/live connectivity. Counters report declaration availability.
note: 05 Findings/D1039 Doctor provider readiness does not pair budget and adapter.md

title: Doctor integrity consumes booleans as well as errors
body: Unlike structural error-list-only aggregation, integrity requires every selected check valid. It also checks current sections and three named release groups. Exceptions are normalized for selected operations; this remains bounded control-plane status rather than certification.
note: 05 Findings/D1040 Doctor integrity consumes booleans as well as errors.md

title: Doctor transaction coverage is a fixed existing-root list
body: Only operations/provider-budget/resource-lifecycle/coordination/diagnostics WAL directories are configured when present. Other owners are outside this list; recovery uses apply false. No discovered roots degrades even if remaining recovery checks healthy.
note: 05 Findings/D1041 Doctor transaction coverage is a fixed existing-root list.md

title: Doctor extension claim selection and clocks are asymmetric
body: First extension.activity-projection claim is assessed; later matching claims are ignored. Assessment uses health owner default clock, while supplied evaluated_at is passed to environment/handoff and report. max_age_seconds routes to coverage only; environment defaults one day.
note: 05 Findings/D1042 Doctor extension claim selection and clocks are asymmetric.md

title: Doctor coverage wording can differ from blocked registry state
body: Coverage section state blocks if route registry or reconciliation invalid, but human summary selects all-routes-current text solely from report.certifiable. Inconsistent delegated flags can therefore produce reassuring summary inside blocked section.
note: 05 Findings/D1043 Doctor coverage wording can differ from blocked registry state.md

title: Doctor report retention does not validate incoming report seal
body: Retention accepts report_sha256 string of length64, without hex syntax, recomputation or full report schema verification. It embeds supplied report and seals new receipt; a valid receipt can preserve a caller-supplied inconsistent report. Path/transaction safety remains delegated to JSON WAL.
note: 05 Findings/D1044 Doctor report retention does not validate incoming report seal.md

title: Doctor digest covers base report before later fields
body: run_px_doctor appends diagnostic_receipt after compose hashes report; CLI then appends requested_contract and contract_satisfied. Hashing the entire returned object minus report_sha256 will differ from base digest. Retained nested report captures original base before those additions.
note: 05 Findings/D1045 Doctor digest covers base report before later fields.md

title: Doctor receipt identity is digest-named rather than authenticated immutability
body: Receipt target uses report hash and transaction ID uses first24 characters. Existing path immutability/idempotence relies on WAL behavior; helper has no existing-receipt equivalence check. Returned byte digest is a separate read after commit, not signed provenance.
note: 05 Findings/D1046 Doctor receipt identity is digest-named rather than authenticated immutability.md

title: Doctor tests measure five WAL roots rather than every effect
body: Live test compares snapshots of five known WAL roots and checks section fields. It does not inventory all filesystem/process/network effects. Freshness fixtures use arbitrary matching hash strings; receipt test starts from valid composer output rather than tampered reports.
note: 05 Findings/D1047 Doctor tests measure five WAL roots rather than every effect.md

title: Doctor CLI tests intentionally distinguish syntax from operability
body: Selected CLI test supplies blocked report and expects default exit2 but syntax exit0. Lazy-loading subprocess test likewise asks syntax while simulating two unrelated import failures. These do not establish healthy/ready installed system.
note: 05 Findings/D1048 Doctor CLI tests intentionally distinguish syntax from operability.md

title: Doctor execution has no aggregate diagnostic deadline
body: Serial validators/recovery/Git/health collection can perform substantial work before compose. Only selected local probes catch failures or use direct subprocess timeouts; an exception in unwrapped coverage/runtime/health/recovery can prevent any final report.
note: 05 Findings/D1049 Doctor execution has no aggregate diagnostic deadline.md

title: Manifest expansion models a subset of build declarations
body: Supports include/exclude and recursive-include/exclude, collecting exclusions independently of directive order. Wheel source packages use longest declared package-dir prefix; data-file target uses source basename. This is a custom projection model, not complete setuptools interpretation.
note: 05 Findings/D1050 Manifest expansion models a subset of build declarations.md

title: Projection source paths have uneven link checks
body: Python package glob reads source without explicit symlink rejection; package/data/license branches differ. Resolving source paths can hide ancestor aliases, while bytes and size are read separately. No aggregate file/byte budget or locked source snapshot is established by generator.
note: 05 Findings/D1051 Projection source paths have uneven link checks.md

title: Projection collision checks miss same-source duplicate and case aliases
body: Collision key is exact package target/installed path and errors only when prior source differs. Repeated record for same source/path survives; case-only installed-path collisions remain distinct. Later expected dictionary can collapse exact duplicate paths.
note: 05 Findings/D1052 Projection collision checks miss same-source duplicate and case aliases.md

title: Source-only skill policy also skips sdist requirement
body: For allowed source-only skill file, helper rejects wheel projection then continues before sdist checks. Thus source-only path may be omitted from sdist while skill projection remains valid. Unknown projected skill paths not present in enumerated source are not separately rejected.
note: 05 Findings/D1053 Source-only skill policy also skips sdist requirement.md

title: Frozen artifact manifest validation is shallow
body: Record validation requires keys and package target but not path safety, field types, required/generated booleans, digest grammar, byte-size values or unique records. Empty record list and arbitrary skill_projection mapping can pass with valid flags and correct self-digest.
note: 05 Findings/D1054 Frozen artifact manifest validation is shallow.md

title: Manifest self-digest is consistency rather than authenticity
body: Digest excludes errors/valid/digest fields; validator separately checks generation errors/valid. A coherent rewritten manifest can be resealed. Higher release certificate owner binds expected manifest digest; direct intrinsic checker does not authenticate author or source.
note: 05 Findings/D1055 Manifest self-digest is consistency rather than authenticity.md

title: Built-artifact checker does not invoke intrinsic manifest validation
body: verify_built_artifact trusts supplied record/allowed-generated mappings, checks required only when exactly True and compares hashes for present records. It ignores manifest.valid and source sizes. bind_artifact_set adds intrinsic validation when manifest supplied; direct verifier is weaker.
note: 05 Findings/D1056 Built-artifact checker does not invoke intrinsic manifest validation.md

title: Generated archive members are allowed by path rather than semantic contents
body: Expected generated metadata paths can appear without matching source bytes; wildcard policy permits matching extras. Inspector only obtains metadata Version, not package Name, wheel tags, entrypoint correctness or RECORD hash closure. This requires higher-level checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1057 Generated archive members are allowed by path rather than semantic contents.md

title: Archive inspectors have format and resource limits
body: Wheel reads every file payload and sdist materializes member list then reads payloads with no aggregate/member/decompression cap. Duplicate names are detected, but case/normalized aliases are not. Tar links rejected; ZIP Unix link mode is not checked. Other nonfile tar entries are ignored.
note: 05 Findings/D1058 Archive inspectors have format and resource limits.md

title: Archive metadata version can come from multiple matching members
body: Every matching dist-info/METADATA or PKG-INFO updates version; no exact-one metadata check. Last matching member wins. Version existence is checked, but archive package identity is not bound to filename/project metadata by inspector.
note: 05 Findings/D1059 Archive metadata version can come from multiple matching members.md

title: Build once is local invocation accounting
body: Helper checks output directory empty then calls backend once; no exclusive reservation or campaign claim occurs inside it. Concurrent calls or later new output directories are not globally prevented. Caller release campaign provides ordered ownership separately.
note: 05 Findings/D1060 Build once is local invocation accounting.md

title: Build helper can succeed without projection manifest
body: If pyproject or MANIFEST.in absent, manifest generation/verification is skipped. A successful runner producing exactly one wheel/sdist can return valid with null manifest; synthetic once-build test uses this path. Actual certification staged source supplies declarations.
note: 05 Findings/D1061 Build helper can succeed without projection manifest.md

title: Build snapshots are collected after backend execution
body: Artifact file hashes and source manifest are read after build, then archive inspection rereads artifacts. No immutable source/artifact handles span these steps. Extra unrelated files in output do not affect one-wheel/one-sdist count. Backend failure can still proceed through verification/custody handling.
note: 05 Findings/D1062 Build snapshots are collected after backend execution.md

title: Intermediate custody does not verify moved bytes afterward
body: Pre-move inventory checks links and hashes files, then each directory moves independently to supplied custody. Existing destinations cause partial movement/errors; no group rollback or post-move equality check. Receipt writes normally afterward. This dependency was inspected only; quarantine cleanup remains skipped.
note: 05 Findings/D1063 Intermediate custody does not verify moved bytes afterward.md

title: Artifact record verification checks provided records only
body: Verifies portable basename uniqueness, selected file/hash/size equality, but permits empty record list, arbitrary type labels and extra unlisted directory files. Type is copied from supplied record into actual result, so this check does not infer file format.
note: 05 Findings/D1064 Artifact record verification checks provided records only.md

title: Artifact binding requires presence rather than exactly one of each type
body: Binding uses next wheel and next sdist; despite error wording it does not reject additional same-type records with different names. All supplied records receive byte checks, but only first wheel/sdist receive version/projection inspection.
note: 05 Findings/D1065 Artifact binding requires presence rather than exactly one of each type.md

title: Record errors do not prevent subsequent archive access
body: After verify_artifact_records returns errors, bind still opens first wheel/sdist paths from supplied records. Invalid filename, missing file or malformed archive can cause further reads or exceptions rather than a clean early refusal. No effect executed in audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1066 Record errors do not prevent subsequent archive access.md

title: Manifest-free artifact binding does not prove source snapshot
body: Without source_root or frozen manifest, binding checks supplied bytes and metadata versions then echoes source_product_digest. Same-source test uses arbitrary a-times64 digest. Certification callers pass current source or frozen manifest, adding stronger projection checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1067 Manifest-free artifact binding does not prove source snapshot.md

title: Wheel installation uses before and after hashes around separate pip read
body: Wheel path is resolved and hashed, pip later reads it, then helper hashes again. Byte replacement and restoration during that window is not detected by endpoint hashes. No immutable copy/handle binds exact installed bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1068 Wheel installation uses before and after hashes around separate pip read.md

title: Install result does not verify installed package bytes
body: EnvBuilder may reuse existing environment; pip no-deps/no-index can report success without fresh replacement of an already installed same version. Helper checks process exit and wheel endpoints, not installed RECORD/files/import origin. Environment creation uses current process interpreter and occurs outside runner timeout.
note: 05 Findings/D1069 Install result does not verify installed package bytes.md

title: Distribution tests combine real builds with mocked installs
body: Module fixture truly builds copied source for manifest omission/extra/member tests if executed. Exact install test uses fake wheel bytes and mocked venv/pip runner, proving argv/env/hash handling rather than successful package installation. No product tests were run by this audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1070 Distribution tests combine real builds with mocked installs.md

title: Frozen-manifest tests preserve intended historical binding
body: Test modifies live completion state after build, verifies live manifest changes, and validates old archive against original frozen manifest. Separate tests reject simple manifest tampering and simultaneous source/frozen authority. This is meaningful snapshot-projection coverage, not proof against coherently resealed claims.
note: 05 Findings/D1071 Frozen-manifest tests preserve intended historical binding.md

title: Installed test can build unless certified wheel variable is supplied
body: Certified-wheel branch checks supplied hash and no-build flag. If wheel variable absent, test builds regardless of no-build flag. Test-local install uses --no-deps without explicit --no-index and inherits environment; higher owner may supply offline configuration.
note: 05 Findings/D1072 Installed test can build unless certified wheel variable is supplied.md

title: Installed scenario covers selected commissioning and memory flows
body: Runs installed validation/helper certification, preserves existing AGENTS bytes, creates/discovers/activates workspace projects, promotes/corrects memory and checks corrected visibility plus foreign-project denial. These concrete checks exceed pure metadata tests, but memory evidence strings and health metrics are fixtures.
note: 05 Findings/D1073 Installed scenario covers selected commissioning and memory flows.md

title: Installed parallel sessions are sequential actions
body: Second project/session activates after earlier commands, then count two is asserted and session released/switched. No simultaneous process race or concurrent writes are exercised. Per-command waits exist, but no single aggregate test deadline or process-tree ownership is shown.
note: 05 Findings/D1074 Installed parallel sessions are sequential actions.md

title: Installed Doctor check proves syntax only
body: Installed test invokes doctor --require syntax and checks valid. It does not require operable/ready, verify extension host health or certify all external services. Installed CLI bytes/import origin are not separately attested by this test.
note: 05 Findings/D1075 Installed Doctor check proves syntax only.md

title: Source limit is defined on an unused export helper
body: The 128MiB limit is enforced by _snapshot, which actual create_clean_export does not call. Actual materialization copies then hashes staged files without that aggregate limit. _snapshot also reads source twice, so its two digest fields would not be an atomic snapshot even if used.
note: 05 Findings/D1076 Source limit is defined on an unused export helper.md

title: Clean export selection preserves only selected custody state
body: Shared repository scope plus local filters exclude environments/builds/evidence and most bootstrap state, while retaining selected project/commissioning/test receipt paths. File symlinks are skipped; resolving root/ancestor aliases is not equivalent to rejecting them. Selection does not establish source stability.
note: 05 Findings/D1077 Clean export selection preserves only selected custody state.md

title: Export preflight checks stage after candidate work
body: Package processing-stage check lives in _preflight, invoked after candidate materialization and optional projection/test operations. It is not an admission before all export effects. Separate release-stage owner run() checks exact campaign phase before using rebuild directly.
note: 05 Findings/D1078 Export preflight checks stage after candidate work.md

title: Cross-platform export condition is a digest-cardinality check
body: Preflight accepts at most one distinct artifact digest, including zero artifacts. This is not observed equivalent behavior across operating systems. Stored completion is compared with fresh completion, while detailed component errors collapse to named check validity.
note: 05 Findings/D1079 Cross-platform export condition is a digest-cardinality check.md

title: Rebuild includes executable helper certification
body: Projection rebuild does not merely format JSON: it runs exact-tool certification then writes Python ownership and other projections. Subsequent writes proceed in sequence, with engine identity near end and classification checks afterward. Failures leave earlier staged mutations; lock release does not roll them back.
note: 05 Findings/D1080 Rebuild includes executable helper certification.md

title: Rebuild static inventory helper is intentionally rootless
body: build_inventory() supplies declared count-computation records and does not inspect a source root. Calling it without root in candidate rebuild is not by itself a live-root leakage defect. Other builders explicitly receive candidate root.
note: 05 Findings/D1081 Rebuild static inventory helper is intentionally rootless.md

title: Export command success is process exit rather than structured verdict
body: _run_command inherits ambient environment while adding no-bytecode/no-user-site/PYTHONPATH, captures complete stdout/stderr, and checks returncode. It does not parse a JSON valid field or use ProcessSupervisor tree/capture accounting. Each timeout is separate.
note: 05 Findings/D1082 Export command success is process exit rather than structured verdict.md

title: Candidate check order has no encompassing rollback or deadline
body: Certification runs stale sections, requires current section status, runs stale groups, then one full profile and validation before publishing evidence/completion. These commands have separate deadlines and mutate staged evidence; no total transaction/deadline restores previous candidate on later failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1083 Candidate check order has no encompassing rollback or deadline.md

title: Git provenance samples independent mutable observations
body: HEAD, commit time and porcelain status are separate subprocess reads. Empty successful status is converted to None, causing clean state to become unknown rather than false. Revision/mtime/provenance are not bound by one tree snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1084 Git provenance samples independent mutable observations.md

title: Frozen records exclude the export manifest itself
body: _candidate_records excludes every file whose basename is AUDIT_EXPORT_MANIFEST.json, along with links. Equality therefore cannot detect changes to those bytes or link/directory state. The ZIP still includes the manifest. Tests cover added pyc but not manifest mutation.
note: 05 Findings/D1085 Frozen records exclude the export manifest itself.md

title: Staging overwrites reserved output names without a source reservation check
body: Materialization writes audit README, SHA256SUMS, replay contract and manifest into copied tree. Optional VSIX artifact names are checked for case-insensitive uniqueness and extension, but archive format and aggregate payload size are not validated there. Copies and hashes occur at separate times.
note: 05 Findings/D1086 Staging overwrites reserved output names without a source reservation check.md

title: Deterministic ZIP metadata does not freeze concurrent bytes
body: Archive writer fixes timestamps and derives executable mode from shebang, sorting files case-insensitively. It rereads bytes after equality check; there is no immutable file handle spanning freeze and archive. Actual filesystem permission/empty directory differences are not preserved.
note: 05 Findings/D1087 Deterministic ZIP metadata does not freeze concurrent bytes.md

title: Uncertified export receipts use skipped-valid checks
body: Library can auto-detect certification mode, while CLI defaults to requiring it unless allow-uncertified. Skipped candidate/replay preflight values are valid true. Manifest explicitly refuses certification claim and filenames containing certified are rejected, even when that substring appears in uncertified.
note: 05 Findings/D1088 Uncertified export receipts use skipped-valid checks.md

title: Resource registration failures can precede export finally
body: Workspace and both prepared file records are registered before try begins. A later registration error can leave earlier owned resource unreconciled by this function. Resource ledger is written under original source root although candidate work occurs in stage.
note: 05 Findings/D1089 Resource registration failures can precede export finally.md

title: Replay checks a self-produced archive rather than independent acceptance
body: Certified branch extracts prepared ZIP, compares selected records, and reruns preflight. This is useful transport replay but shares implementation/inputs with producer. Prepared archive can change between writes/reads; no external signature or independent verifier authority is established here.
note: 05 Findings/D1090 Replay checks a self-produced archive rather than independent acceptance.md

title: Archive and receipt publication can be partial
body: Archive is replaced/promoted before receipt construction and replacement. A later sidecar failure leaves published archive without completed pair. Initial existence checks are not exclusive reservations, so concurrent publication may be overwritten by os.replace. No pair rollback or fsync boundary is shown.
note: 05 Findings/D1091 Archive and receipt publication can be partial.md

title: Export cleanup does not gate successful return
body: Finally catches selected reclaim exceptions and ignores reclaim result validity. Completion state is marked before cleanup, allowing apparent success with incomplete reclamation. A failure during failure-marking can also mask original error. hard_delete false in summary does not mean owned temporary cleanup was absent.
note: 05 Findings/D1092 Export cleanup does not gate successful return.md

title: Returned archive hash is another later read
body: Sidecar binds hash read after publication; returned summary rereads archive afterward. Concurrent replacement can make returned hash differ from receipt without a final equality check. No final sidecar readback is performed.
note: 05 Findings/D1093 Returned archive hash is another later read.md

title: Clean export tests do not run the full certified export sequence
body: Tiny uncertified fixtures check deterministic bytes, modes, CRLF, preserved custody and exclusions. Preflight is patched all-valid and candidate command runner is mocked. POSIX extraction test has platform gating and external subprocesses without timeout. No archive/sidecar failure, manifest mutation or size cap test.
note: 05 Findings/D1094 Clean export tests do not run the full certified export sequence.md

title: Git worktree attributes are distinct from working-tree contents
body: Archive command uses selected revision, default HEAD. --worktree-attributes controls attribute interpretation but does not include dirty/untracked source bytes. Report keeps revision string without resolving commit or retaining archive SHA256.
note: 05 Findings/D1095 Git worktree attributes are distinct from working-tree contents.md

title: Tar membership checks ignore nonregular entries
body: Inspector skips links/directories/special entries and checks only limited case-sensitive forbidden prefixes plus four required regular names. It does not reject duplicate names, traversal/normalized aliases or malicious link targets. No extraction occurs in auditor, so these are proof limits rather than an extraction exploit claim.
note: 05 Findings/D1096 Tar membership checks ignore nonregular entries.md

title: Tar size checks do not establish content authenticity
body: Physical tar cap and declared regular-byte cap bound size, but file content is not hashed or semantically checked. No member-count cap is applied, and declared byte sum is checked after member traversal. Required-name existence can be satisfied with arbitrary bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1097 Tar size checks do not establish content authenticity.md

title: Owned Git process requires actual tree closure
body: ProcessSupervisor applies startup/idle/total limits, grace/force shutdown and 64KiB captures. Result requires exited/zero and tree_closed, then archive existence. Dropped stderr is recorded but not invalidating. This is stronger lifecycle evidence than bare subprocess exit.
note: 05 Findings/D1098 Owned Git process requires actual tree closure.md

title: Archive workspace cleanup affects final validity
body: Auditor reclaims in finally and marks result invalid unless exactly one resource reclaimed without errors. Registration occurs before try and cleanup exceptions can mask earlier errors. No archive payload survives cleanup, while process receipt is retained through manager.
note: 05 Findings/D1099 Archive workspace cleanup affects final validity.md

title: Git archive tests exercise real supervised synthetic children
body: Tests run a tiny Python tar creator, a timeout sleeper and 200000-byte stderr writer, asserting closed process tree and reclaimed workspace. These are meaningful lifecycle checks when executed, but do not exercise actual Git revision/attributes or forbidden member policies. Source-name assertions are structural only.
note: 05 Findings/D1100 Git archive tests exercise real supervised synthetic children.md

title: Git revision and custom command interfaces assume trusted callers
body: Revision is appended as a raw argv item without separator or revision resolution; option-like values may be interpreted by Git. Custom command_builder can return an arbitrary fixture command. Timeout check only requires positive value; caller still owns authorization and acceptable bounds.
note: 05 Findings/D1101 Git revision and custom command interfaces assume trusted callers.md

title: Contract ownership can preserve prior declarations
body: Unknown contract paths fall back to existing ownership records, preserving owner/producers/enforcement/tests without independently deriving them. generated_artifacts compares to build(root), which rereads that same registry. Coherent changes in fallback metadata can therefore regenerate consistently; corpus consumer separately checks declared files/schema.
note: 05 Findings/D1102 Contract ownership can preserve prior declarations.md

title: Contract routing tables classify rather than prove enforcement
body: Directory basename and schema filename select tables; some directories use generic owners, others index known names and raise on unknown. Builder stamps version 1.0.0, packaged true and universal runtime/contracts.py consumer. It reads schema ID/title without establishing actual owner call coverage or test success.
note: 05 Findings/D1103 Contract routing tables classify rather than prove enforcement.md

title: Contract corpus consumer adds limited independent checks
body: Corpus auditor validates schema structure/IDs/references and generated positive/empty negative fixtures, verifies ownership file paths, nonempty enforcement and labels. It does not execute every listed producer/test or demonstrate claimed runtime enforcement merely from ownership registry.
note: 05 Findings/D1104 Contract corpus consumer adds limited independent checks.md

title: Count inventory is a static declaration set
body: build_inventory returns an explicit table, not filesystem-discovered completeness. It handles varied count rules and assigns fallback builder label to undeclared producer paths. Runtime consumer independently discovers count fields and checks rule results, while metadata fields are tested for nonemptiness rather than actual producer execution.
note: 05 Findings/D1105 Count inventory is a static declaration set.md

title: Count inventory check is canonical text equality
body: CLI renders static table and compares read_text, which normalizes newline differences. It reports valid true after successful write/check; actual count values are validated only by runtime envelope consumer, not this script.
note: 05 Findings/D1106 Count inventory check is canonical text equality.md

title: Proof matrix binds inventory bytes rather than probes
body: Matrix records SHA256 of input JSON and canonical plan plus explicit authority that no probe ran. Source references and declared action_count are copied; underlying source bytes and operation outcomes are not verified by builder.
note: 05 Findings/D1107 Proof matrix binds inventory bytes rather than probes.md

title: Proof matrix denominator check is aggregate
body: Control IDs must be unique and total count equal sum of expected surface counts. It does not compare each surface count, so offsetting per-surface discrepancies can pass. Duplicate action keys collapse in dictionary, and action_count is not checked against its list length here.
note: 05 Findings/D1108 Proof matrix denominator check is aggregate.md

title: Action policy comes from mode and effect labels
body: Action chosen from first label token or dynamicRepair second token. Navigate and sidebar controls can receive synthetic contracts; sidebar host-ui-or-read is outside nonmutating allowlist and thus marked disposable/restart. Mode other than exact host is treated as UI for these decisions. No schema validation precedes interpretation.
note: 05 Findings/D1109 Action policy comes from mode and effect labels.md

title: Indicator roles are inferred from words
body: Failure tokens take priority over progress then empty tokens; camel-case splitting and specific phrases determine state. Semantic meaning, negation and actual reachable UI state are not independently derived. All requirement variants mark real external authority false.
note: 05 Findings/D1110 Indicator roles are inferred from words.md

title: Restart flags and stage requirements are separate tables
body: Editor configuration sets requires_restart true, but persistence/reload_reopen stages are not required by the later kind set. Consumers that only use stage_policy can have different obligations from consumers using restart flag. This is a declaration inconsistency to account for, not evidence a restart happened.
note: 05 Findings/D1111 Restart flags and stage requirements are separate tables.md

title: Selected installed branch infers three stages from acknowledgement
body: For contained_host_interaction with attempted and acknowledged probe, required authorization/backend_dispatch/runtime_effect stages are set present with the same receipt reference. Response/live-view change supports an observation, but does not independently expose each internal stage. Whole large operational walk remains under review.
note: 05 Findings/D1112 Selected installed branch infers three stages from acknowledgement.md

title: Proof matrix tests establish metadata consistency
body: Tests compare build output with stored matrix, check unique aggregate counts/stage vocabulary, source-name presence and four indicator labels. They do not execute controls or test malformed action entries, offset surface counts or restart-stage inconsistency.
note: 05 Findings/D1113 Proof matrix tests establish metadata consistency.md

title: Current evidence index apply publishes before validity return
body: CLI calls publish_index then returns 0/2 according to value.valid. Core publisher writes both locations regardless of validity using separate prepared replacements. One target can update before failure of second; CLI invalid result does not undo publication.
note: 05 Findings/D1114 Current evidence index apply publishes before validity return.md

title: Thin projection wrappers have different success meanings
body: Effect and historical writers print valid true after write; graph core writer returns valid true; test-group and engine wrappers return zero without a validator. Provider-route writer returns nested report validity only after writing scan. These results are not interchangeable validation receipts.
note: 05 Findings/D1115 Thin projection wrappers have different success meanings.md

title: Graph writer leaves stale extra artifacts in place
body: Core writer creates output and writes expected files, without removing preexisting extras or post-write validation. Separate validate_graph_artifacts requires exact JSON file set and expected bytes. Wrapper success can therefore precede a later stale-extra failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1116 Graph writer leaves stale extra artifacts in place.md

title: Writer root options select data rather than imported code
body: Thin wrappers prepend their own repository path for imports, then some pass caller-selected root to core builder. Others pin both data and implementation to script ROOT. This is an important portable/candidate invocation distinction, not an execution sandbox.
note: 05 Findings/D1117 Writer root options select data rather than imported code.md

title: Agency output can fail reporting after an outside-root write
body: Wrapper accepts absolute --output and writes it, then output.relative_to(root) for JSON summary raises if outside root. There is no pre-write containment check. Check-only mode can also fail at summary. No such operation was executed here.
note: 05 Findings/D1118 Agency output can fail reporting after an outside-root write.md

title: Historical locator publication does not retrieve historical bytes
body: Writer records dispositions discovered within PRODUCT_STRUCTURED_ROOTS and prints valid true. It does not dereference nonportable locators or establish evidence authenticity; generated gate only compares freshly discovered record list.
note: 05 Findings/D1119 Historical locator publication does not retrieve historical bytes.md

title: Profile apply reports success while extra profiles remain
body: Profile reconciler detects projected names absent from owners, but does not remove them. Apply result is always true after writes, even with extras; check mode rejects them. Missing source/projection directories can yield empty successful result because glob returns no names.
note: 05 Findings/D1120 Profile apply reports success while extra profiles remain.md

title: Byte projection fixed denominators do not inspect all extras
body: Wrapper reconciler checks seven hardcoded destinations; suite template reconciler checks 3 by 7 paths. Neither discovers unexpected additional copies nor validates Python/JSON semantics. Each records pre-write stale list and returns true in apply mode after sequential normal writes.
note: 05 Findings/D1121 Byte projection fixed denominators do not inspect all extras.md

title: Projection writes have separate path and publication limits
body: Profile/domain/suite helpers follow ordinary file operations with no explicit symlink/ancestor containment guard, predecessor comparison or group rollback. Suite helper does not create missing parents. A failure leaves earlier writes intact; no final readback proves exact published bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1122 Projection writes have separate path and publication limits.md

title: Active hash apply intentionally retains pre-write invalid result
body: Active helper returns valid not stale after computing stale before writes. First successful repair may return false; dedicated test asserts false on apply then true on check. Export ignores the return and later derives other projections, so false there is not automatically write failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1123 Active hash apply intentionally retains pre-write invalid result.md

title: Active hash map allows collapsed contracts and trusted paths
body: Paths from map are joined without relative containment or symlink checks. Multiple active entries targeting same contract overwrite output dictionary; active_count counts distinct outputs, not entries. Empty active list passes. Rehashing current bytes does not itself prove those bytes admitted or behavior verified.
note: 05 Findings/D1124 Active hash map allows collapsed contracts and trusted paths.md

title: Active contract replacement is atomic per file only
body: All outputs calculated before mutation, then unique prepared names replace each file, even unchanged outputs. No compare-against-predecessor or group transaction; implementation may change between hashing and later use, and concurrent contract edits can be overwritten.
note: 05 Findings/D1125 Active contract replacement is atomic per file only.md

title: Declared owner reconciliation assigns verification labels without tests
body: Exact_authoritative_recovery state triggers authoritative_implementation_verified, supplied_and_revalidated and authoritative labels while helper only hashes SKILL.md. These metadata assignments must not be interpreted as a freshly executed verification receipt.
note: 05 Findings/D1126 Declared owner reconciliation assigns verification labels without tests.md

title: Owner hash reconciliation gates group write on missing bodies
body: Any missing owner body prevents writing all in-memory changes. Check mode detects label/hash drift; apply writes one normal JSON file if changed and no errors. Owner path/source identities have no containment/uniqueness proof here and no final readback.
note: 05 Findings/D1127 Owner hash reconciliation gates group write on missing bodies.md

title: Declared tool reconciliation maintains a three-level hash chain
body: Target bytes update registry source_sha256 and reference authoritative_source_sha256; newly rendered reference bytes determine owner scripts-index sha256. This establishes computed consistency at read time, not admissibility or behavioral success of changed code.
note: 05 Findings/D1128 Declared tool reconciliation maintains a three-level hash chain.md

title: Tool hash reconciliation assumes valid layout and IDs
body: Owner derived from target path third component, IDs interpolated into reference path, and existing index records selected by ID. No containment/schema/duplicate validation is performed; duplicate IDs/maps can collapse and malformed shapes raise. CLI writes outputs sequentially without rollback/readback.
note: 05 Findings/D1129 Tool hash reconciliation assumes valid layout and IDs.md

title: Rebuild order binds copied owners before derived discovery
body: Export invokes wrappers, templates, profiles, skills, active hashes and tool hash outputs before semantic/cognitive/agent graph rebuilding. This causal order is explicit. It does not call declared-owner hash reconciler in the inspected sequence; that remains a separate entrypoint.
note: 05 Findings/D1130 Rebuild order binds copied owners before derived discovery.md

title: Recovery tests prove declared metadata and routing reachability
body: Test checks fixed 260 identity count, active owner hashes, metadata freshness labels, evidence/test file presence and top-three navigation inclusion. It does not run each recovered owner, verify referenced receipt contents or prove no body hydration by instrumenting reads.
note: 05 Findings/D1131 Recovery tests prove declared metadata and routing reachability.md

title: Byte stability test uses check mode only
body: Generated-artifact test snapshots templates before/after check=True calls, establishing check-mode nonmutation when current. It does not exercise actual generation followed by byte-identical regeneration. Separate wrapper fixture does detect one injected drift.
note: 05 Findings/D1132 Byte stability test uses check mode only.md

title: Engine identity wrapper delegates one-file replacement
body: Core writer prepares a PID-named file then replaces identity; CLI prints count/tree hash and returns zero without running validate_engine_identity. Concurrent same-process calls can share prepared name, and filtered identity scope/installed equivalence remain core consumer concerns.
note: 05 Findings/D1133 Engine identity wrapper delegates one-file replacement.md

title: Candidate queue merges by ID with uneven requirements
body: CSV duplicate skill IDs overwrite earlier rows. Manifest-only IDs start with candidate/defer but omit CSV required_before_promotion list. Multiple unsorted manifest glob entries may overwrite same fields. No duplicate/schema/digest validation establishes one authoritative source.
note: 05 Findings/D1134 Candidate queue merges by ID with uneven requirements.md

title: Manifest scalar extraction is not YAML semantics
body: Anchored regex reads matching key line from anywhere in manifest and strips quotes; comments, block scalars, nested structure and duplicate keys are not parsed as YAML. Priority sorting is lexical, so numeric-looking priority strings may not follow numerical order.
note: 05 Findings/D1135 Manifest scalar extraction is not YAML semantics.md

title: Specialty count deduplication differs from category rows
body: Every queue entry is appended, while represented IDs and top-level counts use sets. Duplicate IDs across rows/categories can remain visible while counts understate rows. Active/mapped state is catalog membership alone; loading_rule prose does not enforce admission or lazy reading.
note: 05 Findings/D1136 Specialty count deduplication differs from category rows.md

title: External promoted bundles bypass candidate regeneration
body: Bundles already active/admitted in skill catalog are omitted from generated deferred manifests. One fixed active intake controller is always assigned; duplicate bundle IDs collapse and an ID collision with controller is overwritten. Promotion status is trusted from catalog, not independently authorized by this builder.
note: 05 Findings/D1137 External promoted bundles bypass candidate regeneration.md

title: External package freshness and validation counts are authored constants
body: Manifests stamp validation_freshness current and test source path as evidence; ledger sets failed zero/passed eight for active and deferred records. No tests run here. clean_room is a fixed active-control declaration or determined from source-license marker.
note: 05 Findings/D1138 External package freshness and validation counts are authored constants.md

title: External catalog marker can suppress reconciliation
body: Append decision searches raw TOML text for exact id marker. Existing entry with wrong body/status/version is not repaired; marker in comment can suppress missing entry. ID/version/body interpolation is not TOML-escaped except tags. Core registry later adds identity/status/file consistency checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1139 External catalog marker can suppress reconciliation.md

title: External reconciliation is a sequence of partial writes
body: Catalog rewrite occurs before package files, ledger and catalog additions. Later failure leaves prior changes. Trusted body/ID paths lack containment checks; source rereads can race, duplicate ledger IDs collapse when update occurs. Return valid reflects initial drift, while apply CLI exits zero despite false result.
note: 05 Findings/D1140 External reconciliation is a sequence of partial writes.md

title: Security archive pin does not bind companion pack
body: Builder hashes archive against fixed expected value, but reads catalog, graph, YAML, workflows and pack inventory from separate source files. It checks catalog/graph nonempty line counts before projection, not derivation from archive or a signed companion manifest.
note: 05 Findings/D1141 Security archive pin does not bind companion pack.md

title: Security source metadata is copied without comparing to verified archive
body: source.json archive hash/entry count/size come from source_archive.json rather than the already measured archive. A mismatch may publish successfully then fail runtime declared-hash check. Catalog hash is of original source JSONL, while published catalog is transformed/sorted JSON; digest scopes differ.
note: 05 Findings/D1142 Security source metadata is copied without comparing to verified archive.md

title: Security metadata count check is weaker than runtime validation
body: Builder line-count checks can accept duplicate IDs or malformed graph lines; graph is copied without parsing here. Runtime adds unique IDs, domains, risks and deferred-state checks; graph loading checks only edge count in inspected loader. Neither uses source catalog/graph hashes to authenticate projected payloads.
note: 05 Findings/D1143 Security metadata count check is weaker than runtime validation.md

title: Security source projections are unbounded separate reads
body: Archive hashing reads full file; catalog is counted, reread into full transformed bytes, hashed later and parsed again for candidate rows. YAML uses safe_load but without size/depth budget. No stable source snapshot or per-file/aggregate resource budget binds all steps.
note: 05 Findings/D1144 Security source projections are unbounded separate reads.md

title: Security provider publication keeps external scripts inert
body: Registration explicitly sets discovery enabled, execution disabled, provider_scripts_admitted zero and source_archive null/not bundled. Actual archive hydration is separate and verifies pinned bytes. Builder itself does not extract or execute provider scripts.
note: 05 Findings/D1145 Security provider publication keeps external scripts inert.md

title: Security operational schemas use local required-field definitions
body: Source YAML supplies contract name/purpose; local OPERATIONAL_CONTRACTS supplies actual required/properties and additionalProperties false. Constants such as approved, immutable, cleanup_verified or selected hashes valid describe accepted claims, not real authorization/evidence verification. Unknown names raise; missing source contract files are not independently counted here.
note: 05 Findings/D1146 Security operational schemas use local required-field definitions.md

title: Security golden queries are derived from domain declarations
body: Golden cases use each canonical domain name as query and expected domain, top_k ten. This is correlated vocabulary coverage rather than independent diverse evaluation. No golden-query execution occurs during generation.
note: 05 Findings/D1147 Security golden queries are derived from domain declarations.md

title: Security skill and workflow merging is recorded metadata
body: Native bodies provide frontmatter; workflows provide ID/output labels; each receives merge_into_existing and fixed owner. duplicate_active_skills_created zero is assigned. No implementation equivalence or execution is established by these records.
note: 05 Findings/D1148 Security skill and workflow merging is recorded metadata.md

title: Security admission publishes fixed test success
body: Active control manifest is current with fixed evidence path, and admission ledger records sixteen passed/zero failed. Builder does not run tests or validate cited receipt. Existing catalog text marker prevents field reconciliation; multiple normal writes can partially publish.
note: 05 Findings/D1149 Security admission publishes fixed test success.md

title: Security workflow binding admits a validator rather than executing operations
body: Binding mode executable_validator points to validate_security_orchestration. Workflow JSON is loaded from a .yaml-named file and copied into orchestration registry after removing version/loading_rule/bounds/scenarios. Source workflow execution and retained bounds are not proved by this projection.
note: 05 Findings/D1150 Security workflow binding admits a validator rather than executing operations.md

title: Security pack unaccounted zero is based on supplied rows
body: Every supplied pack manifest row gets a prefix-based owner/disposition, with fallback fragment_only. unaccounted_count is fixed zero; builder does not enumerate actual pack files, verify row hashes/sizes or compare missing/extra files. Merge label does not show target bytes received source behavior.
note: 05 Findings/D1151 Security pack unaccounted zero is based on supplied rows.md

title: Security apply result retains pre-write drift
body: _write_or_check records drift then performs normal writes; final valid is not drift. Apply CLI exits zero regardless of that false result. No final all-output comparison, group rollback or stale-extra removal closes publication.
note: 05 Findings/D1152 Security apply result retains pre-write drift.md

title: Health snapshot denominator is four fixed routes
