body: ROUTES is a hardcoded list and platform listener path chooses Windows otherwise Linux. All four receipt files must exist even if route is not active. Build does not enumerate current active tier routes; downstream coverage detects missing required route states.
note: 05 Findings/D1153 Health snapshot denominator is four fixed routes.md

title: Remote health is configuration readiness rather than live invocation
body: Remote route healthy requires any OpenAI adapter admitted true/status ready. Local route additionally needs Ollama adapter, enabled budget and any settled successful invocation without policy_overrun. No recent specific model/endpoint smoke is measured by builder; local adapter and budget files are not included in route receipt hash.
note: 05 Findings/D1154 Remote health is configuration readiness rather than live invocation.md

title: Environment health is a shallow declared shape
body: Healthy requires expected schema string, any string snapshot_hash and credential_values_persisted exactly false. Hash format/content, inventory status/age and actual credential handling are not verified here; malformed boundaries value can raise instead of returning unknown.
note: 05 Findings/D1155 Environment health is a shallow declared shape.md

title: Listener route health and canonical readiness differ
body: Route helper prefers top-level listener_health over host fallback and only requires healthy/coverage_complete. Canonical projection requires host listener plus engine connection, bus, closed-tree and unchanged-artifact flags and zero drops. Same receipt can therefore produce different results without contradiction in their distinct predicates.
note: 05 Findings/D1156 Listener route health and canonical readiness differ.md

title: Canonical extension facts trust supplied envelope labels
body: Configured/detected derive from truthy artifact name/VS Code version, authority from supplied flags, and finished time needs only nonempty text. Artifact hash, running host identity and process tree are not independently checked. int conversion of dropped_events accepts some coercions and can raise for malformed input; last_failure is always null.
note: 05 Findings/D1157 Canonical extension facts trust supplied envelope labels.md

title: Observation time fallback can follow filesystem rewrite time
body: Valid timezone-aware receipt times are preserved; malformed/naive/missing times fall back to file mtime. Rewriting or touching old evidence can thus advance fallback observation time. Builder does not reject future/stale timestamps; optional coverage enforces age/future bounds separately.
note: 05 Findings/D1158 Observation time fallback can follow filesystem rewrite time.md

title: Receipt payload and bound hash are separate reads
body: Build parses receipt text, derives health/time, then rereads bytes for SHA256. Concurrent replacement can bind hash of different payload from one interpreted. Optional health claims reread installed receipt again after writing snapshot, without cross-output equality.
note: 05 Findings/D1159 Receipt payload and bound hash are separate reads.md

title: Snapshot write success does not mean healthy or certifiable
body: CLI first writes snapshot and sets valid true even with unknown/unconfigured routes. Only optional coverage changes validity/certifiable fields; missing/malformed optional inputs can fail after initial write. Output paths can alias each other or input evidence, with no preflight collision check or transactional rollback.
note: 05 Findings/D1160 Snapshot write success does not mean healthy or certifiable.md

title: Coverage validates freshness and bytes without rederiving route semantics
body: For active tier A/B routes, consumer checks kind, healthy label, time window, contained receipt path and SHA256 equality. It does not rerun health producer or bind local auxiliary policy files in that branch. A hash-correct receipt supports byte identity but not every derived healthy claim.
note: 05 Findings/D1161 Coverage validates freshness and bytes without rederiving route semantics.md

title: Health tests cover helper transformations rather than full observation
body: Synthetic dictionaries prove selected listener/remote/environment labels, canonical facts and timestamp preservation. Installed receipt test checks nonzero size or skips. No full build/CLI/local branch or fresh live provider/host observation is exercised by this module.
note: 05 Findings/D1162 Health tests cover helper transformations rather than full observation.md

title: Control source binding covers matrix-referenced files only
body: Source manifest strips numeric/semantic anchors and hashes whole referenced files after resolved containment. It does not verify anchor existence, all repository code or current matrix/inventory bytes unless those happen to be source refs. Changed policy with unchanged referenced files can preserve source manifest equality.
note: 05 Findings/D1163 Control source binding covers matrix-referenced files only.md

title: Assembler trusts matrix metadata beyond a deduplicated count
body: Requirements dictionary length must equal control_count, but duplicate rows can collapse if declared count also collapsed. Matrix schema/self-digest and inventory-to-matrix equality are not checked. Test fixture deliberately has minimal matrix and empty inventory controls.
note: 05 Findings/D1164 Assembler trusts matrix metadata beyond a deduplicated count.md

title: Allowed direct evidence kind is a declaration
body: Assembler checks schema/kind allowlist and exact current source manifest. It does not authenticate producer, observed host, underlying artifact, timestamp or claimed measurement process. A permitted evidence_kind label alone does not establish direct observation.
note: 05 Findings/D1165 Allowed direct evidence kind is a declaration.md

title: Stage evidence references are rewritten without dereferencing
body: Present stage requires nonempty detail and evidence list with nonblank string representations. Values are replaced by indexed fragment pointers into input receipt; original targets are not opened or checked here. Arbitrary nonstring objects can stringify nonempty.
note: 05 Findings/D1166 Stage evidence references are rewritten without dereferencing.md

title: Assembler merges monotonic success across receipts
body: Flags OR across inputs; present stages overwrite earlier present details, while missing stages never remove prior presence. There is no common run/host/time identity or contradiction check. A complete chain may combine distinct observations with last-present precedence.
note: 05 Findings/D1167 Assembler merges monotonic success across receipts.md

title: Assembly timestamps are publication time
body: Every output control and aggregate observed_at is datetime.now rather than retained source observation time. Old source-compatible receipts can receive fresh assembly timestamps. No input evidence age or maximum skew is checked here.
note: 05 Findings/D1168 Assembly timestamps are publication time.md

title: Assembled inventory hash names a different digest scope
body: control_chains.inventory.path names operational_surface_inventory.json, while its sha256 is source manifest source_sha256, not inventory file SHA256. This field must be interpreted with that specific schema convention, not assumed to authenticate named inventory bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1169 Assembled inventory hash names a different digest scope.md

title: Assembler source and receipt identities use separate reads
body: Input receipts parsed before per-record receipt hashing; same file can be reread and hashed once for each control. Concurrent edits may bind different bytes, and large receipts amplify read cost. Source manifest is not rechecked after merge. Input root containment occurs after input load.
note: 05 Findings/D1170 Assembler source and receipt identities use separate reads.md

title: Exclusive evidence output prevents overwrite but not partial new file
body: All three CLIs resolve output below root and open with x. This refuses existing outputs, but JSON serialization/write failure can leave partial newly created file. No prepared replacement, fsync or final readback shown. Input paths are contained only late in some builders.
note: 05 Findings/D1171 Exclusive evidence output prevents overwrite but not partial new file.md

title: Installed smoke adapter checks retained bytes without inspecting VSIX contents
body: Artifact before/after SHA256 must match supplied file; file format and packaged-source-to-current-source equality are not examined. Engine identity is a separate receipt declaration matched to local identity and selected control files. A test uses arbitrary non-ZIP bytes and coherent fake tree hash.
note: 05 Findings/D1172 Installed smoke adapter checks retained bytes without inspecting VSIX contents.md

title: Installed smoke flags are not independent process proof
body: Adapter checks receipt engine connection/worker exit/tree closed and Studio/sidebar labels, many by truthiness. It does not authenticate receipt producer, age, full engine manifest self-digest or actual process records; bool exit_code false can compare equal to zero.
note: 05 Findings/D1173 Installed smoke flags are not independent process proof.md

title: Installed smoke maps one scenario into fixed stage sets
body: Agent/workflow success/admission/reopen labels populate persistence and reload controls on both Studio and list surfaces plus lifecycle stages. Sidebar counters populate six stages. Missing policy stages remain missing, but progress/authorization/dispatch/effect are inferred from summary labels rather than separate per-stage observations here.
note: 05 Findings/D1174 Installed smoke maps one scenario into fixed stage sets.md

title: Optional Skill save changes installed adapter denominator
body: Skill persistence record added only for created and content_bound true. Other fixed Studio/sidebar requirements can raise before any output. Expected maximum is twelve records, but missing Skill save can yield eleven; retained test expects twelve when adaptation succeeds.
note: 05 Findings/D1175 Optional Skill save changes installed adapter denominator.md

title: Installed adapter identity reads are not one snapshot
body: Receipt, VSIX, identity and control files are read at separate times; final receipt hash rereads after interpretation. No final identity revalidation binds all artifacts atomically. receipt/vsix relative_to(root) checks happen at output assembly after earlier reads.
note: 05 Findings/D1176 Installed adapter identity reads are not one snapshot.md

title: Owned probe adapter lets caller choose installed evidence label
body: Evidence kind allows direct_current_source_host_measurement or direct_installed_host_measurement, supplied by caller. It checks source/bridge/host-error declarations but no VSIX or installed host identity/process closure. Thus installed label has weaker binding than separate smoke adapter.
note: 05 Findings/D1177 Owned probe adapter lets caller choose installed evidence label.md

title: Optional profile counts need not prove full expected profile coverage
body: Absent profiles accepted; present profile requires schema and record length equal declared eligible count. No independent eligible-ID denominator, profile completion status or unique record check exists before duplicate merge. Matrix dictionary also collapses repeated IDs.
note: 05 Findings/D1178 Optional profile counts need not prove full expected profile coverage.md

title: Owned probe stages merge complementary claims into complete chain
body: Present beats missing; present/present combines detail/evidence; applicability conflict rejected. Duplicate controls across or within profiles are merged, without common run/target/correlation checks. Test explicitly combines setup missing failure and edit missing runtime into both stages present.
note: 05 Findings/D1179 Owned probe stages merge complementary claims into complete chain.md

title: Probe adapter does not resolve evidence strings
body: Present requires detail plus nonempty list, but no nonblank item/dereference/provenance check. Assembler later rejects blank-string items, adding a stronger shape check. Profile dictionary-valued evidence can also fail dedup hashing if duplicate stages combine; malformed fields can raise.
note: 05 Findings/D1180 Probe adapter does not resolve evidence strings.md

title: Adapter tests prove transformation with synthetic receipts
body: Host fixture uses fake artifact and engine digest; probe fixture authors verified/bridge/stage labels. Tests meaningfully reject stale source, endpoint mismatch, host errors and policy/count conflicts, but do not establish real installed operation. Retained host test may skip or accept a specific stale result.
note: 05 Findings/D1181 Adapter tests prove transformation with synthetic receipts.md

title: Assembler tests retain gaps but do not authenticate origins
body: Tests show incomplete control remains observed_only, one exact synthetic direct record completes it, and observed true can complete without attempted. They reject contextual kind, outside IDs and stale source, but not replayed timestamps, policy-only changes, conflicting runs or fabricated nonempty references.
note: 05 Findings/D1182 Assembler tests retain gaps but do not authenticate origins.md

title: Historical aliases can substitute different current artifacts
body: Resolver maps conversation aliases to retained report or whole ledger, one old JS path to Python implementation, and installed extension package locator to source package.json. This resolves a current representative, not necessarily original observed bytes. Installed package special branch returns relative Path before root normalization, depending on process cwd.
note: 05 Findings/D1183 Historical aliases can substitute different current artifacts.md

title: Historical token parsing chooses first resolvable file
body: Command regex extracts one whitespace-delimited script token; semicolon alternatives return first existing file. Numeric anchors/fragments stripped. File paths can be outside root; resolve hides leaf symlink before later is_symlink check, so physical-file wording does not reject all aliases.
note: 05 Findings/D1184 Historical token parsing chooses first resolvable file.md

title: Same-card later evidence need not correspond to original claim
body: Helper takes first hash/size-bearing evidence from history entries after first, regardless of target reference identity or relative chronology of target being attested. It does not read/verify correlated artifact. Same-card correlation can bind a different supporting event than original claim.
note: 05 Findings/D1185 Same-card later evidence need not correspond to original claim.md

title: Retained semantic alias proof is a card-ID substring
body: For selected semantic aliases, raw retained artifact must contain gap ID bytes. This is not structured claim matching, exact token boundary or authorization verification. Nonsemantic aliases skip this check. Hashing entire current ledger/report binds current bytes rather than original authority text.
note: 05 Findings/D1186 Retained semantic alias proof is a card-ID substring.md

title: Exact gap-event fallback hashes first matching raw event
body: If direct file missing, helper scans ledger lines, skips malformed JSON and hashes stripped text of first matching event ID. It does not independently validate event chain in that function or require matched event to support same card. Earlier snapshot validation is a separate read.
note: 05 Findings/D1187 Exact gap-event fallback hashes first matching raw event.md

title: Historical attestation completeness has narrow meaning
body: Skips evidence with any artifact_sha256 truthy or hash-looking reference prefix. check complete means no resolver failures, even when candidate attestations have not been appended. Both unresolved check/apply return zero; callers must inspect complete/unresolved fields.
note: 05 Findings/D1188 Historical attestation completeness has narrow meaning.md

title: Attestation append can partially complete across chunks
body: Candidates derive from one snapshot and current reads, then append in MAX_BATCH_EVENTS chunks. Duplicate/concurrent target change or later failure can leave earlier chunks committed. No final snapshot audit or retry reconciliation occurs in script. Ledger validates each batch under its own lock.
note: 05 Findings/D1189 Attestation append can partially complete across chunks.md

title: Ledger attestation validates binding shape rather than historical truth
body: Consumer requires existing card/target evidence, valid hash/size/nonempty method and no prior target attestation. It does not open artifact or constrain method to proof semantics in this branch. Attested target is removed from unbound denominator; no automatic behavioral proof follows.
note: 05 Findings/D1190 Ledger attestation validates binding shape rather than historical truth.md

title: Typed gap links bind fixed reviewed proposal bytes
body: Script pins exact proposal SHA256 before interpreting assignments; it does not rederive source trace against current files. Retired controls are skipped explicitly, existing gap sets preserved/unioned, and operational controls can be changed to gap. It reports zero operational claims.
note: 05 Findings/D1191 Typed gap links bind fixed reviewed proposal bytes.md

title: Typed proposal aggregate assertion is check-only
body: Expected proposal candidate count compared only inside --check branch. Apply defaults to effects and appends even without that total assertion. Known surfaces/control IDs checked, but duplicate proposal assignments can create conflicting predecessor revisions because all planned from same snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1192 Typed proposal aggregate assertion is check-only.md

title: Typed updater delegates meaningful predecessor validation to ledger
body: Revisions bind hash of existing disposition. Ledger rejects stale predecessor, unknown gap cards, empty gap targets, invalid transition and semantic no-op. Append prepares entire bounded batch before authoritative append under lock; multiple script chunks still lack one all-proposal transaction.
note: 05 Findings/D1193 Typed updater delegates meaningful predecessor validation to ledger.md

title: Typed proposal evidence is bound again at append time
body: Script hashes proposal before planning, while ledger _bind_evidence rereads referenced evidence during append preparation. If source proposal changes between reads, pinned planning bytes and retained event reference hash can differ; no script-side immediate equality recheck spans that gap.
note: 05 Findings/D1194 Typed proposal evidence is bound again at append time.md

title: Ledger event integrity is distinct from actor authentication
body: Reducer verifies sequence, predecessor and unkeyed canonical content hashes. Actor and authority are supplied strings; these checks establish internal consistency, not authenticated identity or independent truth of evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1195 Ledger event integrity is distinct from actor authentication.md

title: Replay and new append admission deliberately differ
body: New event preparation binds discovery actor/time, report physical manifest, work checkpoint predecessor/new-branch denominator and exclusive mutating owner. Historical replay retains weaker legacy envelopes so repair remains possible. A replay success alone does not prove every event satisfies current append policy.
note: 05 Findings/D1196 Replay and new append admission deliberately differ.md

title: Ordinary transition branch bypasses undeclared feature requirement
body: append_event delegates to append_events; eligible ordinary transitions use bulk preparation even for one event. Bulk reducer validates declared acceptance when present but does not set require_declared_feature_acceptance=True. An undeclared integrated card with complete chain can become operationally_verified. Pure memory probe confirmed strict branch rejects the same input and public dispatch branch accepts.
note: 05 Findings/D1197 Ordinary transition branch bypasses undeclared feature requirement.md

title: Feature acceptance regression fixture does not exercise absent declaration
body: The test named new operational transition requires declared acceptance begins with card() that already supplies requirements. It checks missing acceptance evidence and stale revision, leaving the undeclared-card bulk branch untested by that case.
note: 05 Findings/D1198 Feature acceptance regression fixture does not exercise absent declaration.md

title: Gap-switch invalidation can disappear from compact work history
body: Guard searches retained checkpoints newer than admission for another active gap. Projection retains only eight checkpoint details and keeps unclosed admissions indefinitely. After A to B to A and enough same-A checkpoints, original A session passes again. Pure memory replay agrees with incremental projection; no live session was switched.
note: 05 Findings/D1199 Gap-switch invalidation can disappear from compact work history.md

title: Guard omits permanent closed-admission hash index
body: Projection retains closed admission hashes for all history, but guard checks only recent closure rows. With nine concurrent read sessions, closing newest then eight older sessions drops newest closure detail while its recent admission remains. Pure memory guard first rejected then accepted that closed session although closed hash remained. Append-time exclusivity does consult the permanent index.
note: 05 Findings/D1200 Guard omits permanent closed-admission hash index.md

title: Existing work admission guard does not check current card closure
body: New admission requires known non-closed card. guard_work_admission checks active gap/session/effect/scope but never current card state. Pure memory example closes card while session remains unclosed and same checkpoint active; guard still accepts existing read admission. No live card closure performed.
note: 05 Findings/D1201 Existing work admission guard does not check current card closure.md

title: Work owner exclusivity treats expired sessions as open until explicitly closed
body: Append-time conflict check permits overlapping reads but refuses any new mutating admission against existing open read or mutating ownership on the gap. It does not check session expiry or gap-switch invalidation; explicit closure is required to release that owner. Guard separately rejects expired work.
note: 05 Findings/D1202 Work owner exclusivity treats expired sessions as open until explicitly closed.md

title: Work checkpoint new-branch check does not carry every old unresolved branch
body: Append verifies exact newly discovered cards since previous checkpoint and requires their unresolved members except active/closed/superseded. It does not require every still-open ID from previous unresolved_branch_gap_ids to remain. Thus this check protects new intake denominator, not complete branch-history conservation by itself.
note: 05 Findings/D1203 Work checkpoint new-branch check does not carry every old unresolved branch.md

title: Closed-card outgoing handoff condition does not count prior handoffs
body: Validator allows a closed active card when previous checkpoint has same active gap and switching_to is nonempty. It does not reject a second same-card outgoing checkpoint after the first. The test checks absent target, refusal of new work and one valid switch, not repeated outgoing emission.
note: 05 Findings/D1204 Closed-card outgoing handoff condition does not count prior handoffs.md

title: Session scope equality is textual normalization under host authority
body: Guard strips whitespace, normalizes slash direction, rejects duplicate/empty scopes and compares sorted sets. It does not resolve path aliases or execute effects. Actor ownership is not compared with a requesting identity because guard accepts no requester parameter. Host security retains execution authority.
note: 05 Findings/D1205 Session scope equality is textual normalization under host authority.md

title: Historical work tests cover immediate refusal rather than compaction combinations
body: Tests verify same-gap continuity, explicit close, expiry, higher-risk rejection and active gap mismatch; separate compaction case checks session-ID reuse. They do not guard a retained closed admission after closure detail evicts, or return to original gap after switch history eviction.
note: 05 Findings/D1206 Historical work tests cover immediate refusal rather than compaction combinations.md

title: Control ownership resolution is independent of lifecycle completion
body: Non-visible source metadata can resolve ownership without reading path/symbol. Explicit typed bindings can remain resolved after operational disposition removes gap links. Aggregate parents resolve when child ownership resolutions do, regardless of child card state. This is deliberate ownership accounting, not repair completion.
note: 05 Findings/D1207 Control ownership resolution is independent of lifecycle completion.md

title: Card relationships record typed links without enforcing acyclic execution order
body: Relationship reducer requires distinct known cards, supported relation and unique triple. It does not enforce global acyclicity or synchronize links with card dependencies/blockers. Aggregate resolution uses bounded fixed-point passes; cycles can remain unresolved rather than becoming execution ordering guarantees.
note: 05 Findings/D1208 Card relationships record typed links without enforcing acyclic execution order.md

title: Current typed observation is a shape and supplied-source predicate
body: Observation validates stages, flags, kind/mode and completeness; observed_at is nonempty text, not an age check. current_source and source hash are supplied assertions here rather than compared with repository bytes. Read-only observed operation may intentionally have attempted=False.
note: 05 Findings/D1209 Current typed observation is a shape and supplied-source predicate.md

title: Inventory reconciliation examination and operational proof are separate
body: Known-versus-disposed controls can reconcile inventory without any typed current observation. Examined requires all current controls have current_typed proof status, while operationally proven additionally requires operational disposition. surface_examined event alone does not satisfy these derived predicates.
note: 05 Findings/D1210 Inventory reconciliation examination and operational proof are separate.md

title: Same-ID control metadata revision retains prior disposition observation
body: Inventory revision predecessor binds sorted control IDs. If IDs stay the same while kind/label/source refs change, retained control_dispositions are preserved rather than invalidated or revalidated against new kind. Old current_typed status can survive the metadata change. Retiring/removing an ID does remove its live disposition while retaining history.
note: 05 Findings/D1211 Same-ID control metadata revision retains prior disposition observation.md

title: Revised disposition detail history omits old typed observation
body: Disposition revisions preserve prior disposition/gap/evidence/actor/time and predecessor binding, but historical detail row does not copy prior observation or proof_status. Full append-only JSONL remains required to recover that older typed observation; compact history retains only a latest detail plus hashes.
note: 05 Findings/D1212 Revised disposition detail history omits old typed observation.md

title: Evidence binding identifies current bytes without verifying supplied hashes
body: _bind_evidence reads resolvable referenced local file only when artifact_sha256 absent. Caller-supplied digest is not compared with file bytes. Reference prefix sha256 or fragment presence can satisfy some bound checks without reopening immutable storage. These are binding metadata, not independent claim verification.
note: 05 Findings/D1213 Evidence binding identifies current bytes without verifying supplied hashes.md

title: Ledger evidence-path handling has different bounds from report admission
body: Generic evidence resolution strips line suffixes and resolves contained paths before physical checks, so contained aliases can resolve to a physical target. _bind_evidence uses unbounded read_bytes; report manifest admission instead uses a 16MiB physical-file read and exact finding denominator/hash comparison.
note: 05 Findings/D1214 Ledger evidence-path handling has different bounds from report admission.md

title: Historical admission backfill is append-only but changes effective replay payload
body: Full replay validates exact earlier event target then overlays admission fields supplied by later backfill before validating the old transition. Dedicated writer requires full replay and appends one new event without rewriting original bytes. The resulting historical validation is assisted by later evidence, not proof of what the original event carried.
note: 05 Findings/D1215 Historical admission backfill is append-only but changes effective replay payload.md

title: Compact head and dashboard API disagree on feature-aware open count
body: _dashboard_index treats closed/operationally_verified/superseded as resolved only if declared feature acceptance verifies. dashboard_api both compact and full paths recomputes open_count from lifecycle states alone and derives source_status from it. Missing feature acceptance can remain in head critical blockers while punch-card API reports status-only resolved count.
note: 05 Findings/D1216 Compact head and dashboard API disagree on feature-aware open count.md

title: Compact dashboard rows and detailed history are intentionally bounded
body: Head retains first 100 priority-sorted cards, clips display fields and lists first 25 progress IDs with total/truncated flags. Full snapshot has bounded per-card history as well, so full-history investigation still needs JSONL. Unfiltered dashboard uses compact head only within its cached window; filtered/detail queries use snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1217 Compact dashboard rows and detailed history are intentionally bounded.md

title: Checkpoint read verifies cross-file hashes rather than replaying all semantics
body: Reader compares portable ledger size/hash, validates tail digest and links, verifies snapshot/delta hashes when requested, and rereads head for optimistic coherence. read_head intentionally omits snapshot. Unkeyed self-consistent head/snapshot replacement is not independently authenticated by a trusted external anchor or full replay on this path.
note: 05 Findings/D1218 Checkpoint read verifies cross-file hashes rather than replaying all semantics.md

title: Ledger digest cache trusts device inode size and mtime
body: Fingerprint caches whole-ledger digest by device/inode/size/mtime_ns and extends it from admitted append bytes. Same-identity same-size content mutation with restored mtime can evade this cache; source has no post-hash fstat consistency check. Existing same-length mutation test changes file normally and does not restore metadata. This edge is source-derived, not reproduced here.
note: 05 Findings/D1219 Ledger digest cache trusts device inode size and mtime.md

title: Prepared events precede fsync but projection publication follows commit
body: Entire bounded request is semantically prepared before ledger append. Opened file must match expected size/device/inode/mtime and writes loop to completion then fsync. Snapshot/delta/head publish afterward. Later publication error does not roll back JSONL; caller retry of same discovery can hit duplicate identity. Tests prove original event survives snapshot/head failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1220 Prepared events precede fsync but projection publication follows commit.md

title: Atomic publication applies per file rather than across all checkpoint files
body: Writer uses exclusive prepared filename, flush/fsync, os.replace and directory fsync where supported, then removes prepared file. Multiple files publish separately; optimistic readers retry three times and then report unavailable. A failure during prepared-file cleanup can also propagate after replacement.
note: 05 Findings/D1221 Atomic publication applies per file rather than across all checkpoint files.md

title: Large-snapshot fallback can reuse the stale artifact that caused replay
body: After append-base checkpoint failure, fallback returns full replay with predecessor=None. Publication subsequently rereads existing snapshot unbounded and, if at least 8MiB, uses it as delta base without requiring a verified predecessor. Corrupt JSON can raise after append; stale well-formed base plus only new appended rows can produce unreadable delta checkpoint. Source-derived path; normal forced-delta test uses valid base.
note: 05 Findings/D1222 Large-snapshot fallback can reuse the stale artifact that caused replay.md

title: Delta checkpoint preflight and retention have separate limits
body: Preappend preflight builds ordinary head. Delta-specific head fields are added and bounded after authoritative append. Cumulative delta is content-addressed; existing path is reused without reading equality in writer, though reader later verifies it. Old cumulative deltas are not reclaimed here, and compaction occurs only when delta bytes exceed 16MiB.
note: 05 Findings/D1223 Delta checkpoint preflight and retention have separate limits.md

title: Automatic recovery distinguishes malformed suffix from semantic corruption
body: Recovery only considers non-newline-terminated final suffix within event bound and first validates complete prefix. Invalid UTF8/JSON suffix is retained as exact base64/hash receipt before truncation. Syntactically complete but semantically invalid event is preserved and rejected. Valid complete event missing delimiter gets receipt then newline. No recovery executed by this audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1224 Automatic recovery distinguishes malformed suffix from semantic corruption.md

title: Append fallback may perform recovery before requested event is admitted
body: _load_append_base_unlocked is invoked under lock before preparing new requested event. Its recovery can write a receipt and alter final delimiter/torn suffix even if later payload validation fails. project/write_snapshot also invokes recovery; the read-only head/snapshot APIs do not.
note: 05 Findings/D1225 Append fallback may perform recovery before requested event is admitted.md

title: Segment migration is a separate historical projection with partial publication
body: Migration reads events under read_events lock then releases it before fingerprinting and writing segments/manifest. Concurrent append can change legacy identity; final equivalence validation can fail after new files exist. Existing differing manifest refuses overwrite. Legacy JSONL is retained and remains active authority.
note: 05 Findings/D1226 Segment migration is a separate historical projection with partial publication.md

title: Segment validation verifies content equality but not every manifest range claim
body: Validator checks manifest digest, segment byte/hash/count, combined exact legacy event equality, reducer validity and global legacy/head identity. It does not compare per-segment first_sequence/last_sequence/predecessor/head fields or enforce declared segment_event_limit against rows; manifest schema and read bounds are also not validated here.
note: 05 Findings/D1227 Segment validation verifies content equality but not every manifest range claim.md

title: Historical bootstrap conflicts with current provenance and chain admission
body: Historical cards set discovered_by to historical-operational-surface-audit but record actor is bootstrap actor. Fixed current cards also carry fixed 20260816 time/actor while append timestamp defaults current; chain_for creates present/partial stages with empty evidence. Current append rejects these before writing batch. The script is historical producer evidence, not a working current initializer claim.
note: 05 Findings/D1228 Historical bootstrap conflicts with current provenance and chain admission.md

title: Bootstrap surface union and dated findings must not become current truth
body: Regex action collection unions whole files for several surfaces, then filters Studio action names heuristically. Fixed rows PX-OS-068..094 retain dated source narratives and conversation approval text, with selected transitions through implementing. Those statements describe original bootstrap context and authorize nothing in this audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1229 Bootstrap surface union and dated findings must not become current truth.md

title: Live-size benchmark clone omits current delta projection files
body: Benchmark copies JSONL/snapshot/head only after reading source head separately. A delta head points outside those three files; bounded read_snapshot on copy can fail before append fallback. Sequential source copy has no frozen identity check. Small non-delta clone test does not prove this copy works for delta checkpoints.
note: 05 Findings/D1230 Live-size benchmark clone omits current delta projection files.md

title: Benchmark memory and rewrite metrics have narrower meaning than their labels
body: Without psutil RSS is zero and budget passes. RSS sampling covers cold decode only; no process-isolated baseline. projection_rewrite_bytes_per_append compares snapshot endpoints, excludes head and cumulative delta writes, and is not divided by append count. All samples are few warm observations, not tail-latency population guarantees.
note: 05 Findings/D1231 Benchmark memory and rewrite metrics have narrower meaning than their labels.md

title: Benchmark recovery and custody are explicit limits
body: Recovery benchmark removes newline from valid final event rather than writing malformed suffix. TemporaryDirectory and threads are managed by language contexts without local owned workspace/process registration. Optional output permits external/overwriting path; source-size and source-head identities are sampled separately. This report only reviews its source and does not execute benchmark or cleanup.
note: 05 Findings/D1232 Benchmark recovery and custody are explicit limits.md

title: Every-event test title exceeds actual exercised event list
body: The equality test covers initialization/inventory/surface aliases/cards/annotations/one transition/dispositions/examination/report/relationship/checkpoint/revision. It does not enumerate all EVENT_TYPES and omits sessions/closures/attestations/backfill/scope revisions and other transitions in that case. Other tests cover many separately, but title is not exhaustive coverage evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1233 Every-event test title exceeds actual exercised event list.md

title: Scaling tests force representation rather than demonstrate production scale
body: Scaling fixtures use one initial event and a one-byte threshold override; concurrency test appends eight surface events. They establish normal-path delta behavior, ordering and segment corruption handling on tiny inputs. Production-sized capacity, delta fallback after corrupt base and concurrent segmentation remain separate obligations.
note: 05 Findings/D1234 Scaling tests force representation rather than demonstrate production scale.md

title: Operator guard and mutation are separate APIs
body: CLI exposes guard-work as explicit read_snapshot plus guard_work_admission call. Other mutation commands directly append and do not invoke guard themselves. JSON payload may come from unbounded stdin or arbitrary existing file. This interface assumes host orchestration supplies prior authorization/governance; actor flag alone is not proof.
note: 05 Findings/D1235 Operator guard and mutation are separate APIs.md

title: Pinned review registration lacks the current embedded manifest
body: Registration derives finding_ids from four review classification dictionaries and pins source bytes. The retained pinned JSON has neither finding_ids nor findings. Current ledger _validate_report_manifest requires embedded nonempty finding_ids exact equality, so fresh registration fails despite check planning successfully. Existing historical registration may be reused. Metadata observation is retained in historical-reconciliation-inputs.json.
note: 05 Findings/D1236 Pinned review registration lacks the current embedded manifest.md

title: Registration check reports projected zero without append validation
body: Check mode only constructs entries; it does not run ledger admission or recalculate final snapshot. Output unreconciled_after_apply is literal zero in both modes. Existing registered findings are checked for exact card disposition and IDs, but the displayed zero remains a planned result rather than current audited count.
note: 05 Findings/D1237 Registration check reports projected zero without append validation.md

title: Historical binding compatibility accepts typed inventory class drift
body: Same inventory ID rejects reviewed count below current control count; differing IDs are accepted whenever both share pacify-x-typed-surfaces- prefix. No inventory source digest or numeric revision ordering comparison. Exact referenced controls must exist, but that proves identity membership rather than unchanged source meaning.
note: 05 Findings/D1238 Historical binding compatibility accepts typed inventory class drift.md

title: Reviewed bindings preserve gaps but can downgrade operational disposition
body: For each reviewed control script unions missing card IDs and revises current operational or gap disposition to gap with exact predecessor hash. It requires a current disposition and creates no initial one. This deliberately records ownership uncertainty; it is not a new operational observation and it never advances card lifecycle.
note: 05 Findings/D1239 Reviewed bindings preserve gaps but can downgrade operational disposition.md

title: Existing non-visible scope rerun checks only kind and path ID
body: A matching non_visible_path/path_id skips before rechecking source refs, authority, reason or review overrides. New scopes filter source refs for nonempty strings but do not resolve symbols. Aggregate ready compares ordered child list, whereas split tool later compares sets/supersets. Different rerun predicates can disagree.
note: 05 Findings/D1240 Existing non-visible scope rerun checks only kind and path ID.md

title: Reference repair fills all empty present stages from one existing path
body: Quality reconciler selects first existing discovery/source path or entire ledger fallback and inserts that same reference into each empty present/partial stage, retaining stage state and claiming restored support. It checks file existence rather than each stage claim. This can clear required-reference denominator without new interaction evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1241 Reference repair fills all empty present stages from one existing path.md

title: Owner and symbol quality repair is a fixed metadata assignment
body: Only unassigned/unknown owner labels become codex-primary. Six card IDs have fixed path-to-symbol fill rules only for empty symbol lists. No ownership acknowledgment, symbol existence or current source hash is checked by this script; incorrect nonempty metadata is left unchanged.
note: 05 Findings/D1242 Owner and symbol quality repair is a fixed metadata assignment.md

title: Reference selection and ledger binding have different containment rules
body: Quality helper permits absolute existing paths and strips the final colon suffix heuristically; generic ledger evidence binder hashes only resolved contained files. A helper-selected external path can therefore remain unbound. Fallback ledger file is mutable and each independently committed chunk may bind a different prefix.
note: 05 Findings/D1243 Reference selection and ledger binding have different containment rules.md

title: Accepted punch-card refresh changes proof binding without re-execution
body: Reconciler replaces stale hashes with current artifact bytes and updates accepted record timestamp, preserving accepted status. It runs no acceptance tests. Operation coverage checks the newly current digests, so digest drift can clear while original behavior remains un-reverified. Open modern records are intentionally skipped.
note: 05 Findings/D1244 Accepted punch-card refresh changes proof binding without re-execution.md

title: Punch-card refresh can partially write before later error
body: Errors list is shared across sorted records. Dirty records are written only when no errors have yet accumulated; a later malformed/missing record prevents subsequent writes but does not roll back earlier ones. Final valid=False can coexist with earlier accepted-record mutations. Writes are direct and have no retained revision/atomic group.
note: 05 Findings/D1245 Punch-card refresh can partially write before later error.md

title: Punch refresh input checks are weaker than coverage acceptance
body: Empty or non-list artifacts can produce zero checked rows without error; nonobject list entries are silently skipped. accepted_record_count counts all immediate JSON files including skipped open/unsupported/unreadable ones. Coverage requires nonempty list and validates each artifact object/unique path. Reconciler valid is not coverage acceptance validity.
note: 05 Findings/D1246 Punch refresh input checks are weaker than coverage acceptance.md

title: Duplicate modern artifact paths update only their first occurrence
body: Rows are captured before mutation. On mismatch, next(...) finds first artifact with matching path, so later duplicate entries can retain stale digest while apply reports valid when no errors. Coverage separately rejects duplicate resolved paths. Existing tests do not include duplicate entries.
note: 05 Findings/D1247 Duplicate modern artifact paths update only their first occurrence.md

title: External re-audit importer pins denominator rather than source authority
body: Parser requires exact Markdown row syntax, unique A-Z/three-digit IDs, exactly 113 rows and fixed severity/family totals. Other lines are ignored. It hashes original bytes and initializes every finding open with no owner/acceptance evidence. Correct counts do not validate truth or completeness outside this fixed table grammar.
note: 05 Findings/D1248 External re-audit importer pins denominator rather than source authority.md

title: Re-audit import is standalone and its portability substitution is narrow
body: Output is a separate remediation schema, not operational ledger events. Home substitution replaces only current native/doubled-backslash home spellings; it is not general path redaction. CLI directly writes arbitrary supplied output after creating parents, with no exclusive creation or source/output distinction.
note: 05 Findings/D1249 Re-audit import is standalone and its portability substitution is narrow.md

title: Live-walk mapping creates fixed feature families independent of report membership
body: Nine CARD_SPECS are proposed before iterating actual report findings. Existing features are indexed globally by name, with last duplicate winning, without matching surface/control/evidence. New IDs are allocated from a snapshot outside append lock; concurrent discovery can cause collision rejected at append.
note: 05 Findings/D1250 Live-walk mapping creates fixed feature families independent of report membership.md

title: Live-walk historical report registration has the same manifest mismatch
body: Retained walk reports have findings arrays but no top-level finding_ids. Script derives IDs from findings and later hashes a separate reread, while current ledger physical report validator requires embedded IDs. Fresh registration fails current contract; existing report IDs bypass registration. No live walker was run.
note: 05 Findings/D1251 Live-walk historical report registration has the same manifest mismatch.md

title: Live-walk rerun skips existing mappings without verifying their binding
body: If report ID already registered its source hash/finding denominator is not compared to current retained file. If finding ID already reconciled its disposition/gap IDs are not checked, unlike pinned review registration. New mapping relies on fixed dictionaries and unknown IDs raise; historical source claims remain discovery-only.
note: 05 Findings/D1252 Live-walk rerun skips existing mappings without verifying their binding.md

title: Aggregate splitter rejects new children before creating them
body: _parent_child_set always includes new_children IDs. main computes unknown=set(children)-set(cards) and exits before the later loop that would append missing card_discovered events. Therefore new_child_cards cannot become nonzero through this path; script presently reconciles only already-existing allocated IDs.
note: 05 Findings/D1253 Aggregate splitter rejects new children before creating them.md

title: Split rerun treats allocated ID existence as prior application
body: Any planned ID already in cards is accepted as pre-applied without comparing parent, feature, discovery source or payload. Frontier check only requires current maximum at least historical last_existing. Allocation count/uniqueness/min/max are checked but not contiguous sequence or absence of collision with unrelated existing cards.
note: 05 Findings/D1254 Split rerun treats allocated ID existence as prior application.md

title: Aggregate selector membership varies with current gap dispositions
body: Selectors enumerate current disposition rows, filter typed kind/label/regex, and union gap_ids. Operational promotion can remove those gap IDs and change desired child set despite fixed plan bytes. This makes historical plan plus current state the real input, not plan SHA alone.
note: 05 Findings/D1255 Aggregate selector membership varies with current gap dispositions.md

title: Aggregate scope revision preserves extras only in the superset branch
body: When current children already include every required child, script keeps prior extras. If one required child is missing, it revises to exactly ordered_children, dropping prior extra scope children although relationship history remains. Thus preservation depends on whether a missing child triggers revision.
note: 05 Findings/D1256 Aggregate scope revision preserves extras only in the superset branch.md

title: Dormant split discovery payload conflicts with append-time timestamp
body: Child payload uses fixed DISCOVERED_AT, but queued card_discovered event has no matching timestamp. If missing-child guard were repaired, current ledger requires discovered_at exactly match generated event time, creating a second independent incompatibility. This is source-derived dormant-path analysis.
note: 05 Findings/D1257 Dormant split discovery payload conflicts with append-time timestamp.md

title: Review and split dry runs do not invoke ledger admission
body: Check computes planned entries but does not project them through strengthened reducer/append-time validators. Apply uses independent bounded chunks; validation protects each chunk but no all-proposal transaction or final semantic denominator recomputation. A check count is a plan, not guaranteed applicable change.
note: 05 Findings/D1258 Review and split dry runs do not invoke ledger admission.md

title: Stream reconciliation turns implementation labels into executable handler claims
body: Child capability labels partition skills into operational versus deferred. Every handler is then marked executable regardless of missing enhancement count. No function loading, test invocation or receipt check occurs. Runtime uses executable status for admission after its separate preflight, so this writer affects activation metadata rather than merely display titles.
note: 05 Findings/D1259 Stream reconciliation turns implementation labels into executable handler claims.md

title: Stream missing denominator is moved and two files publish separately
body: Writer sets missing_capabilities=[] and retains nonoperational entries under deferred_capabilities, labels source adapted-bounded-runtime and chooses one of seventeen fixed titles. Unknown orchestration IDs fail. Sequential direct writes can leave orchestration and handler views inconsistent on second-write failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1260 Stream missing denominator is moved and two files publish separately.md

title: Studio reconciliation validates byte projection rather than protocol
body: Writer reads owner once and copies raw bytes to two targets without parsing JSON, schema or operation kinds. Apply reports valid whenever writes return; no immediate postwrite/source stability check. Import-time studio_protocol performs schema check, and generated_artifacts later compares bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1261 Studio reconciliation validates byte projection rather than protocol.md

title: Studio projection writes are not a combined atomic publication
body: Targets are fixed paths but writer uses normal path operations, no resolved target containment/physical-file check, exclusive temp replacement or rollback. Existing links can redirect writes; second target failure can leave first updated. This audit only maps behavior and does not reconcile source projections.
note: 05 Findings/D1262 Studio projection writes are not a combined atomic publication.md

title: Reference candidate partial coverage is a fixed mapping declaration
body: Fifteen canonical IDs receive predetermined skill/symbol unions and partial_semantic_coverage. No actual symbol availability, source digest or tests are verified. Existing active_composed rows are skipped entirely, preserving their claims. Broader source capability is explicitly still unadmitted.
note: 05 Findings/D1263 Reference candidate partial coverage is a fixed mapping declaration.md

title: Reference reconciliation marker is historical text rather than fresh certification
body: Helper writes runtime_reconciliation=2026-08-02-structural-recertification and recomputes delivery/canonical/duplicate counts. CLI overwrites registry directly. Neither the marker nor counts are a certification receipt or proof that referenced functions implement broader candidate semantics.
note: 05 Findings/D1264 Reference reconciliation marker is historical text rather than fresh certification.md

title: Punch refresh tests establish narrow preservation and containment cases
body: Tests assert accepted digest refresh, untouched open digest and escaping artifact rejection. They do not execute or validate original accepted behavior, timestamp meaning, duplicate or empty artifact handling, malformed records or multi-record partial commit. Their assertions should support only those narrow helper contracts.
note: 05 Findings/D1265 Punch refresh tests establish narrow preservation and containment cases.md

title: Inventory reconciliation covers incoming surfaces rather than whole-surface retirement
body: Only incoming known surfaces are reconciled. Identical control IDs and records skip the revision without comparing source_files. Entire old surfaces absent from input are not retired here. Expected inventory checks exact source metadata and predecessor, but are a separate event.
note: 05 Findings/D1266 Inventory reconciliation covers incoming surfaces rather than whole-surface retirement.md

title: Receipt classification validates claimed source flags rather than source bytes
body: Current source requires host_source_mismatch false and source_identity.state verified; the control manifest digest is checked for SHA grammar. This helper does not recompute the inventoried source identity or establish receipt age.
note: 05 Findings/D1267 Receipt classification validates claimed source flags rather than source bytes.md

title: Duplicate chain stages collapse before exact-denominator validation
body: Stage rows become a dictionary keyed by stage, so later duplicates replace earlier values. Equality of resulting keys to CHAIN_STAGES does not require exactly one row per stage. Generated receipt fragment references can fill stage evidence without a raw evidence artifact.
note: 05 Findings/D1268 Duplicate chain stages collapse before exact-denominator validation.md

title: Observation fallback and ledger normalization have different semantics
body: A visible clean complete indicator can enter fallback whether observed is omitted or explicitly false. The produced v1 observation can retain observed=false, while ledger v1 normalization derives observed from rendered and drops extra fields. Conversely a nonvisible observed=true/rendered=false planner result may fail ledger operational admission.
note: 05 Findings/D1269 Observation fallback and ledger normalization have different semantics.md

title: Recovered authority boundary is a narrow explicit disposition class
body: Only ten named controls with required boundary metadata, observed failure/recovery and an incomplete stage can qualify. These remain gap dispositions with gap IDs, observed-only outcomes and v2 evidence; accepting their boundary does not establish execution of the protected operation.
note: 05 Findings/D1270 Recovered authority boundary is a narrow explicit disposition class.md

title: Unobserved foreign rows can pad receipt cardinality before membership checks
body: Receipt total, record length and globally unique IDs must equal known control count. A record yielding no observation is skipped before known surface/control membership checks, so cardinality alone does not guarantee exact receipt membership. Full completion additionally requires every expected observation, limiting the effect on final valid status.
note: 05 Findings/D1271 Unobserved foreign rows can pad receipt cardinality before membership checks.md

title: Prior operational state suppresses contrary error observations
body: When a newly classified result would be gap and the current disposition is operational, the planner unconditionally continues. The condition includes new errors and failure results, not just harmless partial metadata. An explicit separate path must therefore correct an old operational disposition.
note: 05 Findings/D1272 Prior operational state suppresses contrary error observations.md

title: Dry simulation retains fields and history that live projection discards
body: Observation simulation copies raw observations and extends full prior history. The live ledger normalizes typed observations and compacts retained history. Proposal equality and card-binding reachability can consequently differ between simulation, first apply and repeated apply.
note: 05 Findings/D1273 Dry simulation retains fields and history that live projection discards.md

title: Historical card advancement depends on retained compact history
body: Binding discovery enumerates current dispositions and retained history only, then tests current disposition outcome. Older gap bindings evicted by ledger compaction disappear from this planner even though original events remain in the durable JSONL. Explicit card control scopes are not an alternate binding source here.
note: 05 Findings/D1274 Historical card advancement depends on retained compact history.md

title: Special feature acceptance copies requirements into synthesized evidence
body: For unverified-operational-control cards, synthesis copies requirement revision, criteria, dependency keys, classes, authority and tests into verified evidence backed by one aggregate receipt, then invokes the metadata verifier. It does not independently demonstrate that the receipt exercised every copied required test or evidence class.
note: 05 Findings/D1275 Special feature acceptance copies requirements into synthesized evidence.md

title: Card planner reuses aggregate proof across lifecycle transitions
body: Eligible primary-state cards receive merged chain evidence and forward transitions through operational verification. The same aggregate receipt supports multiple lifecycle steps. The helper does not execute implementation, tests or integration work, and current outcome checks do not independently revalidate full chain/current source proof.
note: 05 Findings/D1276 Card planner reuses aggregate proof across lifecycle transitions.md

title: Nonprimary card states can abort reconciliation planning
body: The planner skips selected terminal, host-owned and excluded cards, then calls CARD_PRIMARY_STATES.index(state). A bound eligible card in blocked, deferred or reopened state can raise rather than produce a controlled nontransition result.
note: 05 Findings/D1277 Nonprimary card states can abort reconciliation planning.md

title: Completion can accept recovered boundaries with no operational controls
body: Status distinguishes current operational controls from acceptable recovered authority boundaries. A discovered gap card bound to an accepted boundary can be excluded from nonterminal cards. The test fixture demonstrates valid status with zero operational receipt controls; this is boundary accounting rather than complete execution.
note: 05 Findings/D1278 Completion can accept recovered boundaries with no operational controls.md

title: Completion checks terminal labels rather than feature acceptance again
body: Status counts only cards found through current/retained disposition bindings and regards terminal card states as complete without repeating feature acceptance validation. Unbound cards are outside this denominator; boundary-linked cards can be exempted even if their broader bindings remain.
note: 05 Findings/D1279 Completion checks terminal labels rather than feature acceptance again.md

title: Inventory changes can commit before receipt rejection
body: CLI apply submits inventory revisions before it loads and validates the optional live receipt. It later submits discovery, initial disposition, observation and card batches separately. A bad receipt or later invalid completion result can follow already committed mutations.
note: 05 Findings/D1280 Inventory changes can commit before receipt rejection.md

title: Discovery identity and requirements can drift across inventory revisions
body: Missing-card allocation uses a sampled maximum ID outside the append lock and existing cards are indexed by control_action without surface identity. Initial feature requirements pin the discovery inventory hash; later synthesis can retain that old requirement revision with newer aggregate evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1281 Discovery identity and requirements can drift across inventory revisions.md

title: Check-mode completion is based partly on uncommitted plans
body: Check simulates raw dispositions, and planned reconciled card IDs are excluded from final nonterminal count without applying their transition events through the reducer. The printed valid result is proposal validity under that simulation, not a current committed state. operational_claims also counts observation revisions, excluding direct initial operational bindings.
note: 05 Findings/D1282 Check-mode completion is based partly on uncommitted plans.md

title: Reconciliation tests omit live normalization and failing apply sequences
body: Tests cover important planner branches and mocked status, but do not run full ledger append normalization, history compaction, duplicate stage rows, error-based demotion suppression, nonprimary card states or multi-phase partial commits. Their source does not prove those paths safe.
note: 05 Findings/D1283 Reconciliation tests omit live normalization and failing apply sequences.md

title: Installed owner plan is command-shape validation only
body: Plan reports effects=false after command validation. Campaign activity, exact artifact hash/size/mtime, package/install receipts, engine manifest and fresh output paths are checked only by execute. Plan success is not operational readiness.
note: 05 Findings/D1284 Installed owner plan is command-shape validation only.md

title: Installed command validation leaves executable and shell latitude
body: Windows/exhaustive commands check node basename, script and selected flags while allowing extra arguments. Ubuntu checks fixed wsl prefix and shell-string markers rather than parsing or proving command equivalence; markers can occur alongside other shell content. These are caller-controlled commands within host authority.
note: 05 Findings/D1285 Installed command validation leaves executable and shell latitude.md

title: Installed preflight validates upstream receipt claims without redoing their audit
body: Package/install receipt schema, artifact identity, counts, cleanup and stage fields are checked. Engine manifest shape and digest are read. The owner does not itself inspect ZIP contents, reconstruct the installed tree or verify engine tree contents against the manifest. Those remain upstream owner obligations.
note: 05 Findings/D1286 Installed preflight validates upstream receipt claims without redoing their audit.md

title: Fresh output paths are not checked for mutual uniqueness
body: Execute rejects existing summary/log/receipt/lifecycle/report paths, but does not require all configured paths be distinct. Resolved contained aliases are accepted by path construction. Collisions can fail after the stage claim rather than during freshness checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1287 Fresh output paths are not checked for mutual uniqueness.md

title: Process timeout and interruption closure differ
body: Process wait timeout attempts Windows tree termination or POSIX group termination and verifies the leader has stopped. Other BaseException paths close the log but do not terminate the child. POSIX leader polling is not a complete descendant inventory. Owner wrapper itself does not register its launched processes in resource lifecycle.
note: 05 Findings/D1288 Process timeout and interruption closure differ.md

title: Parallel launch uses sequential wait budgets
body: Windows and Ubuntu are started before either wait, but each timeout begins at its own wait call. The second process may run during the entire first wait and then receive its full timeout. Launch/wait errors are retained after waiting existing children. Ordinary smoke result failures still allow the exhaustive member to run.
note: 05 Findings/D1289 Parallel launch uses sequential wait budgets.md

title: Smoke receipt checks do not establish all host status semantics
body: Smoke result validates artifact hashes, platform, engine identity and embedded/separate lifecycle equality. Host receipt is primarily schema-checked; broader host readiness or listener state is not independently established here. Fresh paths provide run isolation, not authentication of every reported fact.
note: 05 Findings/D1290 Smoke receipt checks do not establish all host status semantics.md

title: Exhaustive result trusts aggregate fields rather than enumerating controls
body: The exhaustive member checks reported completion, issues, normalized counters, scope/process/cleanup and artifact fields. It does not enumerate every profile/control chain or bind report and receipt through source, engine or campaign identities. Recursive counter coercion accepts several noninteger input forms.
note: 05 Findings/D1291 Exhaustive result trusts aggregate fields rather than enumerating controls.md

title: Final artifact failure can publish and advance a passed stage
body: After all three members pass, execute sets passed=true and then rechecks the artifact. The catch stores the exception without resetting passed. Summary can contain all_passed=true plus error; finish receives true and repair phase advances before OwnerBlocked is raised. Confirmed using the actual execute flow with all effects faked; retained probe at data/semantic-closure/installed-owner-order-probe.json.
note: 05 Findings/D1292 Final artifact failure can publish and advance a passed stage.md

title: Post-claim summary construction can skip release finish
body: Fresh package/install artifact references are computed outside the main catch and before the guarded summary write. A reference read failure there propagates before effects.finish, leaving claim closure to external recovery. Final source/engine identity and upstream receipt bytes are not revalidated as one stable snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1293 Post-claim summary construction can skip release finish.md

title: Summary publication release finish and repair advance are separate effects
body: Exclusive prepared summary publication uses a prior existence check then replacement; concurrent target creation can race that check. Finish runs before a separate repair-state rewrite. Finish or advance failure is not rolled back by this owner, and advance does not use a shared predecessor-bound transaction with the release stage.
note: 05 Findings/D1294 Summary publication release finish and repair advance are separate effects.md

title: Installed owner tests use synthetic artifacts and effects
body: The tests validate launch order, preflight gates and selected ordinary failures with fake VSIX bytes, fake receipts and fake processes. They do not establish real timeout/descendant closure, final artifact drift handling, summary failure recovery, command equivalence or full installed-host compatibility.
note: 05 Findings/D1295 Installed owner tests use synthetic artifacts and effects.md

title: Frozen DAG inventory does not make every list exact
body: The validator enforces 43 distinct node records and 86 distinct dependency edges, matching known cards and a topological dependency order. Topological_order is checked by set equality without list length/uniqueness, so a duplicate terminal entry passes; confirmed with a pure synthetic 43-node/86-edge graph. Consumer lists must include reverse dependencies but may contain extra known consumers without reverse dependency.
note: 05 Findings/D1296 Frozen DAG inventory does not make every list exact.md

title: Checksum inventory binds expected projection names rather than all directory files
body: SHA256SUMS must list exactly cards, DAG and README and match their bytes. Additional directory files are not part of that inventory. Evidence readers resolve paths before checking symlinks and hash/stat separately; contained aliases and concurrent content changes are not excluded as one stable physical snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1297 Checksum inventory binds expected projection names rather than all directory files.md

title: Historical evidence validates receipt fields without executing behavioral criteria
body: The fixed freeze, final99 full/validation and repair12 receipts are validated and selected referenced files are hashed. Focused-test logs and installed focused receipts/reports are retained by hash rather than interpreted for each card criterion. Benchmark budget_results only requires all supplied values truthy, including the empty dictionary case; full-profile group count equality does not itself establish positive exact counts.
note: 05 Findings/D1298 Historical evidence validates receipt fields without executing behavioral criteria.md

title: Card evidence requires some implementation file rather than every declared file
body: Live references are limited to recognized evidence families or one external orchestration path. Source cards need nonempty criteria/test/symbol strings, but symbols are not resolved and missing declared files are skipped as long as one exists. External anchor validation uses card ID substring presence. These checks establish traceability shape rather than complete implementation.
note: 05 Findings/D1299 Card evidence requires some implementation file rather than every declared file.md

title: Cohesion successor syntax is broader than numerical successor order
body: Installed proof accepts any positive final number/date matching the campaign pattern. Close binds the exact repair12 predecessor through the release kernel, but does not compare the candidate number/date to final99. The word successor therefore carries a caller ordering obligation beyond this regex.
note: 05 Findings/D1300 Cohesion successor syntax is broader than numerical successor order.md

title: Installed proof consumer accepts selected summary facts and retained bytes
body: The consumer requires all_passed, concurrency flags, exact three member names, zero exits, artifact/process flags and exhaustive aggregate counters; it verifies hashes for member logs/receipts/lifecycle/report. It does not parse those member artifacts or check each member valid field, and does not reject a top-level summary error. Actual artifact drift still fails its hash checks; this is not a claim that every owner error bypasses closure.
note: 05 Findings/D1301 Installed proof consumer accepts selected summary facts and retained bytes.md

title: Release timing is checked without proving admission event authenticity
body: Close requires exact release and automation stage insertion order, passing labels, sequential UTC windows and automation windows enclosing release windows. Admission/gap IDs are checked only as nonempty strings, not against ledger work admissions. Source digests bind the release kernel but are not recomputed from current repository bytes here.
note: 05 Findings/D1302 Release timing is checked without proving admission event authenticity.md

title: Installed proof timestamp is not joined to the release window
body: finished_utc is valid UTC syntax and becomes the default card close timestamp. It is not compared with the installed release stage finish, automation finish, earlier card history or explicit --at. A syntactically valid override can therefore predate the evidence it purports to reconcile.
note: 05 Findings/D1303 Installed proof timestamp is not joined to the release window.md

title: Lifecycle history is synthesized from one reconciliation event
body: All intermediate lifecycle entries between current and target receive the same timestamp, reason and evidence references. This is an evidence-backed projection of claimed progress, not a record showing separate admitted implementation, test and integration executions. Existing at-target/closed cards return without refreshing evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1304 Lifecycle history is synthesized from one reconciliation event.md

title: Project-state projection replaces broader state with fixed campaign claims
body: The writer clears degraded_components, replaces failures/open circuits/unknowns, sets branch main without querying branch, fixes revision at least 44 and clears active card. Counts are derived from requested target rather than actual mixed retained card states; existing closed cards can coexist with a downstream target reporting zero closed in management state.
note: 05 Findings/D1305 Project-state projection replaces broader state with fixed campaign claims.md

title: Cohesion WAL validates after-images without a planning predecessor
body: Cards/evidence/state are read and projected before commit. JsonWal captures before-images under its own lock; custom precommit reads transition.after only and does not compare transition.before with the previously validated planning snapshot. A concurrent valid change before lock acquisition can be overwritten by the older proposal while still becoming the transaction before-image.
note: 05 Findings/D1306 Cohesion WAL validates after-images without a planning predecessor.md

title: WAL recovery precedes fresh reconciliation evidence checks
body: Apply invokes recover before card checksums, current evidence and close gates. Check only inspects and fails if recovery is needed. A previous committed proposal may therefore be completed during apply before the new request passes its evidence checks; recovery and new admission are distinct stages.
note: 05 Findings/D1307 WAL recovery precedes fresh reconciliation evidence checks.md

title: Control and cohesion apply are not one atomic operation
body: The release driver requires check-control, check-cohesion, apply-control, apply-cohesion in exactly that order. Control events use append batches while cohesion uses a separate WAL. A failure after control apply can leave control changes committed without cohesion closure; driver final status separately checks both denominators.
note: 05 Findings/D1308 Control and cohesion apply are not one atomic operation.md

title: Closed cohesion is deliberately short of certification
body: Close requires certify pending and active release identity, plus prior installed stage pass. Management state and README explicitly retain certification/publication obligations. A later check after certification changes these conditions, so repeated close is not an unconditional post-certification verifier.
note: 05 Findings/D1309 Closed cohesion is deliberately short of certification.md

title: Cohesion tests prove useful recovery and metadata cases within synthetic evidence
body: Tests cover deterministic plans, checksums, dependency disagreement, explicit idempotent apply, interrupted fifth-target publication/recovery, exact member identity, stage chronology, resource status and repeat close. Synthetic artifacts can be arbitrary bytes; tests do not prove member contents or each acceptance criterion, planning race safety, summary-error handling or duplicate topology rejection.
note: 05 Findings/D1310 Cohesion tests prove useful recovery and metadata cases within synthetic evidence.md

title: Typed inventory fuses historical semantics and current declarations
body: One historical surface overlay replaces the base surface after base SHA validation. Current action contracts and two controller navigation arrays add declarations; fixed mappings add structural/native/variant controls. The output is a hybrid provenance baseline, not a fresh rendered or executed inventory.
note: 05 Findings/D1311 Typed inventory fuses historical semantics and current declarations.md

title: Current action coverage is only at the base action name
body: Every action contract must appear somewhere among historical/current typed action label prefixes. It does not require each rendered surface or template variant to be mapped. Historical actions absent from current contracts are retained, and structural/native controls are hardcoded rather than derived from current handlers/package commands.
note: 05 Findings/D1312 Current action coverage is only at the base action name.md

title: Action inventory duplicate rows can collapse before count validation
body: Action records are keyed by action name and compared only with declared action_count. Duplicate rows can be hidden if the declared count matches unique keys. Navigation parsing uses regex over two specific const-array forms, so source formatting or commented text can affect discovery independently of runtime rendering.
note: 05 Findings/D1313 Action inventory duplicate rows can collapse before count validation.md

title: Typed inventory source provenance is incomplete for generated controls
body: Top-level hashes bind overlay, action inventory and dashboard controller, but not builder source or extension package bytes used by the fixed native-command list. Per-surface source_files come from historical source_refs rather than the union of current per-control rendered references. Source refs and base_report paths are consumed without an overall containment or immutable snapshot check.
note: 05 Findings/D1314 Typed inventory source provenance is incomplete for generated controls.md

title: Inventory lifecycle IDs depend on historical list position
body: Lifecycle identities use path.1, path.2 and so on. Reordering or inserting historical lifecycle labels changes identity-to-meaning association.
