Stable names for actions coexist with positional lifecycle IDs; consumers must evaluate metadata revisions rather than assuming identical ID preserves semantics.
note: 05 Findings/D1315 Inventory lifecycle IDs depend on historical list position.md

title: Typed inventory generation writes directly and tests only a narrow exclusion rule
body: Default CLI overwrites registry bytes; check compares exact bytes with regenerated output. It is not an atomic publication across its input sources. The sole test verifies five hidden fields stay excluded and total count equals unique IDs, not current rendered completeness or negative malformed-source cases.
note: 05 Findings/D1316 Typed inventory generation writes directly and tests only a narrow exclusion rule.md

title: Heuristic catalog does not retain a complete discovery error denominator
body: Catalog prunes named dependency/build directories, silently continues on stat/read failures and uses os.walk without onerror. It emits no file hashes. Its file_count is successful selected rows rather than all physical files. Optional summaries read at most nominal 1 MiB files but only return a short heuristic description.
note: 05 Findings/D1317 Heuristic catalog does not retain a complete discovery error denominator.md

title: Catalog redaction and classification are narrow lexical transformations
body: Three source terms are substituted, not arbitrary private paths or secrets. Classification follows ordered path/name/size rules, with governance before skills before tests and other categories. These recommendations are not capability admission or semantic review. Existing output files under the root can enter later runs.
note: 05 Findings/D1318 Catalog redaction and classification are narrow lexical transformations.md

title: Hash-backed inventory accounting excludes traversal failures and configured omissions
body: Selected file failures are retained and cause CLI failure, but os.walk has no onerror and pruned directories/root-files-only entries never enter files_discovered. Thus discovered=records+errors can hold despite an unreadable or excluded subtree. File symlinks are not rejected before stat/read/hash.
note: 05 Findings/D1319 Hash-backed inventory accounting excludes traversal failures and configured omissions.md

title: File identity text structure and hash can describe different versions
body: Inventory stat, sample read, optional full text read and final streaming SHA are separate operations without before/after identity verification. Concurrent edits can produce old size/structure with new hash. Full-tree freeze likewise stats before hashing each file and does not lock or compare a second snapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1320 File identity text structure and hash can describe different versions.md

title: Inventory text structure is bounded lexical evidence rather than parser semantics
body: Text detection uses a 64 KiB sample, suffix/MIME or UTF-8. Structure extraction uses regex headings, fences, links, command prefixes and declaration lines over text below a size threshold. Normalized digest uses sanitized casefolded whitespace; SimHash takes at most 100000 tokens. Large text remains text with empty structure.
note: 05 Findings/D1321 Inventory text structure is bounded lexical evidence rather than parser semantics.md

title: Structure projection trusts upstream format and identity
body: extract copies selected metadata from rows labeled text and derives format from path suffix. It does not parse any source file or verify the source hash. The test proves only Markdown/JSON retention and binary exclusion from declared input labels.
note: 05 Findings/D1322 Structure projection trusts upstream format and identity.md

title: Exact duplicate groups trust supplied hashes and can contain only one distinct ID
body: Grouping uses declared sha256 and int(bytes), without reading source contents. It requires two input rows before deduplicating IDs, so repeated same-ID rows can emit a count-one group. Group IDs truncate SHA and omit size, though grouping key includes size.
note: 05 Findings/D1323 Exact duplicate groups trust supplied hashes and can contain only one distinct ID.md

title: Duplicate classification implicitly chooses the lexicographically first ID
body: Exact groups sort IDs; classifier marks members[1:] duplicate. That makes the first hash-derived ID canonical by position without reviewed provenance or quality. A missing optional duplicate file silently disables this stage. Duplicates are classified before executable-extension checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1324 Duplicate classification implicitly chooses the lexicographically first ID.md

title: Near-duplicate prefix bucketing loses close neighbors
body: SimHash candidates are only compared within equal extension and equal first four hex digits. A one-bit difference in that prefix prevents comparison even when full Hamming distance is within threshold. Normalized-hash equality is a separate exact grouping path.
note: 05 Findings/D1325 Near-duplicate prefix bucketing loses close neighbors.md

title: Greedy SimHash clusters are not pairwise or transitive equivalence
body: Each unassigned anchor collects later candidates within distance, then all are assigned. Members need not be close to each other and transitive neighbors can be split. Confidence is computed from configured max_hamming rather than actual measured distances. Large same-prefix buckets can require quadratic comparisons.
note: 05 Findings/D1326 Greedy SimHash clusters are not pairwise or transitive equivalence.md

title: Zero unknown classification comes from forced fallback labels
body: The first matching path/heading rule wins; confidence is a fixed lexical score. Remaining records become not_applicable, knowledge_reference_only or clean_room_required, then summary hardcodes unknown_count=0. This does not establish reviewed applicability, safe execution or correct semantic ownership. Quarantine is only a review-state string.
note: 05 Findings/D1327 Zero unknown classification comes from forced fallback labels.md

title: Review cluster identity binds grouping attributes rather than members
body: Clusters group class/domain/review_state and select the shortest lexical path as representative. ID hashes a pipe-joined tuple, without member-list identity or delimiter escaping. Member duplicates are not rejected and representative choice is not evidence quality ranking.
note: 05 Findings/D1328 Review cluster identity binds grouping attributes rather than members.md

title: Partition merge assumes sorted inputs and keeps a global ID set
body: heapq.merge is applied to streams without checking each stream is ordered. It avoids retaining all rows but stores every seen ID, so memory is still proportional to corpus identity count. Output input-aliasing is not rejected; lazy input iterators can open after output truncation.
note: 05 Findings/D1329 Partition merge assumes sorted inputs and keeps a global ID set.md

title: Partition merge failure can replace a good result with a partial file
body: Output is opened directly before row validation. A duplicate ID or malformed later record raises after earlier rows have been written, and summary is not updated as a transaction. Input file existence alone is checked before output mutation.
note: 05 Findings/D1330 Partition merge failure can replace a good result with a partial file.md

title: Partition campaign can reconcile an empty or partially omitted campaign
body: Immediate directories missing summary or inventory are skipped; explicit exclusions further reduce scope. Reconciliation trusts summary counts and root flags, including empty roots/list vacuous truth. Inventory contents, supplied hashes and error-log rows are not read, and logged errors can intentionally count as reconciled files.
note: 05 Findings/D1331 Partition campaign can reconcile an empty or partially omitted campaign.md

title: Map digest refresh does not restore source evidence validity
body: Rehash updates inventory_sha256 from current map bytes and replaces an existing Markdown hash line. It does not validate records, source hashes, counts or the claimed preceding sanitization. Multiple partitions and JSON/Markdown writes can partially finish.
note: 05 Findings/D1332 Map digest refresh does not restore source evidence validity.md

title: Freeze helper captures one file view rather than an immutable full topology
body: Snapshot includes paths recognized as files with content hash, size and mtime, omitting directory and other entry identity. File links can dereference content, casefold-only sorting can tie, and no scan budget or second matching snapshot is enforced. Output under the scanned root changes future manifests; timestamp also changes output bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1333 Freeze helper captures one file view rather than an immutable full topology.md

title: Source comparison misses normalized matches of different byte lengths
body: Workspace candidates are prefiltered by source raw byte sizes before both exact and normalized comparison. Whitespace-only changes that alter length can therefore be absent from normalized matches. Normalization casefolds code/text and collapses whitespace, which is not semantic equivalence.
note: 05 Findings/D1334 Source comparison misses normalized matches of different byte lengths.md

title: Source comparison scope and completeness are heuristic
body: Traversal excludes selected names and quarantine by resolved roots, but does not reject external file links or establish a stable snapshot. Reads are unbounded. active_implementation is assigned from fixed path prefixes, so matching bytes in that scope do not establish current runtime usage.
note: 05 Findings/D1335 Source comparison scope and completeness are heuristic.md

title: ZIP hazard inventory inspects central-directory claims without payload validation
body: Archive hash is computed, but member bodies are never opened; CRC values, sizes and ratios are metadata. Nested archives are only listed and do not themselves trigger danger. Traversal/encryption/link/ratio findings produce recommendations, not extraction, move or deletion. CLI returns zero after writing even when archives contain recorded errors.
note: 05 Findings/D1336 ZIP hazard inventory inspects central-directory claims without payload validation.md

title: Archive thresholds flag metadata after its allocation rather than bound parsing
body: ZipFile loads infolist before max_entries and aggregate thresholds are checked. Optional maps and hazard sets can grow with all entries; no bound limits the archive byte hashing or central-directory parse. Floating NaN thresholds satisfy the simple positivity check but disable greater-than ratio comparisons.
note: 05 Findings/D1337 Archive thresholds flag metadata after its allocation rather than bound parsing.md

title: Sanitized archive identity can collide and old maps remain
body: Sanitization collapses path separators, control characters, drive syntax, colons, source terms and parent markers. Hazard sets deduplicate sanitized names, and map IDs hash sanitized root/path, so distinct originals can collapse or overwrite one map. No old map cleanup occurs when an archive disappears.
note: 05 Findings/D1338 Sanitized archive identity can collide and old maps remain.md

title: Archive metadata and content digest are read at different times
body: Both archive tools hash then independently parse/stat archive bytes, without a stable before/after check. A changing archive can yield a content digest paired with later metadata. The simple catalog reads whole archive bytes into memory; hazard inventory streams its digest but loads metadata.
note: 05 Findings/D1339 Archive metadata and content digest are read at different times.md

title: Deduplicated archive tree hash binds metadata rather than member contents
body: Simple catalog entry trees use path hash, uncompressed/compressed sizes and CRC, sorted by path hash. It does not read payloads or reject duplicate entry paths/hazards. Identical archive bytes share stored maps, but every occurrence is still parsed. Invalid ZIP occurrences remain and CLI still exits successfully.
note: 05 Findings/D1340 Deduplicated archive tree hash binds metadata rather than member contents.md

title: Corpus report writers do not publish one atomic evidence set
body: Catalog, file inventory, classification and partition outputs use direct writes and independently written summaries. Different tools permit arbitrary caller output paths, without common input-output identity checks or retained rollback. A successful earlier file can remain alongside stale or absent later summaries.
note: 05 Findings/D1341 Corpus report writers do not publish one atomic evidence set.md

title: Corpus tests establish fixture accounting rather than broad semantic closure
body: Tests use tiny synthetic files to check repeatability, structure fields, one exact group, class count, merge duplicate rejection and reconciled logged error accounting. They do not exercise near-duplicate search completeness, full tree error handling, mutation races or output aliasing. Subprocess helper has no timeout.
note: 05 Findings/D1342 Corpus tests establish fixture accounting rather than broad semantic closure.md

title: Archive tests support metadata behavior and non-extraction only
body: Tests verify deterministic maps, hazards, configured thresholds, bad ZIP retention and identical-archive deduplication using small fixtures. They do not test payload corruption, sanitized collisions, stale map removal, stable source identity, metadata allocation limits or NaN thresholds. No product archive tests were run in this audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1343 Archive tests support metadata behavior and non-extraction only.md

title: Legacy map wrappers expose different validation and exit contracts
body: Build forwards traversal budgets/exclusions/incremental mode and exits zero when the runtime returns, without checking a valid field. Validation opts into freshness only with --fresh and maps valid to exit status. Query forwards top-k and exits zero on a returned result. Their runtime owners, not wrappers, enforce operational behavior.
note: 05 Findings/D1344 Legacy map wrappers expose different validation and exit contracts.md

title: Portable routing and transcript wrappers delegate authority to selected runtime
body: They prepend local source only when a runtime directory exists, otherwise use imported installed modules and framework_root. Specialist routing returns recommendations and valid-based exit, not spawned agents. Transcript export forwards explicit apply and exits zero if the underlying call returns.
note: 05 Findings/D1345 Portable routing and transcript wrappers delegate authority to selected runtime.md

title: Legacy bootstrap reporter is not an independent certification owner
body: audit_framework performs the work; reporter renders all supplied checks and uses valid for exit. External manifest strictness is opt-in. JSON and Markdown writes use caller paths without creating parents or joint atomic publication. Rendering PASS does not add new evidence beyond the runtime report.
note: 05 Findings/D1346 Legacy bootstrap reporter is not an independent certification owner.md

title: Service discovery heuristic uses whole-file keyword suppression
body: A selected config file warns only when an IPv4 address pattern appears and no discovery/resolver/TTL/registry keyword occurs anywhere. Unrelated comments can suppress a real stale-address concern; hostname-only or IPv6 paths are outside the detector. No service resolution or expiry is observed.
note: 05 Findings/D1347 Service discovery heuristic uses whole-file keyword suppression.md

title: Static service audit completeness omits skipped files and traversal errors
body: Unreadable/oversized/unsupported/link files are skipped without an error denominator; os.walk has no onerror. stat occurs outside the read catch and may abort. complete is hardcoded true, and CLI exits zero with review findings. The test covers only one IPv4 config and an added resolver line.
note: 05 Findings/D1348 Static service audit completeness omits skipped files and traversal errors.md

title: Import audit matches source strings rather than resolved dependencies
body: Python uses AST import names; JS uses a literal regex missing side-effect imports, dynamic imports and runtime resolution. Selection casefolds suffix but parser branch tests exact .py, so .PY takes JS scanning. Any target beginning three dots is marked escape even when package-relative syntax is legitimate.
note: 05 Findings/D1349 Import audit matches source strings rather than resolved dependencies.md

title: Import mirror policy can point outside the project
body: Canonical and mirror strings are joined to root without resolve/containment checks; absolute paths or parent segments can redirect reads. Mirror verification is byte equality only. Source traversal omissions remain outside findings, while parse failures become findings and fail CLI.
note: 05 Findings/D1350 Import mirror policy can point outside the project.md

title: Scanner aggregation complete means parse completion rather than all-pass security
body: Every finding carries its envelope status; complete is simply not errors, so fail/blocked/skipped/uncertain scanner results can coexist with complete=true. Missing or empty input directory can also complete. The focused test explicitly expects aggregation completeness while preserving a fail count.
note: 05 Findings/D1351 Scanner aggregation complete means parse completion rather than all-pass security.md

title: Scanner aggregation can lose malformed finding rows without an error
body: Non-dictionary findings are skipped, but a nonempty all-invalid list suppresses the empty-summary fallback and yields no records. Non-object JSON roots can raise AttributeError outside the catch. Tool/location strings remain raw while messages are hashed; hashing messages alone is not general payload sanitization.
note: 05 Findings/D1352 Scanner aggregation can lose malformed finding rows without an error.md

title: Text repair ordering permits cascades and empty search strings
body: Mappings sort by descending search length then lexical key and apply sequentially. Replacement text may be changed by a later mapping, and empty search keys insert text between characters. JSON repair changes values only and always reserializes, so changed can be true with no replacements while object keys stay unchanged.
note: 05 Findings/D1353 Text repair ordering permits cascades and empty search strings.md

title: Text repair CLI does not enforce separate or immutable output custody
body: Pure repair returns bytes, but CLI accepts arbitrary output and receipt paths without alias checks, allowing input/mapping overwrite or one output replacing another. Receipt binds input/output hashes and version text, not mapping bytes. The test checks only the pure helper leaving input unchanged.
note: 05 Findings/D1354 Text repair CLI does not enforce separate or immutable output custody.md

title: Retrieval readiness can pass without resource measurements
body: Missing p95/memory and missing maxima all default to infinity; infinity <= infinity passes. A pure probe with one perfect case and empty thresholds/metrics/state confirms complete=true with no resource measurements. This is evaluator behavior, not measured performance.
note: 05 Findings/D1355 Retrieval readiness can pass without resource measurements.md

title: Retrieval readiness quality and calibration remain caller assertions
body: Reference/candidate collections are coerced to strings/sets, recall is an unweighted mean with no precision/rank/top-k requirement, and forbidden exposure covers only supplied denied IDs. Numeric bounds/types and finiteness are not fully validated. Compressed readiness checks lifecycle strings and equal fingerprints rather than actual calibration evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1356 Retrieval readiness quality and calibration remain caller assertions.md

title: Incomplete detector collapses all same-file pass sites into one identity
body: ID includes path, rule and normalized semantic_source; for ast.Pass that source is always Pass(). Line and function context are absent. Multiple pass nodes in one file therefore share an ID and the unique dictionary keeps the last locator. Confirmed in memory with two separate functions. source_hash argument is unused.
note: 05 Findings/D1357 Incomplete detector collapses all same-file pass sites into one identity.md

title: Incomplete signal detection is broader and narrower than unfinished behavior
body: Pass can be deliberate control flow, and lexical TODO/unimplemented strings include tests/documentation. Bare raise NotImplementedError is not the AST Call branch but can match lexical text; ellipsis detection requires a one-statement body. Signal review is necessary and absence is not proof of fully implemented behavior.
note: 05 Findings/D1358 Incomplete signal detection is broader and narrower than unfinished behavior.md

title: Incomplete audit omits excluded and oversized sources from completion
body: Custody/generated directories and nonselected/large/link files are skipped without full physical denominator. os.walk traversal failures are unreported; stat and initial raw read occur outside the catch. Python AST reparses the file in a second read, while lexical rules use prior bytes, allowing version mismatch during mutation.
note: 05 Findings/D1359 Incomplete audit omits excluded and oversized sources from completion.md

title: Incomplete review matching validates labels rather than the review condition
body: Reviews bind ID/path/rule while ignoring line movement, require an allowed class plus nonempty rationale/condition, and reject stale IDs. They do not evaluate review_condition, verify an accountable owner or bind whole source bytes. A same-ID new pass site can inherit an earlier classification because of the context-free ID.
note: 05 Findings/D1360 Incomplete review matching validates labels rather than the review condition.md

title: Historical incomplete disposition can complete with missing source
body: First matching path-glob rule supplies arbitrary disposition and targets. Missing source is a recorded flag, not an unresolved condition. Any assigned disposition except literal unresolved can satisfy completion if row count matches; empty targets are accepted. No fresh detector or original-content comparison is run.
note: 05 Findings/D1361 Historical incomplete disposition can complete with missing source.md

title: Historical incomplete reconciliation trusts paths and later input hashes
body: Source path is joined without containment/physical-file checks, and current hashes are cached by path. Report/policy are loaded before later hashing for output, with no stability check. Default CLI can exit zero on incomplete accounting unless require-complete is supplied.
note: 05 Findings/D1362 Historical incomplete reconciliation trusts paths and later input hashes.md

title: Source audit coverage digest has three explicit evidence strengths
body: Included source binds content SHA. Ordinary excluded generated boundaries bind path/size metadata with bounded scandir and errors. Opaque external/preserved/explicit exclusions bind only boundary path identity without recursion. Equal-byte-size changes under metadata exclusions intentionally preserve that digest; opaque contents are not counted as files.
note: 05 Findings/D1363 Source audit coverage digest has three explicit evidence strengths.md

title: Included source traversal is less strict than excluded metadata traversal
body: Ordinary excluded metadata walk retains scandir errors and rejects a linked boundary. Main included os.walk has no onerror, and later nonregular/disappeared paths can silently continue. Included symlinks increase a skip count but do not enter the inventory digest like nested excluded symlinks do. An opaque boundary is selected before the ordinary symlink check.
note: 05 Findings/D1364 Included source traversal is less strict than excluded metadata traversal.md

title: Source audit nominal max bytes is a review threshold not an I/O cap
body: Text above max_bytes but <=8MiB is still line-scanned; above fixed 8MiB is content-hashed only. Those hash-only files still increment text_scanned. Nontext files are hashed without mechanism analysis. No total file/byte/depth/time cap bounds the included walk and retained path list.
note: 05 Findings/D1365 Source audit nominal max bytes is a review threshold not an I/O cap.md

title: Mechanism scan uses combined lexical matches rather than semantic independence
body: Combined regex emits nonoverlapping matches and alternation order can hide a second mechanism matching the same span. It scans line by line with replacement decoding, so cross-line patterns are not found. Declared prefilter/individual-regex/overlap tables are not used by the active _scan_text path. Metadata names/descriptions inspect only the first 12000 bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1366 Mechanism scan uses combined lexical matches rather than semantic independence.md

title: Source audit records retain candidates rather than every hashed file
body: Only score/skill/oversize-positive text produces records; other included file identities contribute only to aggregate inventory hash. Duplicate candidate groups are limited to those retained records. candidate_count counts review dispositions, and complete only means no retained errors even when candidates remain. Catalog match uses token Jaccard similarity, not semantic equivalence or admission.
note: 05 Findings/D1367 Source audit records retain candidates rather than every hashed file.md

title: Source progress complete is positional rather than final validity
body: Progress can mark complete when last selected content iteration finishes even with retained errors. Early continues for nontext/skipped paths can bypass updates, leaving stale incomplete progress when the last path is skipped. No final unconditional receipt corrects this. Progress file created under source before walking can enter and change during its own audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1368 Source progress complete is positional rather than final validity.md

title: Source audit progress replacement is atomic per file but not a durable transaction
body: Progress uses a deterministic .tmp path and os.replace without exclusive creation, fsync, lock or finally cleanup. Final report writes directly. Stat/hash/metadata reads are not an immutable snapshot. CLI allow-errors can exit zero while complete remains false, and printed excluded count uses a key not populated by the coverage counters.
note: 05 Findings/D1369 Source audit progress replacement is atomic per file but not a durable transaction.md

title: Excluded entry budget is checked after each directory is materialized
body: Excluded scanner sorts the entire scandir iterator before incrementing visited_entries and applying its million-entry bound. It limits processed entries but does not cap a single directory listing allocation. Its metadata methods can race directory replacement; no stable physical handle or second tree equality is retained.
note: 05 Findings/D1370 Excluded entry budget is checked after each directory is materialized.md

title: Legacy helper tests support bounded cases rather than universal completion
body: The full capability-mining test module checks meaningful preserved-custody, excluded-body nonread, error, hidden-lock, symlink, progress and historical disposition cases. It does not cover main included traversal failure, self-mutating progress, ID collisions, broad detector precision or policy semantic authority. Retrieval tests similarly omit missing measurement defaults.
note: 05 Findings/D1371 Legacy helper tests support bounded cases rather than universal completion.md

title: Historical hash matches override current owner inspection
body: Historical evidence is indexed by any 64-character source hash, without validating disposition, owner, path or original bytes. A matching hash is accepted before examining a current owner, including historical unresolved or arbitrary labels. The report complete flag counts only literal unresolved rows.
note: 05 Findings/D1372 Historical hash matches override current owner inspection.md

title: Any changed same-path file becomes a superseding owner
body: When historical hash lookup misses, any existing current-root/source-path file becomes current_owner_exact if equal or current_owner_superseded if different. Changed content is automatically considered superseding without a policy rule or semantic evidence. First matching explicit rules apply only after this path lookup misses.
note: 05 Findings/D1373 Any changed same-path file becomes a superseding owner.md

title: Historical reconciliation input hashes are later observations
body: Source inventory paths and rule owner paths have no physical containment guard; lexical parent traversal and links can resolve outside the root. Most helpers parse input first and hash the path later, so mutable bytes can produce a digest unrelated to parsed data. Direct output writes and optional require-complete exit policies do not provide atomic or immutable custody.
note: 05 Findings/D1374 Historical reconciliation input hashes are later observations.md

title: Skill identity joins use metadata rather than body equivalence
body: Inventory and structured-text IDs are dictionaries with last duplicate wins. Canonical identity uses frontmatter name or parent path and catalog name membership, ignoring source body, catalog state and package hashes. A root SKILL.md without a name can raise IndexError. Completion compares matched metadata count with deduplicated skill count.
note: 05 Findings/D1375 Skill identity joins use metadata rather than body equivalence.md

title: Skill alias and vendor routes have different target checks
body: All declared specialty and alias targets are checked against catalog IDs, even unrelated entries, but empty lists pass and delivery/disposition labels are not validated. Vendor-prefix matches emit two hardcoded owner names without checking their catalog presence. Metadata can therefore complete without an active executable owner.
note: 05 Findings/D1376 Skill alias and vendor routes have different target checks.md

title: Classified asset identity joins do not preserve row identity
body: Classified IDs must occur in inventory and be unique, but their path, source tree and digest are not compared with inventory. Policy dictionaries update the result directly and may replace identity/hash/class fields. Skill dispositions join by ID alone, independent of either input hash or upstream complete flag.
note: 05 Findings/D1377 Classified asset identity joins do not preserve row identity.md

title: Unresolved upstream skill labels escape the asset unresolved counter
body: A skill disposition unresolved becomes skill_body_unresolved, while the aggregate only counts unresolved_class plus missing inventory IDs. Other arbitrary policy dispositions likewise avoid that counter. Complete asset accounting can therefore coexist with unresolved skill ownership.
note: 05 Findings/D1378 Unresolved upstream skill labels escape the asset unresolved counter.md

title: Direct audit attachment and optional error logs are not global closure
body: Direct audit records attach by declared source hash without validating audit completeness or outcome. The entire audit file is rehashed inside each record loop. Error logs are optional supplied files; omitted logs are not reconciled against an original summary. Error rule labels and exact default-label comparison drive completion.
note: 05 Findings/D1379 Direct audit attachment and optional error logs are not global closure.md

title: Mechanism ownership requires keys but not owners
body: Every mechanism key must occur in mappings, but a mapped empty target list passes. Owner names, catalog lifecycle, source bytes, record uniqueness and scanner complete/errors are not checked. Expected count is caller candidate_count plus no_reusable_signal records, rather than an independent physical denominator.
note: 05 Findings/D1380 Mechanism ownership requires keys but not owners.md

title: Oversize reconciliation relabels without scanning source bytes
body: An oversize_review_required record with no missing mapping key becomes oversize_stream_scanned_and_mapped. This helper never opens the original source, so the new label does not establish a scan. CLI emits incomplete reports with exit zero unless require-complete is set.
note: 05 Findings/D1381 Oversize reconciliation relabels without scanning source bytes.md

title: Planning coverage proves path existence with an optional denominator
body: Allowed status labels and PC IDs are checked, and owner/test arrays need existing files, but there is no containment, content hash or test execution. Source comparison is optional and recognizes only level-two PC headings. Duplicate source headings collapse in set comparison; empty records with no source pass. Input hashes are taken after parsing.
note: 05 Findings/D1382 Planning coverage proves path existence with an optional denominator.md

title: Staged policy enforces unique highest priority with a narrow absence rule
body: Duplicate typed identities, no rules, equal top priorities, invalid dispositions and unknown owners fail. The absent-body rule rejects only ADOPT and SUPERSEDE when presence exactly equals manifest-only; other labels and presence strings are not schema-validated. A null kind/id becomes a nonempty string through coercion. Catalog names are checked, not active bodies.
note: 05 Findings/D1383 Staged policy enforces unique highest priority with a narrow absence rule.md

title: Staged disposition preserves obligations without executing them
body: Rationale, preserve lists and tests_required are copied from policy; they are not validated as evidence or executed. Empty candidate input can complete. CLI strict completion is optional, and reported input hashes are later reads. This is policy accounting, not capability admission.
note: 05 Findings/D1384 Staged disposition preserves obligations without executing them.md

title: Manifest recovery ledger is a supplied-claim projection
body: The producer intersects supplied missing_paths with manifest rows and copies expected sizes/hashes without inspecting physical files or comparing input provenance. Paths absent from the manifest are omitted; duplicate manifest rows remain. Artifact type comes from first path substring match, so nested scripts under skills classify as skill-component.
note: 05 Findings/D1385 Manifest recovery ledger is a supplied-claim projection.md

title: Empty missing backlog fails after output creation begins
body: CSV fieldnames are taken from rows[0] after the CSV file is opened for writing. Zero missing rows raises IndexError and can leave a truncated file. Markdown is written later, and CLI compares row count with declared missing count only after both outputs; there is no paired atomic publication.
note: 05 Findings/D1386 Empty missing backlog fails after output creation begins.md

title: Reconstruction planner binds a historical fixed denominator
body: Only absent packs 01 through 07 and registry enter the missing set. Candidate count and recovery dictionary count must equal 260 and assigned paths 1133. Duplicate missing paths and multiply assigned paths fail, but slug-generated card IDs are not independently checked for collisions. Other pack declarations are outside this planner.
note: 05 Findings/D1387 Reconstruction planner binds a historical fixed denominator.md

title: Exact recovery branch trusts supplied flags and can accept an empty list
body: Candidates with no missing paths are accepted when every supplied recovery row has exact_match truthy; bytes are not rehashed. With an empty sources list, both all checks pass vacuously. For candidates with some missing paths, other sources outside that set are filtered out without the exact-recovery check.
note: 05 Findings/D1388 Exact recovery branch trusts supplied flags and can accept an empty list.md

title: Support consolidation infers behavior from names
body: Unassigned support paths group by artifact kind and slugged filename, with pack qualification only for certain kinds. Cross-pack contracts can therefore consolidate by stem. Behavior, targets and test filenames are generated strings, and the selected canonical owner is not checked for current existence or semantic equivalence.
note: 05 Findings/D1389 Support consolidation infers behavior from names.md

title: Reconstruction waves declare order without executing it
body: The planner writes eight static waves and acceptance prose with all cards initially assigned_not_verified. It does not construct an executable dependency graph, verify target wiring or run tests. Generated JSON/Markdown do not bind input digests and are written independently.
note: 05 Findings/D1390 Reconstruction waves declare order without executing it.md

title: Historical certifier checks generic plans and script dispatch
body: The certifier asks every outcome for a positive and missing-constraints plan. Scripts additionally run with one shared synthetic payload. The runtime dispatches generic handlers by outcome words; skill/orchestration plans do not execute their domain procedures. Temporary sample creation occurs even without apply, so this command is not a purely read-only checker.
note: 05 Findings/D1391 Historical certifier checks generic plans and script dispatch.md

title: Repeated script certification omits second validity
body: The script check requires first.valid true and equal first/second result_sha256, but does not require second.valid true or a nonempty result hash. Its determinism claim is consequently narrower than two independently valid executions.
note: 05 Findings/D1392 Repeated script certification omits second validity.md

title: Support card certification does not evaluate per-card acceptance
body: Support_ready checks fixed 18/3/257 registry counts, global contract validity and target existence. Directories can count as present, and missing implementation_targets entries are not independently required. Card required_tests, wiring_targets, behavior contract and acceptance text are not evaluated in this branch.
note: 05 Findings/D1393 Support card certification does not evaluate per-card acceptance.md

title: Historical final gates trust supplied aggregate fields
body: Final readiness accepts historical minimum test counters, booleans and failed-zero fields. It hashes the supplied gate file but does not validate source revision, installed artifact identity, execution logs, timestamps or current processing-order receipts. This legacy helper is distinct from current governed release certification.
note: 05 Findings/D1394 Historical final gates trust supplied aggregate fields.md

title: Certifier hashes evidence before later replacing it
body: Evidence cards inspect and hash their target before apply may regenerate pack evidence. First application cannot create a missing target and count it in the same preceding check; existing recorded hashes can describe bytes replaced later. Invalid cards are not reset from a prior implemented_verified state, so persisted states can disagree with fresh counters.
note: 05 Findings/D1395 Certifier hashes evidence before later replacing it.md

title: Certifier valid status and card closure are independent
body: Summary valid and exit success depend only on accumulated errors; invalid support/evidence cards can remain open without adding errors. Receipt status depends only on open count and can say complete despite unrelated errors. The helper has no single predicate combining all closure obligations.
note: 05 Findings/D1396 Certifier valid status and card closure are independent.md

title: Failed certification can still publish certified owner states
body: Confirmed with extracted main and all I/O intercepted in memory: one invalid operational card and an error produce valid=false, one open card and exit 1, yet passing final fields write implemented_verified owners/recovery and certified packs. Apply publication is guarded by final_ready, not global success. Nineteen synthetic writes were intercepted; no product state was changed. Sequential publication has no WAL or joint rollback.
note: 05 Findings/D1397 Failed certification can still publish certified owner states.md

title: Reconciliation fixtures leave cross-helper authority gaps
body: Mechanism tests cover unknown versus named mapping; staged tests cover one MERGE, manifest ADOPT denial and priority tie; reconstruction tests cover 260/1133 synthetic assignment and retained 375-card receipts/current package body hashes. Existing support tests call validate_operational, not main publication. These useful assertions do not establish end-to-end semantic reconstruction or failed-apply safety.
note: 05 Findings/D1398 Reconciliation fixtures leave cross-helper authority gaps.md

title: Sort JSON streaming does not preserve JSON token boundaries
body: Confirmed using in-memory readers: [12345] at chunk size two yields three records [1,23,45]. raw_decode accepts a numeric prefix before the next chunk arrives. The parser also accepts missing/repeated/leading/trailing commas and ignores text after the closing bracket; [,1 2,,,] ignored yields [1,2].
note: 05 Findings/D1399 Sort JSON streaming does not preserve JSON token boundaries.md

title: Sort sample bounds do not bound total parsing work
body: Reservoir record count is bounded, but the entire source stream is parsed and type-checked and later fully hashed. A single huge record or incomplete JSON value can grow the buffer without a byte limit. No input size, deadline or candidate timeout is enforced.
note: 05 Findings/D1400 Sort sample bounds do not bound total parsing work.md

title: Sort coercion and type policy distinguish compatible numeric shapes
body: Every key must have exactly the same Python type, so int/float mixtures fail even when numerically ordered. String coercion applies only to strings; number policy leaves existing integers unchanged. Boolean keys are allowed only as a homogeneous class. Auto coercion can retain non-finite-looking strings as text after numeric conversion fails.
note: 05 Findings/D1401 Sort coercion and type policy distinguish compatible numeric shapes.md

title: Reservoir replacement changes stability requirements for specialized sorts
body: Reference comparison sorts use original source ordinal as tiebreaker. Reservoir replacement does not keep the sample in ordinal order. Counting and radix preserve sample order within equal keys, and all-equal bucket sort returns sample unchanged, so those candidates can fail the declared reference after sampling despite ordinary stable behavior on their input order.
note: 05 Findings/D1402 Reservoir replacement changes stability requirements for specialized sorts.md

title: Numeric sort compatibility is not a full resource or precision gate
body: Counting sort has a span limit, but radix passes scale with integer magnitude and bucket conversion may overflow huge integers or overflow finite float ranges. Exceptions are captured as failed candidate evidence. quick-3way compares key plus unique ordinal, so duplicate scalar keys do not form a large equal partition.
note: 05 Findings/D1403 Numeric sort compatibility is not a full resource or precision gate.md

title: Sort correctness checks ordinal order without payload preservation
body: Confirmed in memory: replacing key1/payload-original with key99/payload-changed at the same ordinal passes validate_output for a one-record reference. The validator compares length, ordinal sequence and output tie stability, not keys or payload equality. Candidate list copies are shallow and can share nested records.
note: 05 Findings/D1404 Sort correctness checks ordinal order without payload preservation.md

title: Direct zero-repeat benchmark reports success without running a candidate
body: CLI enforces repeats1-25, but public benchmark/build_receipt do not validate it. A direct zero-repeat benchmark returns correct=true and stable=true with empty timings and null median/p95. The in-memory probe verified the candidate function was never called.
note: 05 Findings/D1405 Direct zero-repeat benchmark reports success without running a candidate.md

title: Sort ranking measures a fixed pilot and three finalists
body: Pilot is the first at most4096 reservoir slots, one run per candidate in fixed order; only three correct pilots advance. Final choice uses fastest correct/stable median. No warmup, order randomization, uncertainty, memory measurement or runtime fingerprint is retained. A deterministic sample does not imply deterministic timing/winner.
note: 05 Findings/D1406 Sort ranking measures a fixed pilot and three finalists.md

title: Sort receipt fingerprints can follow different source bytes
body: Sampling and benchmarking precede input stat and full SHA read, so mutable input can diverge from sampled records. Sample hash includes only keys and ordinals, not payloads. Output can alias the input and overwrite it despite dry_run=true, because no separate output identity is enforced.
note: 05 Findings/D1407 Sort receipt fingerprints can follow different source bytes.md

title: Model normalization selects first alias and infers defaults
body: First present alias wins even if null; contradictory aliases are not compared. Hidden/query/KV divisibility is checked and missing KV heads default to query heads with a warning. Explicit head_dim and architecture-specific projection dimensions are not consumed; returned formulas use hidden/query.
note: 05 Findings/D1408 Model normalization selects first alias and infers defaults.md

title: Model parameter estimates are a simplified dense formula
body: Parameter count uses standard attention projections, two or three FFN matrices and embedding/norm assumptions. Expert count changes only an active fraction, not total FFN weight parameters. Unknown activation is treated as gated, and truthy tie_word_embeddings strings affect embedding count. These are estimates, not a loaded-model inventory.
note: 05 Findings/D1409 Model parameter estimates are a simplified dense formula.md

title: Architecture status mixes missing optional fields and unknown strings
body: Unresolved includes None fields such as absent expert metadata even for a dense model, while unknown model/position/norm/activation strings are not unresolved. Context limits do not reject a requested token count above configured context. Required_runtime_validation remains an unevaluated list.
note: 05 Findings/D1410 Architecture status mixes missing optional fields and unknown strings.md

title: Architecture input checks have conditional and falsy paths
body: Falsy non-dict workloads such as an empty list are accepted through workload or {}. bits_per_weight is validated only if all parameter-estimate dimensions are present. Public arithmetic helpers themselves do not enforce the inspect integer bounds. CLI can emit review status with normal success and does not bind source config bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1411 Architecture input checks have conditional and falsy paths.md

title: Deployment planner accepts non-finite numbers and truthy strings
body: Numeric validation rejects negative values and booleans but not NaN/infinity. Architecture, streaming, privacy and remote flags use bool coercion rather than boolean types. Confirmed supplied strings false for architecture_supported and remote_fallback_allowed produce native feasible and remote conditional under fitting memory; no effects occur.
note: 05 Findings/D1412 Deployment planner accepts non-finite numbers and truthy strings.md

title: Deployment feasibility omits some artifact and cache prerequisites
body: Missing KV cache defaults zero. A transformed weight size zero falls back to original size. Disk preflight gates streaming only; native/quantized/offload can be labeled feasible or conditional with failed disk budget. Streaming does not check minimum working memory or task throughput, and zero model weights are accepted.
note: 05 Findings/D1413 Deployment feasibility omits some artifact and cache prerequisites.md

title: Deployment complete means only bandwidth metadata is present
body: The only blocking_unknowns entry is missing sustained_disk_read_mib_s. Supplying zero marks complete even with failed disk preflight and unmeasured compatibility/quality. Rankings use fixed strategy scores and heuristic memory fractions. Required validation and global release lists are declarations, not receipts.
note: 05 Findings/D1414 Deployment complete means only bandwidth metadata is present.md

title: Model estimate and deployment schemas require an explicit handoff
body: Architecture helper emits parameter/byte estimates from config; deployment helper expects separate hardware/model/workload GiB and support flags. Neither imports or calls the other, converts units or probes actual hardware. Both remain nonexecuting planning helpers, distinct from local model admission/server owners.
note: 05 Findings/D1415 Model estimate and deployment schemas require an explicit handoff.md

title: Sort and model fixtures exercise selected formulas and policies
body: Sort tests cover seeded JSONL sampling, CSV conversion and mixed-key rejection. Model tests cover MHA KV arithmetic, two dimension errors, private remote denial and missing disk bandwidth. They omit parser chunk/grammar defects, payload preservation, zero direct repeats, MoE sizing, non-finite numbers and string flags. Sources read; tests not run.
note: 05 Findings/D1416 Sort and model fixtures exercise selected formulas and policies.md

title: Behavior extractor privacy is limited identifier substitution
body: Only three configured name patterns are replaced. Source aliases pass through unchanged; headings, test descriptions and frontmatter text are copied with that limited substitution. Those fields can contain private paths or secrets. secret_indicator_count counts words rather than redacting values, so the broad privacy label is not a general sanitization guarantee.
note: 05 Findings/D1417 Behavior extractor privacy is limited identifier substitution.md

title: Behavior extraction reads broad mutable source trees without size bounds
body: It enumerates all is_file paths with rglob and no exclusion policy or error denominator, follows file links, hashes then stats then reads entire text separately. Large files and full record lists are unbounded. Missing/unreadable hash paths abort rather than entering parse_failure_count; changing files can break hash-to-metadata identity.
note: 05 Findings/D1418 Behavior extraction reads broad mutable source trees without size bounds.md

title: Python syntax failure is counted as parsed behavior text
body: The AST symbol extractor catches SyntaxError and returns empty symbol/test lists. The caller still sets parse_status=text_parsed, so parse_failure_count covers only text read failure, not syntactically unparsed Python. Lexical behavior/effect tags may still be emitted.
note: 05 Findings/D1419 Python syntax failure is counted as parsed behavior text.md

title: Behavior metadata extraction has explicit lexical coverage limits
body: JS/TS regexes omit many arrow/property/method forms; PowerShell matching is line-based; Markdown frontmatter is a simple single-line name/description regex. Symbols/tests are truncated to500 and headings100 without a truncation receipt. Whole-text substrings detect effects without resolving actual calls, and can count comments or miss equivalent syntax.
note: 05 Findings/D1420 Behavior metadata extraction has explicit lexical coverage limits.md

title: Behavior tree identity depends on aliases and sanitized path strings
body: Tree digest concatenates alias:path:hash lines in caller root order after path sanitization. Aliases/delimiters are not constrained and normalized path collisions are not rejected. The digest does not bind extractor version or extraction configuration. Output inside a scanned tree can enter later scans.
note: 05 Findings/D1421 Behavior tree identity depends on aliases and sanitized path strings.md

title: Content-addressed extraction is not an atomic multi-file publication
body: Destination mkdir uses exist_ok=false, so repeated identical input fails rather than verifies/reuses existing output. Index is created exclusively, but later summary/candidate/duplicate files are separate writes; interruption leaves a partial directory that blocks a same-digest rerun. CLI returns zero even with text-read failures.
note: 05 Findings/D1422 Content-addressed extraction is not an atomic multi-file publication.md

title: Exact metadata names can claim existing semantic coverage
body: Confirmed _catalog_match returns score1 for an identical normalized name despite unrelated tokens and deferred catalog state. Jaccard token equality can also return1. build_plan calls score1 already_covered_exact, without body, behavior or active-admission verification. At zero overlap the nearest owner still becomes the lexicographically first catalog ID.
note: 05 Findings/D1423 Exact metadata names can claim existing semantic coverage.md

title: Staged priority is selected by a hardcoded source alias
body: Only source-12 gets clean_room_contract_candidate for unmatched recognized families and enters priority_staged_candidates. Alias is caller-controlled metadata, not a provenance or authority check. Family and match decisions use token overlap with deterministic lexical tie-breaking, not semantic review.
note: 05 Findings/D1424 Staged priority is selected by a hardcoded source alias.md

title: Admission plan trusts supplied index identity and denominators
body: Summary tree_sha256 and file_count are copied without recomputing the behavior-index or joining candidate rows to source records. Catalog hash is read after catalog parsing. The output plan hash binds generated content, but does not prove input consistency or current source equivalence.
note: 05 Findings/D1425 Admission plan trusts supplied index identity and denominators.md

title: Metadata duplicate grouping does not validate source hash identities
body: Planner groups str(item.get(sha256, empty)) without digest grammar or row uniqueness checks. Missing/default and null values differ; a null becomes the nonempty string None and can form a duplicate group. Duplicate source rows remain separate candidates. Repeated same plan output fails at exclusive directory creation.
note: 05 Findings/D1426 Metadata duplicate grouping does not validate source hash identities.md

title: External requirement integration is a fixed filename mapping
body: Only source-12 records enter; rule files use the exact persistant_rules prefix and first two stem characters, while SKILL.md uses its parent name. Fixed RULE_OWNERS/SKILL_OWNERS membership plus catalog IDs decides integrated/reference labels. It does not inspect original behavior, package hashes or active catalog status.
note: 05 Findings/D1427 External requirement integration is a fixed filename mapping.md

title: External requirement cards have positional rather than stable identity
body: Card IDs use sorted record sequence, so adding an earlier path renumbers subsequent cards. Duplicate paths/rows and declared hash grammar are not checked. validation=complete follows integrated/reference labels, and bool(cards) only prevents vacuous empty completion.
note: 05 Findings/D1428 External requirement cards have positional rather than stable identity.md

title: External disposition digest does not bind its input artifacts
body: The digest covers produced cards but omits index and catalog file digests. Report can remain unchanged across different unreferenced catalog/index content. Content-addressed output uses exclusive creation and CLI returns zero even when complete=false and cards are blocked.
note: 05 Findings/D1429 External disposition digest does not bind its input artifacts.md

title: Mining migration mutates catalog before confirming skill bodies
body: update_catalog runs first; missing body later raises after catalog mutation and perhaps earlier package writes. Packages list resources from scripts/references/assets, excluding bytecode but without resource hashes or link containment. Existing package files are overwritten with fixed version/status/effects rather than reconciled through an admission transaction.
note: 05 Findings/D1430 Mining migration mutates catalog before confirming skill bodies.md

title: Catalog text matching is narrower than TOML identity
body: The migration detects existing IDs only with an exact double-quoted id = line regex. Equivalent TOML quoting/spacing can be missed and append duplicates; an existing matched entry is not updated for status/body/version changes. Catalog is rewritten even if no new entry was added.
note: 05 Findings/D1431 Catalog text matching is narrower than TOML identity.md

title: Mining admission writes success and freshness claims without executing validation
body: Every fixed skill receives active status, validation passed2/failed0 and package validation_freshness=current. Five scan receipts and their counts/hashes are constants. The script does not invoke those tests, verify raw scan reports or establish current operational behavior before publishing these labels.
note: 05 Findings/D1432 Mining admission writes success and freshness claims without executing validation.md

title: Mining migration refreshes every package body digest
body: After the fixed wave and lifecycle updates, every registry/skill_packages JSON is loaded and its declared body read and hash replaced. This extends mutation beyond the twenty added skills, follows unguarded body paths and does not compare expected previous hashes or validation freshness. A failure late in this sweep retains prior writes.
note: 05 Findings/D1433 Mining migration refreshes every package body digest.md

title: Mining workflow definitions preserve order but do not execute it
body: Five workflows declare assimilation, secure service release, retrieval readiness, failure/recovery and external tool lifecycle. Assimilation branches incompleteness/relationships/boundaries after inventory, derive waits on relationships/boundaries, certify waits on incompleteness/derive. Other chains are linear. Producer replaces the whole workflow registry and emits a JSON-shaped YAML projection; it does not schedule the steps.
note: 05 Findings/D1434 Mining workflow definitions preserve order but do not execute it.md

title: Mining receipt uses historical maximum coverage and fixed oversize disposition
body: The receipt uses the maximum declared scan file count and separately sums focused observations, correctly avoiding naive additive coverage claims but not verifying nested membership or raw hashes. Fixed411 oversize records are labeled reference_only. Receipt hashes the generated admission registry; that proves document identity, not source reconstruction.
note: 05 Findings/D1435 Mining receipt uses historical maximum coverage and fixed oversize disposition.md

title: Mining publication can stop between independently written control surfaces
body: Order is catalog; per-skill packages; admission ledger; mining admission; workflow registry/projection; mining receipt; source coverage; engineering lifecycle; every package hash refresh. Direct writes have no joint preflight, lock, WAL or rollback, and overwrite retained wave entries. Idempotent wording does not imply transactional recovery or preservation of newer metadata.
note: 05 Findings/D1436 Mining publication can stop between independently written control surfaces.md

title: Contract ID normalization rewrites identifiers without reconciling consumers
body: All contracts/**/*.json are treated as schema objects. A changed ID requires $schema and otherwise raises after earlier writes; already matching ID skips that check. The path-derived URI is written directly, without updating absolute references, registries or provenance hashes or validating schema compatibility. Missing contracts directory returns zero changes.
note: 05 Findings/D1437 Contract ID normalization rewrites identifiers without reconciling consumers.md

title: External intake fixtures do not validate all claims in their names
body: Extractor test checks one Python symbol/body-marker fixture, planner test uses an arbitrary supplied tree hash and inspects nonexecution flags, and staged requirement test reads retained75-card/6353-file counts without rebuilding owner dispositions. It does not execute the fixed admission migration or check broad metadata privacy.
note: 05 Findings/D1438 External intake fixtures do not validate all claims in their names.md

title: Downstream assimilation validation remains a declaration check
body: The consumer verifies scan IDs, positive counts, complete/error fields and hash grammar; target catalog membership; selectable workflow skills; dependency identities and acyclicity; and admission document hash/maximum denominator. It does not open the raw scan reports or execute the declared skill workflows, so producer constants remain claims at this boundary.
note: 05 Findings/D1439 Downstream assimilation validation remains a declaration check.md

title: CLI parser and dispatch denominators are independently accounted
body: Pure parser construction yields69 top-level commands and169 leaf parsers. AST inspection finds a corresponding top-level dispatch branch for every command. Leaf count retains positional action choices rather than counting them as executed routes. Hardcoded section/profile choices are an additional CLI exposure boundary over registry data.
note: 05 Findings/D1440 CLI parser and dispatch denominators are independently accounted.md

title: Four CLI paths fail on a branch-local JSON loader
body: Confirmed with unchanged main AST and intercepted dependencies: declared-suite plan, declared-suite run-script, metacognitive run and scheduling simulate raise UnboundLocalError before invoking their owner. load_json is imported inside other mutually exclusive branches, making it a local variable not initialized in these paths. The exception is not in the CLI JSON-error catch tuple.
note: 05 Findings/D1441 Four CLI paths fail on a branch-local JSON loader.md

title: Startup emits a tooling command that the parser rejects
body: Startup guidance emits python -m runtime.cli tooling --project path, but tooling requires the assess subcommand. Pure parser probe returns exit2 for that emitted shape. Existing startup test checks deferred metadata but does not parse or execute its suggested command.
note: 05 Findings/D1442 Startup emits a tooling command that the parser rejects.md

title: CLI argument semantics vary across command families
body: Several file inputs are interpreted from process cwd while others are rebased under framework or project root. plan --effect appends to the default read_local list. skill-backup --verify is parsed but not consulted; default nonrestore path always verifies. audit --write-report affects licensing only. These distinctions are retained in the complete argument index.
note: 05 Findings/D1443 CLI argument semantics vary across command families.md

title: Processing project mutation can use a different orchestration lock root
body: Confirmed in isolated main: the orchestration lock receives framework root, while processing-order --project claim-release-stage passes the selected project root to the release owner. This does not remove the release owner own state checks/locks, but the repository-wide orchestration exclusion is not scoped to that mutated project.
note: 05 Findings/D1444 Processing project mutation can use a different orchestration lock root.md

title: Inherited test ownership is restricted to one immediate stale-group child
body: Only run-stale with matching owner and supervised-child environment values requests inherited ownership. The child marker is removed after claim so descendants cannot reuse that one-generation path. Managed project group runs additionally require an active exact full_profile claim, inspected structurally without rehashing live source.
note: 05 Findings/D1445 Inherited test ownership is restricted to one immediate stale-group child.md

title: Stale-group child timeout expands to cover the full queue
body: Refresh finds noncurrent groups, requires each in registered topology and uses max(requested timeout,sum group timeouts plus max60 or15 seconds per group). It launches one owned run-stale child with three workers and aggregate disk budget. This is intentionally larger than a single profile budget, not a global wall-time cap shared with the subsequent coexistence run.
note: 05 Findings/D1446 Stale-group child timeout expands to cover the full queue.md

title: Stale-group resource closure is scoped to newly unresolved identities
body: Baseline unresolved ephemeral IDs are excluded from the final new-resource check. Late current/parent PIDs and exact release-owner run/lane identities are also exempted. Reconciliation can return globally invalid while refresh succeeds when only prior/exempt resources remain. This is a scoped closure predicate, not a claim that the entire resource ledger is clean.
note: 05 Findings/D1447 Stale-group resource closure is scoped to newly unresolved identities.md

title: Contained child failure is interpreted through fresh group receipts
body: An exited, tree-terminated, nontimed-out child can have valid=false/exit1 without immediately aborting refresh. The owner checks receipt freshness, then returns all fresh failed groups. Full profile still runs cross-group checks and forces final valid=false if that failure list is nonempty. Noncontainment and unresolved new resources fail earlier.
note: 05 Findings/D1448 Contained child failure is interpreted through fresh group receipts.md

title: Section owner invalidates the aggregate before launching work
body: Section execution first requires processing stage and current dependencies, then writes a failing in-progress aggregate receipt before any child launch. This prevents an older passing section receipt from surviving an interrupted attempt as current authority. Final receipt follows all reused/executed chunks.
note: 05 Findings/D1449 Section owner invalidates the aggregate before launching work.md

title: Section chunk reuse depends on stored receipt integrity and declared input hash
body: Caller reuses only passed receipts matching section, chunk ID and input_sha256. The reader separately checks exact keys/schema, member count, bounded output-evidence shape and an unkeyed content digest. Reuse is tied to declared inputs and retained evidence; it is not a fresh execution or an authenticated external attestation.
note: 05 Findings/D1450 Section chunk reuse depends on stored receipt integrity and declared input hash.md

title: Section chunk scheduling preserves all pending results rather than failing fast
body: All pending chunks are submitted under max_parallel_chunks and individual timeouts. Worker Exceptions become failing chunk receipts while siblings continue. Aggregate duration measures scheduling time; no separate aggregate deadline or cancellation-on-first-failure exists here. BaseException and failure while publishing the failure receipt escape this per-worker conversion.
note: 05 Findings/D1451 Section chunk scheduling preserves all pending results rather than failing fast.md

title: Group reruns do not invalidate prior group receipts before execution
body: Unlike sections, execute_group checks index freshness, runs the child, then writes the group receipt. A failure before that write can leave an older passing receipt untouched. Direct run can select an already current group, so interruption semantics differ between group and section owners.
note: 05 Findings/D1452 Group reruns do not invalidate prior group receipts before execution.md

title: Group scheduling can stop before collecting the full selected denominator
body: Parallel-safe futures are consumed with future.result without a per-group exception conversion, followed by serial groups. An exception in one future causes pool context shutdown and exits before later serial execution; other completed receipts may exist without a complete result report. Ordinary returned failed executions do not take this exception path.
note: 05 Findings/D1453 Group scheduling can stop before collecting the full selected denominator.md

title: Completion projection refresh has a specific place in serial group order
body: The CLI writes completion projection immediately before a serial group containing test_completion_status.py, and once after the serial loop if any selected group contains that member. Parallel-safe groups run first. The second refresh occurs after all serial group receipts, not necessarily immediately after the derived-integrity group.
note: 05 Findings/D1454 Completion projection refresh has a specific place in serial group order.md

title: Full profile claim precedes section validation and uses required group status
body: Full/release claims full_profile before checking current section receipts, so later gate failure follows the failed-stage path. group_status.valid only checks configured required groups; if those are current, optional noncurrent groups do not trigger refresh. The executed profile command becomes the cross-group coexistence command, rather than the original full member command.
note: 05 Findings/D1455 Full profile claim precedes section validation and uses required group status.md

title: Full-profile refresh keeps freshness and passing status distinct
body: Post-refresh remaining detection tests fresh rather than current so failed fresh receipts can be gathered explicitly. Returned valid depends on failed rows, while status contains the required-group predicate. That status is retained in the profile output; its overall valid is not independently rechecked after refresh before coexistence execution.
note: 05 Findings/D1456 Full-profile refresh keeps freshness and passing status distinct.md

title: Successful release preflight retains the certify claim for finalize
body: Authoritative preflight checks certify processing stage and claims certify once. On valid=true it reports completion_deferred_to release finalize and clears only the local variable, leaving the durable claim. Finalize can reuse matching active certify claim or claim one if absent, then delegates actual artifact finalization.
note: 05 Findings/D1457 Successful release preflight retains the certify claim for finalize.md

title: CLI failure receipts do not cover every exception or final output failure
body: Only OSError, ValueError, KeyError, RuntimeError and JSONDecodeError enter failed-stage handling. TypeError, NameError/UnboundLocalError, KeyboardInterrupt and serialization errors can escape. Finally releases orchestration ownership; output serialization and print occur afterward, following any successful finish_release_stage. A stage can therefore finish before response delivery fails.
note: 05 Findings/D1458 CLI failure receipts do not cover every exception or final output failure.md

title: Registry validation and doctor expose different completion contracts
body: validate returns registry validity with operational_state and certification_claim=false; unavailable completion projection does not change registry valid. It claims ordered validate only when the release-identity pointer file exists, preserving installed registry checking. doctor instead sets exit0/2 from requested syntax/operable/ready/certification-ready predicate.
note: 05 Findings/D1459 Registry validation and doctor expose different completion contracts.md

title: CLI successful evaluation does not always mean an approved decision
body: Claims-only admission/outcome evaluation, authorization simulation and security/hook authority decisions can return valid=true and exit0 for a denied or nonauthoritative decision. Authoritative admission/outcome paths use explicit disposition codes; retry maps allowed to valid. Default output without valid is treated as successful. Consumers must use the command-specific contract.
note: 05 Findings/D1460 CLI successful evaluation does not always mean an approved decision.md

title: Hardware admission fingerprint omits decision-relevant inputs
body: Confirmed isolated dispatch: changing batchable, estimated-device-bytes and operation-id leaves hardware_input identical. Those values are passed to WorkloadProfile but omitted from work identity. The shared work plane can join matching in-flight results, so cache_seconds=0 on route does not make the omitted fields irrelevant to concurrent identity.
note: 05 Findings/D1461 Hardware admission fingerprint omits decision-relevant inputs.md

title: Hardware report caching and timeout are work-plane contracts
body: Hardware report uses a60-second cache while route uses0; both declare a10-second work-plane timeout. The reviewed work plane applies timeout to admission waiting, not interruption of the hardware callback. Benchmark file bytes are fingerprinted separately before the callback parses that file, leaving a mutable-input gap.
note: 05 Findings/D1462 Hardware report caching and timeout are work-plane contracts.md

title: Bounded CLI output does not imply bounded input hydration
body: Visibility ingress caps stdin at4MiB and requires a batch/event-object shape. Most file-based commands read entire JSON/text payloads before owner validation, including transcript record lists. Audit --summary runs the full audit first, then retains counts and at most100 error entries; error strings and hygiene dictionaries are not byte-bounded.
note: 05 Findings/D1463 Bounded CLI output does not imply bounded input hydration.md

title: Visibility ingress chooses its allowed root from caller bus location
body: The CLI resolves --bus-root, chooses its parent as allowed_root and creates that directory before constructing OperationalEventBus. This is a caller-selected publication boundary, not containment under the framework root. Batch validity does not independently confer event authority; the downstream bus owns its checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1464 Visibility ingress chooses its allowed root from caller bus location.md

title: Some descriptive CLI operations publish artifacts without an apply flag
body: Every placement action publishes its result through publish_placement_artifact, including advisory decisions and failed promotion results. Audit always invokes hygiene analysis, with actual application controlled separately; full/release profiles and selected release-audit groups apply hygiene automatically. Tool-intake scan suppresses recording apply but can still execute explicitly requested/approved scanners.
note: 05 Findings/D1465 Some descriptive CLI operations publish artifacts without an apply flag.md

title: Plan effect declarations are descriptive rather than execution authorization
body: plan passes goal and available input labels to navigation, then adds sorted declared_effects and an unload-plan string. Effects are not sent as navigation constraints and no authorization or task execution occurs. Selection, routing, hydration and specialist prompt compilation are distinct branches with different success predicates.
note: 05 Findings/D1466 Plan effect declarations are descriptive rather than execution authorization.md

title: Cognitive freshness validation is confined to status in the CLI
body: All cognitive actions load the index, but only status calls validate_cognitive_index and integration_healthcheck. Query and hydrate-plan use the loaded index directly; run also requires the index file even though dispatch uses a separate facade. Agent list valid is based on matches before limit, so limit0 can return valid=true with no agents.
note: 05 Findings/D1467 Cognitive freshness validation is confined to status in the CLI.md

title: CLI fixtures cover ownership well but leave dispatch and publication gaps
body: Tests exercise real lock exclusion, one-generation ownership, scoped resource exceptions, two concurrent missing chunks, decision codes and selected bounded routes. Four broken loader branches and hardware fingerprint omissions are absent. Preflight/finalize tests assert source strings rather than executing the claim lifecycle. test_bootstrap_cli calls underlying APIs directly, not parser/main. No product tests were run for this report.
note: 05 Findings/D1468 CLI fixtures cover ownership well but leave dispatch and publication gaps.md

title: Pytest plugin loading has two entry paths
body: Root conftest loads tests.pytest_guards for direct discovery, while the governed runner adds explicit -p loading for tests outside that discovery tree. The test package initializer contains only a docstring.
note: 05 Findings/D1469 Pytest plugin loading has two entry paths.md

title: Per-test reclamation inherits ownership rather than checking it
body: The hook resolves the environment marker once and snapshots child names. It does not query the resource ledger, verify a cleanup receipt, bind root identity after yield, or classify every new child. The normal runner supplies a registered workspace; direct calls with an arbitrary marker would rely on that caller assertion. Audit performed no cleanup.
note: 05 Findings/D1470 Per-test reclamation inherits ownership rather than checking it.md

title: Name baselines are not per-test content or producer identity
body: Existing child names are preserved even if their contents change. Every newly named child is selected, including one produced concurrently after the baseline. Directory existence after yield does not establish the same root identity. This is a lifecycle assumption, not demonstrated destructive behavior.
note: 05 Findings/D1471 Name baselines are not per-test content or producer identity.md

title: Cleanup retry is bounded but narrowly typed
body: Only PermissionError receives six attempts with delays totaling2.65 seconds. Nested permission failures chmod entries to read/write before retry; other OSError values propagate to fixture aggregation. Tests cover transient retry, non-permission failure and read-only children, not root replacement or concurrent producers.
note: 05 Findings/D1472 Cleanup retry is bounded but narrowly typed.md

title: Thread leak failure does not terminate leaked threads
body: The shutdown hook compares object IDs of live non-daemon threads with an initial snapshot, prints their names and changes exitstatus. It does not join or stop them and cannot by itself guarantee process exit; preexisting and daemon threads are outside this predicate.
note: 05 Findings/D1473 Thread leak failure does not terminate leaked threads.md

title: Shared pytest base guard observes only a directory during call
body: The runtest_call wrapper obtains the shared base, then recreates it and forces an exception if it is no longer a directory. It does not verify contents, identity, or deletion during all setup/teardown phases.
note: 05 Findings/D1474 Shared pytest base guard observes only a directory during call.md

title: Bytecode suppression has startup timing limits
body: sitecustomize sets sys.dont_write_bytecode when Python loads it. The package initialization test explicitly allows at most one __init__ cache file, showing that later package suppression is not a guarantee of zero startup bytecode. The second test only inspects CLI hygiene call ordering as source text.
note: 05 Findings/D1475 Bytecode suppression has startup timing limits.md

title: Fixture copy preserves selected receipt metadata
