body: canonical_copy_ignore prunes generated patterns, every case-insensitive .lock suffix and external environment paths. The scope test confirms exclusion of local gate fixtures while retaining a current section receipt. Retention is a copy boundary, not a fresh receipt for the clone.
note: 05 Findings/D1476 Fixture copy preserves selected receipt metadata.md

title: Quickstart timeout is per child rather than aggregate
body: Eight sequential CLI calls each have a60-second bound, while the end-to-end test bounds the entire demonstration at90 seconds. No aggregate deadline or registered child-process custody appears in the demo owner; an earlier failure leaves the already-created output tree without the final receipt.
note: 05 Findings/D1477 Quickstart timeout is per child rather than aggregate.md

title: Quickstart validity and selection rely on result shape
body: The demo treats absent valid as true and applies bool to present values, then assumes selection capability_ids has an element. Its framework_validation label contains processing-order status rather than full validation. This is explicitly a pre-validation demonstration.
note: 05 Findings/D1478 Quickstart validity and selection rely on result shape.md

title: Quickstart hash binds an envelope rather than complete effects
body: The canonical unkeyed digest covers the receipt before its digest field. Nested step outputs are retained and may include absolute paths despite the relative project label. changed_paths lists project and receipt, not every possible runtime control-plane write.
note: 05 Findings/D1479 Quickstart hash binds an envelope rather than complete effects.md

title: Declared wrapper is a projected executable template
body: Installed imports take precedence and any ModuleNotFoundError triggers fallback imports after inserting parents[4]. Argument parsing executes at module import. Input JSON is read without a byte bound and malformed shape/owner exceptions are uncaught. The directory-depth assumption belongs to projected wrappers, not arbitrary direct template execution.
note: 05 Findings/D1480 Declared wrapper is a projected executable template.md

title: Supabase scaffold does not implement authentication or idempotent work
body: The handler only requires a nonempty idempotency header and any non-null JavaScript object, including arrays. JWT/signature validation and bounded idempotent work remain comments; the key is echoed without persistence or deduplication. OPTIONS returns before body checks, other methods are not restricted, malformed JSON becomes500, and CORS uses a placeholder origin without an allow-methods header. This is a template, not a deployed service claim.
note: 05 Findings/D1481 Supabase scaffold does not implement authentication or idempotent work.md

title: Ownership tests exercise two declared records
body: The builder tests assert semantic-memory and local-model owners, producer lists, enforcement labels and named tests. They do not invoke those producers or cover every schema-owner entry.
note: 05 Findings/D1482 Ownership tests exercise two declared records.md

title: Graph manifest tests include real rejection paths
body: Ten graph declarations must validate; duplicate path, missing source revisions and a stale graph hash must fail. Distinct purpose strings and ten paths are also asserted. This is stronger than presence-only checks but does not independently inspect all semantics represented by those graphs.
note: 05 Findings/D1483 Graph manifest tests include real rejection paths.md

title: Historical audit test checks presence and a weak status exclusion
body: The retained audit test requires exactly30 unique A01-A30 IDs and zero stored open_count. Each status must omit pending_review and evidence paths must exist; it does not require a closed allowlist, bind hashes or validate evidence content.
note: 05 Findings/D1484 Historical audit test checks presence and a weak status exclusion.md

title: Source migration receipt tests trust recorded disposition
body: Tests require complete/runtime_loaded flags, every recorded batch unresolved=0, owner path existence and absence of externalized directories. They do not fetch or hash external payloads, verify historical scans, or reject an empty batches list through that all predicate alone.
note: 05 Findings/D1485 Source migration receipt tests trust recorded disposition.md

title: Candidate and specialty tests preserve honest metadata distinctions
body: Candidate records with runtime_symbols must remain partial_semantic_coverage; counts are recomputed internally. Specialty entries must cover queue IDs exactly once, and active IDs/counts must match catalog intersections. Neither test verifies runtime symbol behavior or original external source identity.
note: 05 Findings/D1486 Candidate and specialty tests preserve honest metadata distinctions.md

title: Research contract tests establish candidate-only shape admission
body: Every declared research contract is tested with a generated minimal instance and must remain candidate_only with auto_activate false; one empty research-record must raise. Source coverage testing separately asserts a valid summary and a minimum control count, not each control execution.
note: 05 Findings/D1487 Research contract tests establish candidate-only shape admission.md

title: Historical revocation tests preserve certificate bytes and reject authority
body: The0.6.1 and0.6.2 tests hash retained certificates against revocation records and constrain project lifecycle labels; the0.6.2 test additionally calls the certificate verifier and expects invalid. Hardcoded public wording and release paths are historical policy fixtures, not live marketplace status.
note: 05 Findings/D1488 Historical revocation tests preserve certificate bytes and reject authority.md

title: Fault campaign aggregate test does not call the aggregate owner
body: One test loads campaign metadata and checks dimensions, command tokens and referenced test paths. The failed-lane test writes its own two-row JSON fixture and asserts Python all is false; it never invokes run_release_fault_campaign publication or its failure handling.
note: 05 Findings/D1489 Fault campaign aggregate test does not call the aggregate owner.md

title: Supply-chain writer test uses declared artifact hashes
body: The test passes invented wheel/sdist digests and no artifact files, then checks output types, one checksum, version and a provenance subject. Its final hash assertion merely checks a nonempty computed string. It does not verify real artifact bytes, signatures or complete source provenance.
note: 05 Findings/D1490 Supply-chain writer test uses declared artifact hashes.md

title: Platform policy fixtures do not execute a multi-platform matrix
body: Tests validate declared Python3.11-3.14 and three OS policies, synthetic version bounds, current-host Unicode paths/read-only bits/lock creation, and LF attributes. The POSIX host check only requires policy intersection with Linux or Darwin; this does not prove which OS or all CI jobs ran.
note: 05 Findings/D1491 Platform policy fixtures do not execute a multi-platform matrix.md

title: Publication workflow tests inspect local strings and retained bindings
body: Tests hash local certificate/signature files against a stored public receipt and compare artifact metadata; they do not cryptographically verify the signature or retrieve remote assets. Workflow ordering, OIDC, exact VSIX values and manual transport are checked as strings, not parsed/executed CI behavior. User-reported marketplace publication remains a separate fact.
note: 05 Findings/D1492 Publication workflow tests inspect local strings and retained bindings.md

title: Completion tests mix formula checks with historical state expectations
body: The tests bind stored projection to a fresh builder result and compare readiness/certified formulas, but also require fixed historical counts and explicit open-gap labels. A mock proves compact head use without loading snapshot. These assertions exercise declared projection semantics, not exhaustive feature completion.
note: 05 Findings/D1493 Completion tests mix formula checks with historical state expectations.md

title: Completion writer tests mutate authoritative fixture paths
body: Both writer tests call owners against ROOT, then restore target bytes in finally. They assert final JSON and absence of prepared files; they do not inject mid-write crashes or concurrent changes. Restoration itself is a write and can overwrite intervening state. These tests were read only.
note: 05 Findings/D1494 Completion writer tests mutate authoritative fixture paths.md

title: Adversarial routing test uses a fixed synthetic catalog
body: Twelve hand-built summaries cover ambiguous terms, negative matches, unsafe risk and supersession. The fixed corpus checks top1, exclusions and deterministic ties with synthetic revision labels. No live catalog drift, adversarial corpus expansion or runtime capability execution is established.
note: 05 Findings/D1495 Adversarial routing test uses a fixed synthetic catalog.md

title: Hybrid retrieval test signals are supplied rather than computed
body: Each optional signal changes an unrelated baseline into a hit by replacing one input field. This proves fusion consumes six signal types, not that an embedding model, graph scorer or external service computed them. The adapter subprocess fixture has no timeout; import portability is also checked by source strings.
note: 05 Findings/D1496 Hybrid retrieval test signals are supplied rather than computed.md

title: Memory fabric tests keep scope and trust separate from address encoding
body: Fixtures exercise exact structured route priority, project/ACL/expiry/trust rejection, canonical semantic roundtrip and adaptive address expansion. The provider test explicitly requires disabled even when all seven self-attested booleans are true. Correction checks a rebuild plan and transfer_exports membership, not actual rebuilding of every derived surface.
note: 05 Findings/D1497 Memory fabric tests keep scope and trust separate from address encoding.md

title: Capture tests verify proposal state without proving durable accepted origin
body: The semantic candidate fixture uses a dry-run capture and supplied semantic envelope, then checks candidate/proposal/retrieval-disabled state and rejection of a quarantined label. Capture apply testing checks schema and repeat event ID, not a crash/restart chain or byte-for-byte immutability of every repeated file.
note: 05 Findings/D1498 Capture tests verify proposal state without proving durable accepted origin.md

title: Promotion tests use evidence and reviewer identifiers as fixtures
body: The high-impact constraint is held without reviewer IDs and becomes validated with human-1 plus two supplied evidence strings. This demonstrates the decision branch; the test does not authenticate a human or establish independent evidence provenance.
note: 05 Findings/D1499 Promotion tests use evidence and reviewer identifiers as fixtures.md

title: Memory queue retry fixture does not establish exactly-once effects
body: The first callback raises before performing a recorded effect; the same PersistentWriteQueue object then flushes through an append callback once. Stable idempotency key and ready status do not test process restart or a crash after the external writer commits but before queue publication.
note: 05 Findings/D1500 Memory queue retry fixture does not establish exactly-once effects.md

title: Memory context and offload tests include actual tamper rejection
body: Tests enforce L0 pointer-only assembly, a character bound, deterministic scenes and same-project borrowed-agent limits. Offload preview leaves no file; apply restores the original body; altered stored bytes raise hash mismatch. These are bounded fixtures, not proof of all storage/concurrency or injection cases.
note: 05 Findings/D1501 Memory context and offload tests include actual tamper rejection.md

title: Scheduler tests certify simulated policy rather than execution
body: Metadata counts assert30 capabilities/owners, five workflows, three policies and eight schemas. Simulation tests reject cycles/missing dependencies and approval/resource/privacy/budget/retry blocks, and assert deterministic would_dispatch plans with execution_authority none. They call Python directly and do not cover CLI load_json failure found in batch89.
note: 05 Findings/D1502 Scheduler tests certify simulated policy rather than execution.md

title: Agent replay tests distinguish immutable artifacts from allowed run evidence
body: Eighteen receipt mutations plus altered builder artifacts and undeclared topology are rejected. A well-shaped run filename containing empty JSON is accepted for reopen, while rogue.txt is rejected. Legacy creation receipt reopens without graph backfill; modern missing triplet fails. This tests definition topology, not every retained run payload.
note: 05 Findings/D1503 Agent replay tests distinguish immutable artifacts from allowed run evidence.md

title: Worker success and host-model success have different fixture origins
body: The owned harness test requires process_started/exited/tree_closed and worker_invoked true with model_invoked false. Host-model tests instead supply completion status, output and model/token metadata directly to complete_host_run. These establish terminal envelope handling, not a real Copilot/model request.
note: 05 Findings/D1504 Worker success and host-model success have different fixture origins.md

title: Agent structural admission can coexist with blocked runtime memory
body: The unresolved-memory fixture passes candidate tests and admission but marks runtime_ready false; preview blocks and invocation must fail before adding a run. Host tool preflight likewise tests structural attestation and authority preview, not an actual external host tool invocation.
note: 05 Findings/D1505 Agent structural admission can coexist with blocked runtime memory.md

title: Worker diagnostic fallback tests intercept storage and stderr
body: Primary diagnostic failure is injected before a second durable write. When both writes fail, os.write is intercepted and the JSON payload inspected. No real supervised stderr transport, short-write loop or total diagnostic failure is exercised by these tests.
note: 05 Findings/D1506 Worker diagnostic fallback tests intercept storage and stderr.md

title: Agent lifecycle test observes autonomous publication directly
body: The real-lifecycle fixture starts through one-shot authority, denies unapproved pause, then pauses/resumes one run and cancels another. It polls run_control.read for up to45 seconds rather than session_status, verifying publication does not depend on that API. Observer inactive and worker reclaimed assertions are fixture requirements; no fresh cross-platform result is claimed here.
note: 05 Findings/D1507 Agent lifecycle test observes autonomous publication directly.md

title: Dashboard timeout assertion does not measure producer execution
body: The snapshot test mocks RuntimeWorkPlane.execute, returns connected true immediately, and inspects timeout_seconds=60. It proves argument plumbing, not an enforced60-second total callback or end-to-end UI latency bound.
note: 05 Findings/D1508 Dashboard timeout assertion does not measure producer execution.md

title: Dashboard runnable counts are stored-state observations
body: Tests create unsigned minimal admission JSON with decision admitted/runnable_state runnable and minimal session/run state JSON, then expect runnable revision and run counts. Display totals therefore must not be interpreted as authenticated admission, current executable readiness or completed operations.
note: 05 Findings/D1509 Dashboard runnable counts are stored-state observations.md

title: Dashboard graph tests establish bounded presentation behavior
body: Tests cover global typo ranking, qualified ambiguous IDs, aggregate cluster accounting, endpoint membership, depth clamp6 and node/edge limits500/1000. Oversized bytes are rejected before JSON decode; excessive node count is rejected after parsing but before graph materialization. A single-node repository fixture lacks freshness metadata, so its current-project-map test name does not establish current source identity.
note: 05 Findings/D1510 Dashboard graph tests establish bounded presentation behavior.md

title: Completion display tests separate source hashing from mocked selection
body: One fixture changes actual authority bytes and verifies stale detection with a mocked ledger head. Several runtime/registry preference tests mock _completion_projection_current true, while stale fallback tests require green claims revoked and the builder uncalled. Host source identity excludes a generated bundle while binding source/action contract changes.
note: 05 Findings/D1511 Completion display tests separate source hashing from mocked selection.md

title: Hardware dashboard fixtures test cache integrity with a mocked probe
body: Tests check miss/hit/forced/expired states, malformed JSON rebuild, tampered report hash, future timestamps and an upper TTL rejection. hardware_report is mocked, so these are cache lifecycle tests rather than measurements or hardware compatibility evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1512 Hardware dashboard fixtures test cache integrity with a mocked probe.md

title: Provider LIVE display classification can come from budget state alone
body: One test expects the local ollama budget projection to have provenance class LIVE. Another writes sealed synthetic reservation/settlement metadata and checks30 percent use, seven units remaining and redacted fallback details. No provider call, token observation or billing reconciliation occurs in those fixtures.
note: 05 Findings/D1513 Provider LIVE display classification can come from budget state alone.md

title: Memory dashboard states are classification fixtures rather than attachment operations
body: Tests distinguish detached, configured empty, expired and new-project onboarding; mocked workspace-monitor and project-map values suppress unrelated attention for new repositories while retaining invalid existing-map warnings. They do not initialize, attach or renew actual memory sessions.
note: 05 Findings/D1514 Memory dashboard states are classification fixtures rather than attachment operations.md

title: Cache discovery fails closed on walker limits but excludes by a distinct policy
body: The Python cache owner uses100000 files, depth128 and2GiB observed file size, with links skipped. Repository-root pytest cache and canonical external custody are pruned after removing cache components from the classification path. Directory matching itself is case-sensitive while suffix matching is casefolded. This differs from the extension scanner.
note: 05 Findings/D1515 Cache discovery fails closed on walker limits but excludes by a distinct policy.md

title: Whole cache directory moves can carry uninventoried descendants
body: The walker can skip links and excluded subtrees while still selecting their containing cache directory. shutil.move then relocates the entire selected directory, including entries not in covered_files. Post-move verification checks only recorded inventory, so it is not a complete moved-object denominator.
note: 05 Findings/D1516 Whole cache directory moves can carry uninventoried descendants.md

title: Nested cache moves can invalidate expected destination layout
body: Targets sort deepest-first. Moving an inner cache creates its destination parent; later moving the outer cache to that existing parent makes shutil.move append the source basename. Recorded expected paths can then fail reconciliation after earlier effects. An isolated unchanged-stdlib probe confirmed existing-directory destination behavior with rename intercepted; no directory was moved.
note: 05 Findings/D1517 Nested cache moves can invalidate expected destination layout.md

title: Cache move receipt is published only after all effects
body: Inventory hashes and size stats are separate reads; target containment is checked before inventory, not immediately before moves. No second matching tree snapshot, pre-move equality, durable intent or rollback exists in this owner. A move/reconciliation failure can leave partial quarantine without its final receipt. Caller quarantine roots may be external or even inside a selected subtree; only workspace/root equality is rejected.
note: 05 Findings/D1518 Cache move receipt is published only after all effects.md

title: Cache CLI output is an additional unguarded publication path
body: Even preview can write caller-selected --output, creating parents and replacing a file. This path has no collision/alias restriction against scanned input. Successful return always exits0 and the result has no valid field; errors raise before that return.
note: 05 Findings/D1519 Cache CLI output is an additional unguarded publication path.md

title: Sanitizer traversal materializes excluded subtrees before filtering
body: A complete rglob list is sorted deepest-first without file/byte/depth/time limits. Exclusions are applied in later loops, not traversal pruning. changed_nodes is built without exclusions and later adds renamed-node descendants to preservation, so excluded names can still be read/copied when selected by name transformation.
note: 05 Findings/D1520 Sanitizer traversal materializes excluded subtrees before filtering.md

title: Sanitizer preservation receipt hashes source after copy
body: Apply creates an empty external preservation directory, scans readable UTF-8 candidates, copies affected files and then hashes/stat-checks each source. It never compares copied destination bytes against the source digest, nor checks immediate source equality before rewrite. Concurrent changes can make preserved bytes and receipt disagree. Preflight errors stop mutation but may leave the created preservation directory.
note: 05 Findings/D1521 Sanitizer preservation receipt hashes source after copy.md

title: Sanitizer rename resolves links before applying the operation
body: _extended_windows_path calls path.resolve for source and target, and _rename passes those resolved paths directly to os.rename. The owner does not reject symlink files or recheck resolved containment. An unchanged-function probe with fake resolution confirmed that an in-tree logical link resolving outside would pass the outside target as rename source; actual links/moves were not created.
note: 05 Findings/D1522 Sanitizer rename resolves links before applying the operation.md

title: Sanitizer text classification and binary coverage differ
body: The first64KiB NUL check decides binary versus UTF-8 treatment. A NUL-free binary with invalid UTF-8 raises preservation preflight failure under apply; later text errors are recorded. Binary scanning checks configured identifier patterns in Latin-1 chunks but does not rewrite binary content. Root names themselves are outside the rglob rename list.
note: 05 Findings/D1523 Sanitizer text classification and binary coverage differ.md

title: Sanitizer text replacement and multi-file operation are not transactional
body: Each text file uses a same-directory temporary, copied stat and os.replace; there is no file/directory fsync or concurrent-identity recheck. Finally retains a failed temp by move, which can itself fail and mask the original error. Later rename errors are outside the text-error catch. Earlier rewritten/renamed files remain changed if a later file fails.
note: 05 Findings/D1524 Sanitizer text replacement and multi-file operation are not transactional.md

title: Sanitizer collision naming checks availability without reservation
body: Overlong components use a deterministic name digest and limited suffix; collisions try widening source-name hash suffixes. Availability is checked before rename rather than reserved atomically, and preview does not reserve generated names. Path-change output hashes the original relative path and stores a sanitized target string; it is not a complete actual-path journal after ancestor renames.
note: 05 Findings/D1525 Sanitizer collision naming checks availability without reservation.md

title: Identifier audit file and byte counts include unscanned binary contents
body: Known binary suffixes bypass content scanning but add stat size to bytes_scanned. Unknown suffixes are fully decoded once for classification, then read again for scanning if admitted. Unknown-suffix OSError/UnicodeDecodeError returns false rather than recording the error; an isolated unreadable-file probe confirmed this classification result. Counts are visited/stat-accounted bytes, not universally inspected content bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1526 Identifier audit file and byte counts include unscanned binary contents.md

title: Identifier audit has traversal and pattern scope limits
body: The audit fully materializes rglob before exclusions and has no total resource bound. File symlinks can be followed by is_file/open without resolved-root containment. Nonexistent roots can yield empty scoped results. Pattern matching uses finite overlap, configured spellings and ASCII home-name grammar; ZIP detection is suffix-only and does not inspect archive content.
note: 05 Findings/D1527 Identifier audit has traversal and pattern scope limits.md

title: Identifier-only audit intentionally never claims comprehensive validity
body: Five controls are always not_run, so valid remains false even when scoped_valid passes. Four pattern/archive gate statuses depend on hit lists rather than errors; read failures can coexist with those individual passed gates while scoped_valid is false. CLI exits1 for noncomprehensive valid, not merely for identifier findings.
note: 05 Findings/D1528 Identifier-only audit intentionally never claims comprehensive validity.md

title: Sanitation composition does not propagate identifier top-level errors
body: build_sanitation_summary copies only identifier_audit.gates, replaces the five not-run controls and derives validity from gate statuses. It does not carry identifier_audit.errors or scoped_valid. A transient identifier-only read failure can therefore be lost if other scans pass and base gate hit lists are empty. Release/export callers use this compositor result; this is a source-derived failure path, not an executed release.
note: 05 Findings/D1529 Sanitation composition does not propagate identifier top-level errors.md

title: Identifier provenance exemptions are path labels rather than content authentication
body: Four fixed provenance paths receive host-home exemptions and one n8n template admits a fixed container home literal. Exemptions apply to home matches, not configured private identifiers. The audit itself does not verify append-only integrity or authenticate those paths before granting their typed exemption.
note: 05 Findings/D1530 Identifier provenance exemptions are path labels rather than content authentication.md

title: Historical deletion scripts embed an old authority claim
body: All three PowerShell receipts hardcode explicit_user_request_2026-08-13 and protected_data_touched=false. They do not consume a current admission, retention decision or resource ledger. Those source strings are historical labels and are not authorization to run deletion in this task.
note: 05 Findings/D1531 Historical deletion scripts embed an old authority claim.md

title: Historical ownership discovery is based on names or fixture shapes
body: One script selects four temp prefixes plus extension/.vscode-test; another selects every child of the user-wide pytest-of-USERNAME directory; the third matches temp names plus framework/repository/package/key-pair signatures. Generic tmp directories with repository/.git or a matching release-output suffix can qualify. These heuristics do not prove exclusive Pacify-X ownership.
note: 05 Findings/D1532 Historical ownership discovery is based on names or fixture shapes.md

title: Historical live-process and reparse checks have time and resolution gaps
body: Each script snapshots process command lines once and matches path substrings, missing users of files whose paths are absent from command lines and later processes. GetFullPath is lexical; relative link targets are resolved against current directory, not their containing link directory. Only the generated-fixture script explicitly rejects a top-level reparse target. No immediate content snapshot is compared before removal.
note: 05 Findings/D1533 Historical live-process and reparse checks have time and resolution gaps.md

title: Historical deletion evidence is late and accounting is not physical reclamation proof
body: The owned-cache script aborts on error and writes no final receipt after partial deletion. The other two catch per-target failures but retained targets may already be partly changed. Counts use logical file lengths; C-drive free-space differences are host-wide and can include unrelated activity or another target volume. Receipts are final direct writes without a durable per-effect journal.
note: 05 Findings/D1534 Historical deletion evidence is late and accounting is not physical reclamation proof.md

title: Historical cleanup redaction claims exceed its verification
body: The redactor replaces only current root/home/temp literal spellings in string values, not dictionary keys, other hosts, slash/case variants or arbitrary path patterns. It then unconditionally labels host_paths_removed and semantic_fields_preserved true. All four files are overwritten sequentially even if text did not change; no before-image, digest rebinding or verification scan is retained. Its nonauthoritative historical classification is explicit.
note: 05 Findings/D1535 Historical cleanup redaction claims exceed its verification.md

title: Extension cache custody differs from canonical repository custody
body: The JS scanner skips .git/node_modules and root evidence/quarantine trees, but has no canonical exclusions for virtual environments, Python installations or preserved-skills trees. Any recognized cache basename can receive safe-to-delete and retentionRequired=false after structural inventory. Name classification does not establish content ownership or retention. Host requires explicit selection and modal approval, which remains a separate boundary.
note: 05 Findings/D1536 Extension cache custody differs from canonical repository custody.md

title: Extension scan bounds do not bound candidate hashing time
body: maxDirectories/maxCandidates use Number(options.value || default), so nonfinite/nonnumeric truthy values can disable comparisons for direct callers. Each candidate permits50000 entries but has no byte/time bound; a large readdir is allocated before counting. Cancellation is checked between discovery entries, not inside inventoryDirectory/hashFileStable. Candidate failures are silently dropped without an unresolved list.
note: 05 Findings/D1537 Extension scan bounds do not bound candidate hashing time.md

title: Extension main path binds multiple identities and snapshots
body: Root lstat/realpath, every target ancestor, no-follow file open where available, file identity/size/mtime, hardlink rejection and directory identity checks support the normal path. Candidate, preflight, immediate, staged and final inventories must agree before adapter invocation. This is materially stronger than legacy cache mover, while remaining userspace pathname operations with a final check-to-effect interval.
note: 05 Findings/D1538 Extension main path binds multiple identities and snapshots.md

title: Extension candidate IDs are selectors rather than authorization tokens
body: IDs are truncated root/path hashes and execution verifies basename/name/relativePath/classification/retention plus inventory. directoryIdentity is optional in executeCleanup, but the normal host retains its nonenumerable scan object and only sends display fields to the webview. The host passes its own candidates after modal approval, so a webview cannot directly substitute arbitrary candidate objects through that route.
note: 05 Findings/D1539 Extension candidate IDs are selectors rather than authorization tokens.md

title: Extension staging protects a replaced original path but not all OS races
body: A random sibling stage becomes the adapter target, preserving a concurrently recreated original path. Identity/hash checks occur before rename/disposal, but no filesystem handle-based atomic compare-and-remove exists. A receipt write occurs between immediate inventory and stage rename. Claims of no remaining pathname race would exceed the implementation.
note: 05 Findings/D1540 Extension staging protects a replaced original path but not all OS races.md

title: Extension recycle fallback validates leaf but omits ancestor containment
body: Fallback forms .quarantine/cleanupId with lexical isInside checks, recursively creates it and verifies only that leaf is a plain directory. It does not call assertPlainDirectoryUnderRoot or compare realpath with rootGuard for this route. An existing linked .quarantine ancestor can redirect the destination outside the root. This is a conditional source finding; no symlink or move was executed.
note: 05 Findings/D1541 Extension recycle fallback validates leaf but omits ancestor containment.md

title: Extension restoration has a narrower guard than disposal
body: restoreUnchangedStage checks stage/plain-directory, original absence and matching inventory, then renames. It receives no root guard and does not repeat ancestor containment or reserve the absent original destination. A concurrent path/ancestor change can invalidate those checks before rename. Failed quarantine verification after a successful move can also leave an unrecorded quarantine location while stage-based restore finds nothing.
note: 05 Findings/D1542 Extension restoration has a narrower guard than disposal.md

title: Extension receipts distinguish adapter uncertainty but can themselves fail after effects
body: The owner explicitly separates partial retention, disappearance after adapter error, unchanged restoration and successful fallback. Phase receipts flush a temporary file then rename, with directory fsync only off Windows. A write outside the per-candidate try or terminal write failure aborts the loop/return after prior effects; no restart reconciler is defined here. Callback temporary-file removal errors are suppressed.
note: 05 Findings/D1543 Extension receipts distinguish adapter uncertainty but can themselves fail after effects.md

title: Extension reclaimed byte totals include preserved local quarantine
body: Confirmed results include moved-to-local-quarantine as well as recycle/permanent disposition. bytes_reclaimed sums original logical candidate sizes, so it can be positive when bytes remain in the same project. The host announces reclaimed count. This is removal from the active cache location, not demonstrated freed disk capacity.
note: 05 Findings/D1544 Extension reclaimed byte totals include preserved local quarantine.md

title: Extension recycle tests use a deletion adapter rather than OS trash
body: Success fixtures call fs.rm even when asserting useTrash=true; they prove adapter option plumbing and receipt logic, not recoverability through the operating-system recycle bin. Tests cover link/hardlink rejection, changed trees, partial/uncertain outcomes, original-path replacement and Unicode depth. They omit quarantine ancestor redirection and receipt publication failure after effects.
note: 05 Findings/D1545 Extension recycle tests use a deletion adapter rather than OS trash.md

title: Sanitation tests preserve scanner scope rather than full secret assurance
body: Identifier tests explicitly expect clean scoped_valid=true but comprehensive valid=false; they test chunk-boundary placeholder behavior, immutable provenance, binary exclusion and external custody. The summary test supplies passed base identifier gates and valid licensing while running local shape/email/magic checks. Matching PNG magic permits embedded email bytes without text PII review by design.
note: 05 Findings/D1546 Sanitation tests preserve scanner scope rather than full secret assurance.md

title: Secret review tests bind content identity while allowing line movement
body: Tests assert redacted literal credential shapes, selected false positives, complete private-key block detection and stale reviews after value changes. A separate fixture permits formatting-only movement to line3. These test deterministic identity policy; they do not prove detection of unknown secret encodings or provider revocation.
note: 05 Findings/D1547 Secret review tests bind content identity while allowing line movement.md

title: Sanitizer and cache tests leave several operational failure paths open
body: Fixtures cover ordinary preview/apply, canonical expansion, long names, collisions, named exclusions, preflight read failure and single-level cache recovery. They do not cover nested cache targets, content drift between preservation and mutation, copy-byte verification, linked source rename or failed final receipt. Some sanitizer tests preserve a sibling directory outside their TemporaryDirectory context. None were run here.
note: 05 Findings/D1548 Sanitizer and cache tests leave several operational failure paths open.md

title: Global host lease can return without a successfully created lock
body: The two-attempt loop removes a stale lock after each EEXIST. After the second removal it leaves the loop and constructs a lease even though neither exclusive create succeeded. A VM probe of unchanged source with fake fs confirmed two failed creates, two removals and a returned token. No real lock was touched.
note: 05 Findings/D1549 Global host lease can return without a successfully created lock.md

title: Lease stale ownership is PID-based and release is best-effort
body: Signal-zero EPERM means alive; other probe failures mean dead. There is no process birth identity, compare-and-unlink predecessor check or fsync. release sets its released flag before reading/unlinking and suppresses errors, preventing retry after a transient failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1550 Lease stale ownership is PID-based and release is best-effort.md

title: Timeout followed by zero exit can report completed
body: The worker records termination_reason=timeout but classifies numeric zero as completed. The explicit timeout error is limited to a null code. Unchanged source in a fake child/terminator VM produced status completed, timeout reason and both closure booleans true.
note: 05 Findings/D1551 Timeout followed by zero exit can report completed.md

title: Termination rejection can escape timeout settlement
body: Signal handlers discard the termination promise; timeout attaches then without a rejection handler. A rejecting terminator can produce unhandled rejection and a hanging one can leave the outer worker unresolved. Windows taskkill helper itself has no timeout. No live termination was attempted.
note: 05 Findings/D1552 Termination rejection can escape timeout settlement.md

title: Process-tree closure changes meaning without an ownership token
body: Without ownershipToken reconciliation equates tree closure to worker exit. With a token it scans command-line substring matches, requests termination, then scans once immediately. POSIX termination only sends SIGTERM; it does not await exit/escalate. Command-line token presence is not ancestry or PID-birth proof.
note: 05 Findings/D1553 Process-tree closure changes meaning without an ownership token.md

title: Host output tail bound is characters rather than bytes
body: The retained stdout/stderr tail limit is applied to JavaScript strings after independently decoding chunks, so UTF-8 boundaries can be replaced and memory bytes exceed the nominal character count. Forwarded output is not bounded by that tail. Callback or lease release exceptions in finally can replace the operation outcome.
note: 05 Findings/D1554 Host output tail bound is characters rather than bytes.md

title: Cache marker creation and cache reads enforce different custody checks
body: Read paths lstat root/marker and reject links, while ensure creates/writes through the selected root without equivalent root/ancestor identity checks. Existing marker owner/schema are checked, but direct read-modify-write has no lock or atomic publication and can lose concurrently retained versions.
note: 05 Findings/D1555 Cache marker creation and cache reads enforce different custody checks.md

title: Cached executable resolution does not bind executable bytes
body: The resolver checks platform layout, directory/sentinel/executable plain-file state and marker owner/schema. It does not verify retained_versions includes requested version, sentinel contents, executable digest/signature/version or all ancestor realpaths. Darwin has no supported layout despite a macOS browser lane elsewhere.
note: 05 Findings/D1556 Cached executable resolution does not bind executable bytes.md

title: Temporary host marker is a lexical ownership declaration
body: Marker creation requires an immediate OS-temp child with pacify-x- prefix, then writes expected cleanup obligations. It does not establish physical root identity or register a current resource-ledger lease. Both smoke parents allocate and prepare before entering their execution try/finally and global lease.
note: 05 Findings/D1557 Temporary host marker is a lexical ownership declaration.md

title: Installed smoke runtime identity checks a retained marker
body: The optional engine identity path validates schema, hash shape and count fields from the runtime marker; it does not recompute all engine files. Expected VSIX SHA is checked if supplied; child hashes before and after install. Parent later trusts child result rather than independently rehashing the artifact.
note: 05 Findings/D1558 Installed smoke runtime identity checks a retained marker.md

title: Installed fixture setup can retain unreceipted work before lease acquisition
body: Marked temp creation, prepare and config write precede try and runOwnedHostWorker. Missing input, setup failure or duplicate lease can leave allocated paths before a cleanup lifecycle exists. Installed fixture git calls have no checked status or timeout; development fixture checks statuses but lacks timeouts.
note: 05 Findings/D1559 Installed fixture setup can retain unreceipted work before lease acquisition.md

title: Installed host network environment is not network containment
body: The child inherits HTTP/HTTPS proxies pointed at localhost port 9 plus localhost bypass and a PX deny flag. These influence cooperative clients, not direct sockets or arbitrary process access. This route uses a pre-existing owned cache; development smoke can use test-electron downloading.
note: 05 Findings/D1560 Installed host network environment is not network containment.md

title: Installed CLI execution and host results have separate checks
body: Installation has a 120 second spawnSync limit, requires exit success and an English success string, and sets shell=true on Windows. The test suite writes a receipt; child checks existence and parent parses it. A retained file alone is not newly authenticated suite execution, and parent runtime-marker verification remains distinct from exact package checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1561 Installed CLI execution and host results have separate checks.md

title: Smoke success receipt precedes workspace reclamation
body: Both parents publish retained host evidence before finally writes lifecycle and conditionally fs.rm when process_tree_closed_verified. They do not verify absence afterward or bind workspace_reclaimed proof into the already written success receipt. Lifecycle write failure can prevent cleanup; prior retained receipts are not invalidated at start.
note: 05 Findings/D1562 Smoke success receipt precedes workspace reclamation.md

title: Development portable receipt and console output differ
body: Development receipt recursively rewrites strings resolving to engine root as dot, while stdout prints the original parsed result. Other absolute paths remain. Source and installed smoke files execute main at module load, so importing them is not a passive inspection operation.
note: 05 Findings/D1563 Development portable receipt and console output differ.md

title: Manual installer verifies a selected hash manifest rather than signed release authority
body: The installer derives expected package/version, chooses first filename-regex match in SHA256SUMS and hashes the VSIX once. It does not authenticate the manifest, enforce exact whole-line filename membership or recheck bytes immediately after install. Hash integrity and certified publication authority are distinct.
note: 05 Findings/D1564 Manual installer verifies a selected hash manifest rather than signed release authority.md

title: Manual installed verification is version observation
body: Same exact version is refused, but other versions use force including downgrade. List-extensions exit status is not checked, and final verification searches exact extension/version text without inspecting installed file hashes. No prior installation snapshot or rollback is retained by this script.
note: 05 Findings/D1565 Manual installed verification is version observation.md

title: Uninstaller uses a fixed identity and CLI exit status
body: The uninstall script hardcodes mountain-nomad-bc.pacify-x-vscode, invokes the CLI and checks exit status without a subsequent absence query. Settings retention is stated but not independently verified in this owner. No uninstall was executed.
note: 05 Findings/D1566 Uninstaller uses a fixed identity and CLI exit status.md

title: Test profile partition can tolerate a missing isolated file
body: Only top-level test files are discovered. Named isolated lists are filtered by existence and the profile fails only if empty; removal of one member can reduce coverage. Unit concurrency is four, UI lanes are serial, and child executions have no explicit timeout or resource registration in this runner.
note: 05 Findings/D1567 Test profile partition can tolerate a missing isolated file.md

title: UI browser lane identity is based on executable existence
body: Windows requires Edge and Chrome; macOS Chrome lane can select Chromium; Linux Chromium lane may select Google Chrome. Selection tests existence without executable version/digest. Profile contract tests invoke lane resolution, so unit execution itself depends on browser availability.
note: 05 Findings/D1568 UI browser lane identity is based on executable existence.md

title: UI matrix receipt can be absent after a spawn error
body: Nonzero lane exits are collected and remaining lanes continue, but a spawn error throws before writing the final matrix. There is no start/partial receipt. Unit/performance profiles return child status without the UI matrix receipt; inherited environment is not filtered here.
note: 05 Findings/D1569 UI matrix receipt can be absent after a spawn error.md

title: Package contract assertions are mostly lexical
body: All command IDs need only occur in extension source; presence does not prove registration, reachability or correct owner. Packaging pins, check scripts, hash guard text, contribution assets, marketplace-boundary defaults and ontology fields are asserted without executing those production flows.
note: 05 Findings/D1570 Package contract assertions are mostly lexical.md

title: Host lifecycle tests omit the reproduced outcomes
body: Tests cover duplicate active lease, one stale retry, fake worker success/error/timeout and residual process matches. They do not cover two stale failures or timeout followed by exit zero. A listenerCount>=0 assertion is tautological, and two matched PID fixtures do not establish a process-count bound.
note: 05 Findings/D1571 Host lifecycle tests omit the reproduced outcomes.md

title: Fixture packaging is deterministic within the chosen runtime inputs
body: The builder fixes UTC ZIP time, sorts names, deflates at level 9, stores CRC32 and produces two fixed identities. It directly overwrites VSIX files then publishes receipt, without transactional pair replacement or rollback; compression/runtime differences are not cross-version reproducibility proof. Import executes all builds.
note: 05 Findings/D1572 Fixture packaging is deterministic within the chosen runtime inputs.md

title: Lifecycle fixtures are inert with a declared command conflict
body: v1/v2 activation returns a frozen identity/version object and deactivate does nothing; installed harness activation is empty. The v2 manifest test asserts a contributed pacifyX.openDashboard command with no activationEvents. This supplies declarative conflict input, not real extension work.
note: 05 Findings/D1573 Lifecycle fixtures are inert with a declared command conflict.md

title: Fixture tests prove repeatability without full independent ZIP validation
body: The test runs builder twice at shared generated paths, compares file hashes and checks leading ZIP signature and size range. It does not independently extract every member/CRC, install in VS Code or impose a subprocess timeout. Shared paths can race under concurrent owners.
note: 05 Findings/D1574 Fixture tests prove repeatability without full independent ZIP validation.md

title: Publication fixture replaces cryptographic and custody verification
body: Positive/negative release tests mock verify_certificate_signature and reconstruct_evidence_custody as valid. Dummy wheel/sdist/VSIX bytes and literal signature fields exercise binding and expected asset checks, not real signing, archive extraction or remote publication.
note: 05 Findings/D1575 Publication fixture replaces cryptographic and custody verification.md

title: Publication negative cases distinguish mutable subjects from certificate binding
body: Tests reject changed candidate identity, substituted standalone VSIX, extra draft asset and changed summary whose custody subject hash is updated without matching certificate binding. This demonstrates the selected consumer comparison despite mocked cryptographic validation.
note: 05 Findings/D1576 Publication negative cases distinguish mutable subjects from certificate binding.md

title: Template completeness schema checker implements a subset
body: The local helper checks type, const/enum, pattern/minimum, required/additionalProperties and items. It does not implement references, combinators, max/unique/minItems or format; successful fixtures are not full JSON Schema validation. Historical 318-file counters and completeness/index flags are retained metadata checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1577 Template completeness schema checker implements a subset.md

title: All workflow fixture routes use supplied preflight and evidence authority
body: The 17-workflow loop derives effect grants from the same handler registry and supplies all-true preflight, approved for non-read effects. Cross-project resolver returns fixed accepted source/destination evidence for every reference; many payloads provide true test/rollback flags and evidence strings. These exercise real handler routing when run, not independent trusted evidence acquisition.
note: 05 Findings/D1578 All workflow fixture routes use supplied preflight and evidence authority.md

title: Missing operational owners are subtracted twice
body: The duplicate filter selects any owner count other than one, including zero, while missing selects zero separately. owned_once subtracts both lengths. An unchanged-source VM with one unowned filesystem-write control reports total=1, owned_once=-1 and the same control in missing/duplicate. Exit remains correctly nonzero.
note: 05 Findings/D1579 Missing operational owners are subtracted twice.md

title: Control owner coverage is a declared assignment test
body: Eleven hardcoded direct controls and sixteen probe functions called with empty observations contribute records. A finite effect-name set selects the denominator. Exactly one record establishes assignment uniqueness, not successful admission, input handling, effect, persistence or recovery. New effect vocabulary outside this set is excluded.
note: 05 Findings/D1580 Control owner coverage is a declared assignment test.md

title: CSS audit scope omits cascade layer identity
body: Only media/supports/container preludes contribute scope. Layer and other at-rules are omitted; selector parsing strips comments lexically and splitSelectors tracks bracket/parenthesis depth without quote state. Matching selector strings can therefore collapse semantically distinct layer/declaration contexts.
note: 05 Findings/D1581 CSS audit scope omits cascade layer identity.md

title: CSS deduplication does not compare declarations
body: The rewrite removes a legacy branch whenever its normalized selector/scope key exists in modular CSS. A pure probe with legacy red text plus white background and modular blue text in another layer removes the entire legacy rule, including unmatched background. This is selector migration, not proof of equivalent computed styles.
note: 05 Findings/D1582 CSS deduplication does not compare declarations.md

title: CSS contrast gate is a finite literal-token check
body: Two named text tokens are matched as six-digit hex literals and compared against three fixed backgrounds at 4.5. It does not resolve var fallback, theme overrides, opacity, rendered background or actual component text sizes. Missing numeric baseline maxima compare as undefined and do not independently fail.
note: 05 Findings/D1583 CSS contrast gate is a finite literal-token check.md

title: CSS rewrite publishes directly without recovery custody
body: Check mode exits one if generated rewrite differs; write mode directly overwrites dashboard.css. No atomic temp/rename, backup, before/after render comparison or collision with concurrent editor writes is managed here. The audit did not run write mode.
note: 05 Findings/D1584 CSS rewrite publishes directly without recovery custody.md

title: Efficiency scan failure leaks its measurement interval
body: measureScan starts setInterval and clears it only after successful await scanEnvironmentAsync. A fake-dependency VM forced rejection and observed zero clearInterval calls. A real failure could keep its process alive; no real timer or scan was created by the probe.
note: 05 Findings/D1585 Efficiency scan failure leaks its measurement interval.md

title: Efficiency acceptance measures narrow synthetic loads
body: Profiles use 200/400/1000/2500 files over a small reused directory pattern and a fabricated Python environment. Synchronous fixture creation is outside duration measurement; passed requires duration/lag below thresholds and uncapped tree but not any heartbeat tick or expected inventory count. A hundred identical held requests tests one single-flight case, not mixed-key contention.
note: 05 Findings/D1586 Efficiency acceptance measures narrow synthetic loads.md

title: Efficiency ownership label exceeds the local implementation
body: The function creates a temporary tree and deletes it in finally without registering a marker/lease here. Scan worker ownership belongs imported discovery code; governor disposal is not in a dedicated finally if its request loop fails. Standalone report publication occurs only after measurement and cleanup succeed.
note: 05 Findings/D1587 Efficiency ownership label exceeds the local implementation.md

title: Environment refresh uses a partial on-disk extension view
body: The wrapper scans user .vscode/extensions and one Windows local installation builtin path. First encountered publisher/name wins across versions, directory order is not sorted before deduplication, and isActive=false is supplied for every extension. It does not query the active host or additional portable/Insiders/remote installations.
note: 05 Findings/D1588 Environment refresh uses a partial on-disk extension view.md

title: Environment manifest bounds precede a following stat/read
body: Entry directories reject symlinks, but manifest stat follows file links and a separate full read follows the 2 MiB stat check. Roots/ancestors are not physically bound. Errors silently omit manifests. Root validation only rejects filesystem root/non-directory; reason text says governed but wrapper itself performs no admission check.
note: 05 Findings/D1589 Environment manifest bounds precede a following stat/read.md

title: Outage ownership marker does not prove current disposable custody
body: Outage validation resolves sibling engine and user-data paths, rejects selected links and checks marker schema/owner/classification. It does not require an OS-temp boundary, active lifecycle lease, current admission or complete inventory. Arbitrary similarly marked sibling trees satisfy this local contract.
note: 05 Findings/D1590 Outage ownership marker does not prove current disposable custody.md

title: Engine outage publication is in-memory after rename
body: begin renames the whole runtime before returning a receipt; no durable intent, startup reconciler or automatic finally exists in this helper. Only cli.py and dashboard_api.py hashes are retained, so exact restoration claim covers those bytes, not every runtime file. Caller must ensure restoration after failure.
note: 05 Findings/D1591 Engine outage publication is in-memory after rename.md

title: Outage restore verification follows the effect
body: Restore requires original absent, renames displaced runtime back, then checks two hashes. If a hash check fails, restored remains false but the original path now exists, so the next restore call fails its boundary guard. Parent/root identity is not revalidated immediately before either rename.
note: 05 Findings/D1592 Outage restore verification follows the effect.md

title: Native input client checks lexical sibling paths once
body: Configuration checks same parent, leaf existence/nonlink and request/results directories, but does not bind all ancestor realpaths or require token to be a directory/current owned marker. Passing options.config bypasses constructor checks. Atomic request write uses exclusive random temp then rename without fsync or failed-temp recovery.
note: 05 Findings/D1593 Native input client checks lexical sibling paths once.md

title: Native approval keys are not bound to dialog semantics
body: Cancel alone maps to Escape; any other label approves via Enter with zero/one/two Tab traversals. Correlation strings are retained but neither server nor client verifies the targeted modal label, control action or operation payload at send time. Process ownership constrains host, not intended UI decision.
note: 05 Findings/D1594 Native approval keys are not bound to dialog semantics.md

title: Native input result is correlated but not authenticated
body: Client accepts schema, exact request ID/sequence, sent status, positive foreground PID, owned_process=true, expected key count and boolean focus_recovered. It does not verify signature, process ancestry itself, timestamp freshness or result file link/size identity. A writer inside the result directory can supply these assertions; directory custody is therefore the trust boundary.
note: 05 Findings/D1595 Native input result is correlated but not authenticated.md

title: Native input retry and numeric bounds have limited validation
body: Only the exact activation-refusal error is retried, with at most two numeric attempts and a new sequence each time. NaN/fractional option values are not explicitly rejected; NaN maximumAttempts can skip the loop and throw null. TTL is caller numeric input while server independently restricts lifetime to ten seconds.
note: 05 Findings/D1596 Native input retry and numeric bounds have limited validation.md

title: Native input server authenticates PID birth before foreground recovery
body: Requests require secret equality, sequence above in-memory last value, exact root PID, allowed key/action and current ten-second-max interval. Each accepted request compares root process creation time. Ancestry walk is bounded to 128 parents; visible owned windows are preferred, hidden owned windows can be restored, and disabled modal owners are not excluded.
note: 05 Findings/D1597 Native input server authenticates PID birth before foreground recovery.md

title: Native input focus and expiry checks are not atomic with SendInput
body: Request expiry is checked before up to 0.75 seconds of focus recovery. Root birth is checked before recovery and foreground PID is observed before SendInput; focus can change in that gap. The helper verifies sent key-event count but cannot prove the intended dialog consumed or committed the action.
note: 05 Findings/D1598 Native input focus and expiry checks are not atomic with SendInput.md

title: Native input crash can leave an effect without durable replay protection
body: last_sequence advances after successful SendInput, before result write, and resets to zero at server startup. A crash after input but before durable result can permit replay on restart. Partial SendInput raises a refusal after some key events may have occurred. Result temp name uses PID and stale temp can block publication; no fsync or write-ahead intent exists.
note: 05 Findings/D1599 Native input crash can leave an effect without durable replay protection.md

title: Native server directory custody is checked only at startup
body: Config is read once for command token comparison and reread inside serve. Request JSON files are globbed/read without per-file link, size, filename-sequence or stable identity checks; existing result files suppress requests. Stop is any stop.json existence. Config/secret shape is not independently validated by serve. These are local same-directory trust assumptions.
note: 05 Findings/D1600 Native server directory custody is checked only at startup.md

title: Fault walk counts only controls already rendered in a prior UI receipt
body: The selected set intersects supported UI kinds, rendered IDs in a zero-error UI receipt and required failure/recovery policy. It binds current source manifest and emits input receipt/matrix hashes, but unrendered controls never enter this denominator. A zero eligible set can still produce a successful process.
note: 05 Findings/D1601 Fault walk counts only controls already rendered in a prior UI receipt.md

title: Fault acceptance can use an unrelated or hidden alert
body: failureContained accepts nonempty alert text even if exact control text is unchanged. The collector uses allTextContents across alert/loading/empty selectors without a visibility or control-association check. Therefore unrelated/hidden fallback text can credit containment. Disappearance and changed text also lack semantic error-state validation.
note: 05 Findings/D1602 Fault acceptance can use an unrelated or hidden alert.md

title: Recovery can credit a freshly prepared page
body: After restoring original test snapshot, if the exact control is not visible, the walker calls prepare and revealControl again before checking visibility. RecoveryObserved only requires baseline/recovered visibility and zero new page errors, not original state/text, same page lifecycle or successful operation.
note: 05 Findings/D1603 Recovery can credit a freshly prepared page.md

title: Fault walk exit success does not mean every required stage passed
body: Final exit is nonzero only for pageErrors or thrown exceptions. Missing failure/recovery stages and unattempted controls are reported but do not independently fail. Browser/pages close in finally, while receipt is published only after all workers finish; an early exception leaves no partial receipt.
note: 05 Findings/D1604 Fault walk exit success does not mean every required stage passed.md

title: Operational bootstrap retains ready receipt after later failure
body: The bootstrap awaits activation, actual command registration and command return, writes ready with wx, then waits up to fifteen minutes for a sentinel. Catch writes failed only if receipt does not exist, so release timeout leaves the earlier ready record. Activation/command awaits have no local timeout and sentinel contents/identity are not checked.
note: 05 Findings/D1605 Operational bootstrap retains ready receipt after later failure.md

title: Native and fault helper tests use synthetic effects
body: Native client tests manufacture sent/refused JSON; Python tests use parent maps/window fakes and construct Win32 bindings but do not send keys. Fault tests simulate DOM/keyboard events and selected command helpers; direct element.click fallback is accepted. They demonstrate logic contracts, not current installed-host operation.
note: 05 Findings/D1606 Native and fault helper tests use synthetic effects.md

title: Native Python test portability is constrained before skip checks
body: The helper imports WinDLL and WINFUNCTYPE at module import, while the test imports the module before its Windows-only test decorator. On platforms lacking these ctypes names, collection fails before the skip. ABI checks alone do not prove foreground or SendInput effects.
note: 05 Findings/D1607 Native Python test portability is constrained before skip checks.md

title: Outage tests verify only selected happy and refusal paths
body: Tests create real temporary trees, confirm ordinary/idempotent restoration and reject mismatched token root or linked runtime. Link test can skip for host permissions. They do not cover crash after displacement, restore hash mismatch, root substitution or unrelated runtime-file drift.
note: 05 Findings/D1608 Outage tests verify only selected happy and refusal paths.md

title: MCP mutation fixture uses real signing with a narrow negative set
body: Generated approval keys and launch authority are exercised to replace forged actor/session/harness inputs. Other-project replay, changed token and unadmitted operation are rejected. No expiry, mutated signature, changed trusted key or process transport case is asserted in this file.
note: 05 Findings/D1609 MCP mutation fixture uses real signing with a narrow negative set.md

title: Team Fabric test claims are narrower than full registry nonmutation
body: Tests hash a three-file pack, count two entities and one collision, use one async worker and stage a renamed candidate. canonical_registry_mutated=false is asserted from receipt without before/after registry byte comparison. Worker adapter readiness/authentication is based on supplied host flags and labels, not a real login attempt.
note: 05 Findings/D1610 Team Fabric test claims are narrower than full registry nonmutation.md

title: Late-card worker combines physical probes with injected authority
body: Physical occupancy/link probes and independent framed hash are meaningful when the worker runs; inspection denial is injected and external-authenticated allocation uses supplied digest strings. Scaffold overwrites registry files under caller root, promotion calls approved=true and no local disposable-root gate exists. completed aggregates booleans but does not set nonzero exit on false.
note: 05 Findings/D1611 Late-card worker combines physical probes with injected authority.md

title: Late-card framed hash and rollback checks cover distinct moments
body: Independent hash is computed after rollback against the earlier promotion hash, alongside exact first-projection byte restoration. Preserved provenance is checked at draft/validation/admission/promotion/projection stages. Authenticated committed transaction is verified for second promotion; rollback_projection_authenticated itself compares path sets, with receipt authentication owned elsewhere.
note: 05 Findings/D1612 Late-card framed hash and rollback checks cover distinct moments.md

title: Studio crash worker covers one explicit publication boundary
body: The helper monkeypatches _atomic_bytes to os._exit(91) before first skill-index projection in promotion or rollback. A separate recovery command verifies a signed receipt and computes canonical tree hash, but prints expected canonical version without reading/comparing canonical manifest version here. Parent must check actual crash exit and recovery details; all crash points are not covered.
note: 05 Findings/D1613 Studio crash worker covers one explicit publication boundary.md

title: Audit bundle wrapper delegates completion to clean export
body: The wrapper requires existing output directory and VSIX, checks package version, calls clean_source_export and checks exit code before hashing resulting archive and writing sidecar. It has no own subprocess timeout or rollback for sidecar failure; wrapper valid=true depends on the child contract rather than independently reopening all archive evidence.
note: 05 Findings/D1614 Audit bundle wrapper delegates completion to clean export.md

title: Deep host tool input bypasses target checking
body: visit returns any value at depth greater than eight without examining it. An unchanged selected-function VM with fake filesystem rejects a top-level C:/outside/secret path but retains the same target nested nine times and records no validated target pointers. No tool or filesystem effect was invoked.
note: 05 Findings/D1615 Deep host tool input bypasses target checking.md

title: Host tool policy constrains declared inputs rather than actual implementation effects
body: The owner unions all grant effects and scope roots, rejects effects outside read/inspect/query/observe and requires non-billable, deny/loopback-only and no credential namespace. Recognized path/URI strings are checked and rewritten to physical paths, but the tool implementation receives no OS/network sandbox from this function. Undeclared internal effects remain outside these input checks.
note: 05 Findings/D1616 Host tool policy constrains declared inputs rather than actual implementation effects.md

title: Host input scope relies on heuristic locator discovery and a pathname interval
body: Keys ending in path/file/folder/directory/root/cwd/target/source/resource/uri/url or path-shaped strings trigger scope checks; ordinary strings may pass unchanged. Existing ancestor realpath is joined with nonexistent suffix. A path can change after check and before tool use. These are input normalization boundaries, not stable opened handles.
note: 05 Findings/D1617 Host input scope relies on heuristic locator discovery and a pathname interval.md

title: Live tool interface hash is observed rather than matched to admitted bytes
body: Registered tools are matched by name and required to expose an object schema; canonical name/description/schema are hashed before model execution. The digest is placed in receipts but not compared to an expected admitted interface digest, and registered interface is not re-read before each invokeTool.
note: 05 Findings/D1618 Live tool interface hash is observed rather than matched to admitted bytes.md

title: Exact model identity checks are explicit but initial calls precede the deadline
body: The route must contain exact model ID, pacify-local must bind exact vendor, and selected ID/vendor/family/version are checked. selectChatModels and initial countTokens occur before starting the bounded request timer. A stalled initial host API call is therefore outside that local deadline.
note: 05 Findings/D1619 Exact model identity checks are explicit but initial calls precede the deadline.md

title: Host model output budget is checked after full stream accumulation
body: Each stream is consumed into responseText, streamedText and responseParts before countTokens compares accumulated output to a clamped cap. Tool-call argument content is not counted as responseText output tokens. Requested maxOutputTokens itself is constructed before clamp. A noncooperative/large stream can exceed memory/time expectations before the check.
note: 05 Findings/D1620 Host model output budget is checked after full stream accumulation.md

title: Host model cancellation is cooperative rather than an enforced race
body: The deadline cancels a token and wall time is checked between rounds. Awaited host token-count/request/invoke calls and stream iteration are not raced against a rejecting timeout. Cancellation requested before listener registration is not explicitly inspected at that point. The host API must honor the linked token for timely completion.
note: 05 Findings/D1621 Host model cancellation is cooperative rather than an enforced race.md

title: Host output schema is a prompt here and a downstream contract elsewhere
body: The prompt includes an output schema, but this helper parses final text or wraps invalid JSON as text and non-object values as value. It returns completed without JSON Schema validation locally. Authoritative acceptance belongs complete-host-run and its runtime consumer, not this return label.
note: 05 Findings/D1622 Host output schema is a prompt here and a downstream contract elsewhere.md

title: Tool call receipts are collected in memory before final host completion
body: At most eight requested calls are permitted and each exact binding is policy-checked. Started receipt is appended before invoke; failed invocation annotates error and propagates all collected receipts. Completed input/result hashes are unkeyed observations held in memory until backend completion; no per-call durable journal is written here.
note: 05 Findings/D1623 Tool call receipts are collected in memory before final host completion.md

title: Prepared host run can outlive initial webview failure
body: The backend prepares a durable run before the running result is posted. That post occurs before creating activeHostRuns cancellation state and before the try wrapping model execution. A disposed/erroring webview can leave the prepared run without executing/completing it through this local branch; external reconciliation remains necessary.
note: 05 Findings/D1624 Prepared host run can outlive initial webview failure.md

title: Host completion publication can fail after model execution
body: After model work, the controller signs and submits complete-host-run and only then posts terminal result and refreshes. Failure in signing, backend completion, reply or refresh follows already observed model/tool work. The terminal run result omits the original requestId, while initial running result includes it.
note: 05 Findings/D1625 Host completion publication can fail after model execution.md

title: External host run cancellation is classified differently from progress cancellation
body: Progress UI cancellation sets hostCancelled=true and cancels token; pause/cancel/stop routes first call backend then cancel activeHostRuns token without setting that local boolean. A resulting thrown model error can be labelled failed by this helper rather than cancelled. Backend run-state reconciliation may impose the final state separately.
note: 05 Findings/D1626 External host run cancellation is classified differently from progress cancellation.md

title: Chat participant model execution is a separate authority and budget route
body: Status/skills/context commands do not invoke a model. Ordinary prompt uses request.model supplied by VS Code, checks input against maxInputTokens, streams text and records provider activity as effect observe. It does not call the Studio model selector/tool policy/output budget or a local timeout, and does not consult the imported provider policy report here.
note: 05 Findings/D1627 Chat participant model execution is a separate authority and budget route.md

title: Host asset identity omits modular styles and the shipped host bundle
body: extensionAssetIdentity includes dashboard JS, src JS excluding extension.bundle.js, legacy dashboard CSS, sidebar assets and action inventory. The loaded modular media/styles files and generated bundle bytes are absent from asset digest. This host/source identity is selected-source parity, not complete installed-package byte identity.
note: 05 Findings/D1628 Host asset identity omits modular styles and the shipped host bundle.md

title: Package hash is emitted but excluded from host/source match
body: identityMatches compares version, asset hash, asset protocol and message schema, not package_sha256. Version comes from require(packagePath), potentially cached, while hash reads current disk. Equal selected assets/protocols can still yield a match across other package metadata changes.
note: 05 Findings/D1629 Package hash is emitted but excluded from host/source match.md

title: Workspace selection and canonical memory root are distinct
body: workspaceRoot uses first open folder or engine fallback; settings.workspaceRoot resolves separately for canonical memory. Dashboard state keys lowercase paths on every platform and keep eight entries. Case-distinct POSIX workspaces can share a state key. The activation coordination watcher is bound once to its initial root.
note: 05 Findings/D1630 Workspace selection and canonical memory root are distinct.md

title: Host context cache does not carry a workspace key
body: Five-minute hostContextCache and governor key host-context are shared inside activation. Current environment is also reused through currentEnvironment || readEnvironmentInventory(root). Configuration/extension events clear context, but there is no workspace-folder-change handler in this file. A changed first workspace can reuse context/environment until another invalidation.
note: 05 Findings/D1631 Host context cache does not carry a workspace key.md

title: Portable context snapshot retains absolute locators
body: The named portable snapshot includes repository fsPath and environment current path. Its memory_refs branch dereferences workspace.uri when coordination paths exist, although workspace may be absent under engine fallback. Guarantee flags describe content choices but do not establish locator portability.
note: 05 Findings/D1632 Portable context snapshot retains absolute locators.md

title: Opening cached context does not force a fresh read
body: openContextSnapshot uses currentContextEnvelope when present. continueWithCodex sets the objective-bearing envelope, opens it, then publishSnapshot(false) can replace global context with cached host-context envelope. The displayed document and later global context can differ; cancellation clears only local context, not an external Codex session.
note: 05 Findings/D1633 Opening cached context does not force a fresh read.md

title: Snapshot composition catches only the canonical bridge snapshot call
body: Memory lease ensure runs before try; host-context, enterprise initialization, environment read, identity hashing and sidebar publication can throw afterward. currentSnapshot is assigned before composition completes. The promise finally resets joining state but does not roll back partial shared fields or guarantee an error snapshot to all callers.
note: 05 Findings/D1634 Snapshot composition catches only the canonical bridge snapshot call.md

title: Forced snapshot refresh joins or follows the current publication
body: A forced caller waits for an in-flight nonforced promise then requests a forced pass; ordinary callers share one promise. Each awaiting caller posts to its own target afterward. Rejection of the first promise prevents that forced retry path. There is no workspace generation binding around assigning shared currentSnapshot.
note: 05 Findings/D1635 Forced snapshot refresh joins or follows the current publication.md

title: Validation cache is keyed to snapshot identity at publication time
body: Validation runs against current configured engine root, then stores result under validationCacheKey(currentSnapshot) after completion.
