title: Query and pagination restoration resets defaults rather than the predecessor
body: Catalog restoration writes blank query/status, label sort and limit50 without capturing original filters. Returned offsets do not verify complete item order, overlap or total identity coverage. Hydration accepts string ID/hash without comparing exact selected ID and recomputed body bytes. Error paths may leave state changed.
note: 05 Findings/D1797 Query and pagination restoration resets defaults rather than the predecessor.md

title: Conditional input scenarios may exercise invented operating conditions
body: Local select probes inject an alternate option if none exists; invalid value rejection is native select behavior. Memory pagination sets memoryOffset=-59 to align a fixed60-step UI with a one-item query. Other cases seed project rows, zero-hash learning history and literal failure/recovery flags. They are renderer fixtures, not authoritative production scenarios.
note: 05 Findings/D1798 Conditional input scenarios may exercise invented operating conditions.md

title: Temporary observation fixtures lack complete failure restoration
body: Several branches clear preexisting working drafts, assign snapshot/catalog/pending state and restore only marker absence or one field on success. Exceptions can bypass restore; select finally may reset DOM value without dispatching model restoration. Later errors can leave completed flags true.
note: 05 Findings/D1799 Temporary observation fixtures lack complete failure restoration.md

title: Graph identity ignores labels weights and rendered attributes
body: graphProjectionIdentity hashes sorted node keys and edge source/relation/target triples. Labels, node/edge weights, other attributes and layout are excluded, while empty graphs/duplicate IDs and inconsistent total counts are not fully rejected. Pure probe changed labels and weights without changing identity. This matters directly to the requested weighted navigable map.
note: 05 Findings/D1800 Graph identity ignores labels weights and rendered attributes.md

title: Saved-view restart proof does not bind all saved presentation state
body: Graph profile resets baseline rather than preserving prior filters/layout. Restart compares a reduced graph identity and saved-view name, not every normalized preset field. Delete restoration checks current memory/DOM absence without another storage reconstruction; failure can leave the view and baseline altered.
note: 05 Findings/D1801 Saved-view restart proof does not bind all saved presentation state.md

title: Request-bound system snapshot helper has no request identifier binding
body: requestBoundSystemSnapshotIdentity verifies refresh/snapshot types and a projection tuple, but does not compare request IDs. Empty map, extension and campaign identity fields can pass the tuple. Pure probe accepted an unrelated snapshot request; test explicitly uses no request ID.
note: 05 Findings/D1802 Request-bound system snapshot helper has no request identifier binding.md

title: Snapshot selection can return older matching state after a newer contradiction
body: selectLatestMatchingInstalledSnapshot retains the latest predicate match separately from latest observed snapshot. If a newer snapshot fails the predicate, it still returns the earlier match and callers may accept it. Pure probe shows revision1 success selected after revision2 failure. Existing test covers only stale-then-good ordering.
note: 05 Findings/D1803 Snapshot selection can return older matching state after a newer contradiction.md

title: Project reconstruction equality is selected metadata rather than graph content
body: Project identity compares path, revision, inventory digest and counts, not graph bytes or validation/errors. Build result acceptance is broadly truthy. Initialization cancellation from one entry is shared across two attempted controls; a common build result contributes across multiple entrypoints.
note: 05 Findings/D1804 Project reconstruction equality is selected metadata rather than graph content.md

title: Sidebar bounded journals use length offsets that stop advancing at capacity
body: Full snapshots are capped at20 and outbound requests at80, but subsequent scenario waits use previous array length and slice offsets or require length growth. At capacity new entries cannot increase length, so new evidence is missed or recovery times out. Synthetic snapshots also enter the same host journal.
note: 05 Findings/D1805 Sidebar bounded journals use length offsets that stop advancing at capacity.md

title: Sidebar restoration and reconstruction cover selected state only
body: Preference identity binds wave/expanded plus integer revision without freshness. Stable reconstruction intentionally excludes volatile task progress, and conditional completion can be true despite failed conditional flags. Error finally restores outage/sidebar visibility but not all wave/task preferences or original projection.
note: 05 Findings/D1806 Sidebar restoration and reconstruction cover selected state only.md

title: Cleanup receipt accepts claimed reclamation with an empty resource list
body: validCleanupResult requires reclaimed count but uses resources.every, which passes for an empty array. It does not bind each resource to the exact selected fixture/source digest or rehash quarantine destination. The report pure probe accepted one reclaimed resource with resources=[]. Inventory absence after restart is not restored destination custody.
note: 05 Findings/D1807 Cleanup receipt accepts claimed reclamation with an empty resource list.md

title: Cleanup preexistence rejection can still recursively remove existing fixture parents
body: runInstalledCleanupProfile rejects preexisting fixed fixture paths but its finally recursively removes both fixture parents whenever present. It has no created-this-run guard, so rejection itself can lead to deletion of preexisting contents. This was source-reviewed only; no cleanup was executed.
note: 05 Findings/D1808 Cleanup preexistence rejection can still recursively remove existing fixture parents.md

title: Environment fixture preexistence rejection still reaches recursive cleanup
body: The environment lifecycle finally removes its target even when an initial exists check rejected that target. The temporary_registered flag is literal, not a checked ownership receipt. Restored marker/path and inventory observations do not themselves prove equal snapshots, exact tree restoration or failed quarantine reconciliation.
note: 05 Findings/D1809 Environment fixture preexistence rejection still reaches recursive cleanup.md

title: Enterprise team fixture cleanup lacks exact creation custody
body: Fixed team fixture preexistence is rejected, but finally removes an existing in-root fixture regardless of creation ownership. A staged path supplied by a result is accepted if within workspace/existing, not bound to an exact owned candidate. Target configuration uses hardcoded values without full baseline restoration; nonnull toggle result is weaker than exact state equality.
note: 05 Findings/D1810 Enterprise team fixture cleanup lacks exact creation custody.md

title: Plugin pending receipt plus visible version is not terminal durable custody
body: Mutation can accept a pending-host-reload receipt and mark physically reconciled after workbench restart/version observation. No new terminal journal/tree receipt is required by that path. Current-version polling may reuse a cached result, and most execution waiters omit request ID despite stronger preview binding.
note: 05 Findings/D1811 Plugin pending receipt plus visible version is not terminal durable custody.md

title: Plugin failure cleanup can uninstall a preexisting fixture
body: The initial absent check happens after manager entry actions. If it fails because fixture v1/v2 already exists, catch may uninstall that version as failure cleanup without a created-by-this-run marker. Final absent inventory also leaves retained rollback custody, so it is not complete initial state restoration.
note: 05 Findings/D1812 Plugin failure cleanup can uninstall a preexisting fixture.md

title: Plugin source and manager denominators have incomplete custody
body: Fixture VSIX bytes are checked against receipt SHA/size, a useful boundary, but receipt schema/provenance and path ancestor containment are not fully admitted before reads. Four manager entry IDs receive shared evidence after at least two positional actions. Physical version scan ignores malformed manifests/duplicates and does not bind complete installed tree bytes.
note: 05 Findings/D1813 Plugin source and manager denominators have incomplete custody.md

title: Exact preview confirmation is a strong local boundary with separate downstream obligations
body: Plugin confirmation binds preview request ID, token, exact target, enabled visible modal and rechecks control identity at click. Tests exercise stale/substituted and transient replacement cases with fake DOM. This proves the local selection contract; native focus, execution request, installed bytes and durable custody remain separate and must not inherit that proof automatically.
note: 05 Findings/D1814 Exact preview confirmation is a strong local boundary with separate downstream obligations.md

title: Validation profile ordering is not bound to the registered campaign oracle
body: Actual validation requires two independent environment flags, but no local processing-order check precedes it. Main invokes it before later graph, cleanup, plugin, outage and late adversarial work. One shared validation result credits both UI entrypoints; source regex counting one click does not prove global single-owner campaign sequence. Backend enforcement must be checked separately.
note: 05 Findings/D1815 Validation profile ordering is not bound to the registered campaign oracle.md

title: Expected-fault filtering assumes historical marketplace and cancellation state
body: Console classification suppresses a hardcoded PX marketplace404 as unpublished although user says extension is published/verified. Other text-based network/config classifications are broad. Native recovery requires three project cancellation keys while the current profile includes initialization keys too, creating a stale denominator. These are classifier assumptions, not independently attributed causes.
note: 05 Findings/D1816 Expected-fault filtering assumes historical marketplace and cancellation state.md

title: Late-card closure uses fixed historical artifacts rather than current findings
body: all_report_findings_reconciled reads specific August closure/findings files without binding the current atlas denominator/hash. Empty repair disposition can pass a negative regex; implemented_pending_remote_os_execution is accepted. post_repair_incompleteness_audit derives from prior booleans and host errors rather than a new independent audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1817 Late-card closure uses fixed historical artifacts rather than current findings.md

title: Worker envelope validation is weaker than physical worker evidence
body: Crash/late worker wrappers accept status/schema/hash-shaped summaries without rehashing canonical outputs or requiring complete nonempty recovery actions. Missing engine root resolves to cwd, defeating empty-root check. Late worker errors can be normalized away. Independently reviewed worker internals provide evidence only for their exact scope.
note: 05 Findings/D1818 Worker envelope validation is weaker than physical worker evidence.md

title: Bridge conflict helper counts fixture invocations rather than mutation retries
body: Two child commands emit an error envelope with exits2 and1. no_mutation_retry is inferred from attempts==2 across those fixture calls, not from exercising a mutating operation retry path. request_bound_reason checks text rather than exact original request custody. Keep its claim limited to exit classification.
note: 05 Findings/D1819 Bridge conflict helper counts fixture invocations rather than mutation retries.md

title: Late controller adversarial fixture restores only selected globals
body: Synthetic proofs/hashes and MessageEvents exercise stale/cross-kind/detached save handling. Saved globals are partly references, and final closeModal after restoration can consume restored state. Catalog/request arrays, detached maps and all proof/presentation state are not fully restored. Object.values(checks).every lacks a separately enforced expected check denominator at this producer.
note: 05 Findings/D1820 Late controller adversarial fixture restores only selected globals.md

title: Test names exceed the behavioral scope of many installed assertions
body: The4277-line suite includes useful pure predicate, callback DOM, exact plugin substitution and spawned worker cases. Many claims about ordering, restoration, authority, source gating and exact denominators merely search source text. Reducer tests apply one probe only; timeout tests never resolve old work after reset; no product tests were run by this report audit.
note: 05 Findings/D1821 Test names exceed the behavioral scope of many installed assertions.md

title: Bundle identity lacks a retained complete producer-input receipt
body: build-mcp uses no sourcemap/metafile, strips legal comments and writes one bundle. Existing check mode would compare fresh build bytes, but has not run during this audit because campaign order forbids speculative build reconciliation. Report partition and normalized AST prove narrower correspondence only.
note: 05 Findings/D1822 Bundle identity lacks a retained complete producer-input receipt.md

title: Generated source correspondence does not preserve module-relative worker locations
body: Bundled exported inventoryTeamPackAsync and scanEnvironmentAsync still use __dirname plus worker filenames. In server/index.js that resolves under server; both physical worker files are under src. Current registered routes call synchronous inventory and stored reads, so no current tool failure is asserted. The dormant helper contract must be resolved before route reuse.
note: 05 Findings/D1823 Generated source correspondence does not preserve module-relative worker locations.md

title: SDK cancellation signal is discarded before PX handler execution
body: executeToolHandler invokes executor(args,ctx), but mcpActivityIntegration returns async(input) and calls handler(effectiveInput). ctx.mcpReq.signal and exact transport request identity never reach PX handlers. Synchronous spawnSync can also block receipt of cancellation; SDK aborted replies do not roll back already executed effects.
note: 05 Findings/D1824 SDK cancellation signal is discarded before PX handler execution.md

title: Cancellation with valid numeric request ID zero is ignored
body: The wire RequestIdSchema accepts integer IDs, but Protocol._oncancel returns on falsy requestId. The extracted-method pure report probe shows ID0 yields no abort while1 and a string abort their fake controllers. This is a bundled dependency behavior, not a whole SDK operational test.
note: 05 Findings/D1825 Cancellation with valid numeric request ID zero is ignored.md

title: Inbound request concurrency is not bounded by the raw stdio buffer
body: ReadBuffer limits raw accumulated bytes to10MiB. Decoded messages enter an unbounded queue, and _onrequest schedules handler promises without a configured global in-flight bound. Async callbacks can overlap and parsed request memory can outlive the byte buffer. Synchronous PX handlers add event-loop blocking instead of cooperative admission.
note: 05 Findings/D1826 Inbound request concurrency is not bounded by the raw stdio buffer.md

title: Duplicate request IDs replace cancellation controller ownership
body: _onrequest stores a new controller at request.id without rejecting an existing active entry. A duplicate ID displaces cancellation ownership for the prior handler; finally protects against deleting the replacement but does not prevent the duplicate effects. No duplicate-ID operational proof was run.
note: 05 Findings/D1827 Duplicate request IDs replace cancellation controller ownership.md

title: Stdout backpressure and close have no aggregate deadline
body: StdioServerTransport.send waits for drain/error after a false write result without a timeout. closeAll awaits subscription writes, product.close and wire.close without an aggregate bound. Application shutdown ownership cannot be inferred from a bounded inbound frame size or3-second probe-answer wait.
note: 05 Findings/D1828 Stdout backpressure and close have no aggregate deadline.md

title: PX does not retain the serving handle or integrate application shutdown
body: The final serveStdio call discards its close handle and supplies only onerror. Stdio transport attaches data/error callbacks, not stdin end/close callbacks in this implementation. No source-level application hook reconciles PX effects on EOF/signal here; generic SDK closure only aborts cooperative handlers.
note: 05 Findings/D1829 PX does not retain the serving handle or integrate application shutdown.md

title: Domain result validity is not supplied by MCP input schemas
body: The SDK validates output only when outputSchema exists. PX registers strict input schemas but no output schemas, and wraps arbitrary values into structuredContent. A normal unavailable/failure object can be logged as completed/success by instrumentation because it did not throw. Wire result shape and domain success are different contracts.
note: 05 Findings/D1830 Domain result validity is not supplied by MCP input schemas.md

title: Malformed JSON lines can be discarded without a parse-error receipt
body: ReadBuffer catches SyntaxError from JSON.parse and continues to the next line. Schema-invalid messages reach transport.onerror, but syntax-invalid lines disappear at this boundary. Diagnosis and client retry must not assume every rejected request generates a typed error response.
note: 05 Findings/D1831 Malformed JSON lines can be discarded without a parse-error receipt.md

title: Protocol fallback can instantiate PX authority and instrumentation twice
body: A modern discover probe creates a server, and a later legacy opener discards it and constructs another. Factory buildServer recreates authority/instrumentation state. The SDK waits for answered probe requests but does not prove application-owned resource disposal beyond product.close. This matters to future factory side effects and registration ownership.
note: 05 Findings/D1832 Protocol fallback can instantiate PX authority and instrumentation twice.md

title: Embedded dependency origins are not fully described by direct dependency names
body: Bundle has80 Zod regions, MCP core types, protocol/stdio implementation and an SDK AJV chunk containing validator engines and format support. Lock lists SDK/core/Zod versions but AJV is embedded upstream. Origin accounting and retained dependency notices need to describe these shipped contents rather than treating all4383 functions as PX-authored.
note: 05 Findings/D1833 Embedded dependency origins are not fully described by direct dependency names.md

title: Packaged dependency notice custody is missing from the reviewed inputs
body: MCP build strips legal comments. Custom VSIX packaging copies root LICENSE/NOTICE and selected directories, while root NOTICE describes branding only; SDK/core/Zod license files remain in node_modules, which is excluded. This is a source-observed release-documentation gap for review, not a legal opinion or a claim about a remotely published artifact.
note: 05 Findings/D1834 Packaged dependency notice custody is missing from the reviewed inputs.md
